questions.explanation: Menaka Guruswamy made history by becoming India’s first openly queer Member of Parliament after taking oath in the Rajya Sabha in April 2026. A distinguished senior advocate of the Supreme Court of India, she played a key role in the landmark 2018 case that led to the decriminalisation of homosexuality by reading down Section 377 of the IPC. Representing West Bengal as a member of the All India Trinamool Congress, her achievement marks a significant step toward inclusivity and representation of LGBTQ+ individuals in India’s political landscape.

questions.question: Which Indian Navy ship arrived at Male, Maldives, on April 06, 2026, under the IOS SAGAR initiative?
questions.explanation: INS Sunayna is a Saryu-class offshore patrol vessel of the Indian Navy that arrived at Male as part of its operational deployment under the SAGAR initiative. Commissioned in October 2013 and built by Goa Shipyard Limited, the vessel plays a vital role in maritime security and surveillance. Its deployment reflects India’s commitment to regional cooperation, particularly under the Neighbourhood First policy and MAHASAGAR vision, aimed at ensuring security and growth across the Indian Ocean region through collaborative maritime efforts.

questions.question: Who assumed the role of Managing Director (MD) and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Yes Bank on April 6, 2026?
questions.explanation: Vinay Muralidhar Tonse took charge as the Managing Director and CEO of Yes Bank on April 6, 2026, succeeding Prashant Kumar, who completed his tenure. With over 35 years of experience in the banking and financial services sector, he has held several key leadership positions at State Bank of India, including Managing Director (Retail Business & Operations) and MD & CEO of SBI Mutual Funds. His appointment ensures experienced leadership and continuity in the functioning and strategic direction of the bank.

questions.question: In which state is the Kalai-II Hydro Electric Project being constructed on the Lohit River?
questions.explanation: Arunachal Pradesh is the location of the Kalai-II Hydro Electric Project, which has been approved with a significant investment of ₹14,105.83 crore. The project is situated in the Anjaw district on the Lohit River, a major tributary of the Brahmaputra. With a total installed capacity of 1200 MW, it is expected to generate substantial annual energy, contributing to the regional power supply. Implemented through a joint venture between THDC India Limited and the state government, the project also includes infrastructure development like roads and bridges, while providing economic benefits such as free power allocation to the state.

questions.question: Which bank launched the AI-powered conversational platform ‘bob SAMVAD’ for multilingual communication in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Bank of Baroda introduced the ‘bob SAMVAD’ platform as an AI-driven solution to enhance customer interaction at its branches. The platform enables real-time communication in 22 languages using advanced features like voice-to-text and text-to-speech conversion. Initially deployed across 250 branches in multiple states, it aims to improve accessibility for customers with diverse linguistic backgrounds. Developed in-house, the system ensures low-latency responses for smooth communication. This initiative reflects the bank’s focus on digital innovation and customer-centric services, strengthening its position as a leading public sector bank in India.

questions.question: What is the name of the new AI model introduced by Meta to power its AI assistant?
questions.explanation: Muse Spark is the latest artificial intelligence model launched by Meta as part of its new Superintelligence Labs initiative. It is designed to power the Meta AI assistant and assist users with a variety of everyday tasks, such as estimating calories from food images, visualising objects in different settings, and answering questions across multiple subjects. Despite being a compact and fast model, it demonstrates the ability to handle complex queries. While it has received mixed feedback from experts regarding performance benchmarks, Meta continues to improve its capabilities and plans to expand its usage across platforms like WhatsApp, Instagram, and Facebook.

questions.question: Which state launched the ‘Majha Gaon, Arogyasampann Gaon’ rural healthcare initiative in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra launched the ‘Majha Gaon, Arogyasampann Gaon’ initiative with a budget of ₹65.25 crore to improve rural healthcare delivery. The programme emphasises preventive healthcare, focusing on sanitation, clean drinking water, nutrition, and disease control, including mental health and lifestyle-related illnesses. It adopts a decentralised administrative structure with committees at state, district, and village levels to ensure effective implementation. Villages meeting specific health benchmarks are recognised as ‘Arogyasampann Gaon’. The initiative aligns with the broader objective of enhancing public health infrastructure and awareness, especially in rural areas, marking its launch on World Health Day.

questions.question: Which country launched the world’s first commercial Upper 6GHz (U6GHz) network in April 2026?
questions.explanation: The UAE became the first country to launch a commercial Upper 6GHz (U6GHz) network, marking a major milestone in telecommunications innovation. Operated under the Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority (TDRA), the network uses the 6425–7125 MHz spectrum, often referred to as the “Golden Spectrum” due to its optimal balance of coverage and capacity. It delivers ultra-fast 5G-Advanced speeds, including up to 10Gbps downlink and 1Gbps uplink, enabling advanced digital services and AI-driven applications. Developed with global partners like Huawei and Nokia, the rollout highlights the UAE’s leadership in next-generation connectivity.

questions.question: In which city is the second edition of the International SMOPS-2026 conference being held in April 2026?
questions.explanation: The International Conference on Spacecraft Mission Operations (SMOPS-2026) is being conducted in Bangalore from April 8 to 10, 2026. The conference focuses on innovative approaches to spacecraft mission management, including the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning for autonomous operations. It is jointly organised by ISRO, the Astronautical Society of India, and the International Academy of Astronautics. The event brings together experts from leading global space agencies such as NASA, ESA, and JAXA to discuss advancements in mission design, cybersecurity, and space domain awareness, reinforcing Bangalore’s status as a major hub for space research and technology in India.

questions.question: Which Indian Navy sail training ship participated in the ‘Escale à Sete’ maritime festival in France in April 2026?
questions.explanation: INS Sudarshini, a sail training ship of the Indian Navy, took part in the biennial ‘Escale à Sète’ maritime festival held in France. The event marked the 400th anniversary of the French Navy and is considered one of the largest maritime gatherings in the Mediterranean region. During the festival, the ship and its crew participated in various activities, including competitions and cultural exchanges. The Sudarshini rowing team even secured a bronze medal. The ship is also on the Lokayan 26 mission, which aims to strengthen international maritime cooperation and relations.

questions.question: Which organisation released the report titled “From Borrowers to Builders: Women and India’s Evolving Credit Market” in April 2026?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog released the second edition of the report focusing on women’s participation in India’s evolving credit market. The report highlights significant growth in credit access among women, with total outstanding credit rising to ₹76 lakh crore by 2025. It also emphasizes increased credit penetration, higher participation in commercial lending, and strong regional growth trends in states like Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. Developed in collaboration with organisations such as TransUnion, CIBIL and MicroSave Consulting, the report reflects expanding financial inclusion and the growing role of women in India's formal credit ecosystem.

questions.question: In which country is the joint military exercise Cyclone-IV being conducted in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Egypt is hosting the 4th edition of the joint military exercise Cyclone-IV, where the Indian Army Special Forces are participating alongside Egyptian Special Forces. The exercise is being conducted at Anshas from 09 to 17 April 2026 and focuses on enhancing operational coordination in desert and semi-desert environments. It aims to improve interoperability, joint mission planning, and tactical capabilities between the two nations. This bilateral exercise strengthens defence cooperation and strategic ties. Earlier editions were held alternately, with the previous one conducted in India, highlighting the growing military collaboration between both countries.

questions.question: Which city topped the national pollution index in India for March 2026 as per CREA rankings?
questions.explanation: Gurugram secured the top position as the most polluted city in India for March 2026, according to the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA). It recorded a high monthly average PM2.5 level of 116 µg/m³, indicating hazardous air quality conditions. Haryana had a significant presence in the rankings, contributing several cities among the most polluted. The findings emphasise the ongoing challenges of air pollution in urban and industrial regions. Efforts under the National Clean Air Programme aim to reduce particulate matter levels, but the data highlight the need for stronger implementation and monitoring measures.

questions.question: Which country was elected by acclamation to several subsidiary bodies of the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC)?
questions.explanation: India was elected by acclamation to multiple subsidiary bodies of the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC), reflecting its growing global influence and active participation in international governance. These bodies include the Commission on Science and Technology for Development and the Committee on Non-Governmental Organisations. Additionally, India secured a position in the Committee for Programme and Coordination for the term 2027–2029. This election highlights India’s commitment to global development, multilateral cooperation, and its role in shaping policies related to science, technology, and social and economic progress worldwide.

questions.question: Which company launched the Unit Linked Insurance Plan (ULIP) named Promise4Wealth to offer life insurance and wealth creation solutions?
questions.explanation: Canara HSBC Life Insurance introduced the ULIP product Promise4Wealth to combine life insurance coverage with investment opportunities. The plan offers multiple fund options, including equity, debt, and balanced funds, allowing policyholders to tailor their investments based on risk appetite. It also includes features like a safety switch option to secure gains, loyalty additions to boost returns, and return of mortality charges at maturity. Additionally, flexible withdrawal options such as systematic withdrawal plans and milestone withdrawals help meet financial goals, making it a comprehensive financial planning solution.

questions.question: Where was the 25th Foundation Day of the National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC) celebrated on April 10, 2026?
questions.explanation: The National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC) celebrated its 25th Foundation Day on April 10, 2026, marking its Silver Jubilee year. The event took place at Vishwa Yuva Kendra in New Delhi, which also serves as the headquarters of the organisation. NSTFDC operates under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs and plays a crucial role in providing concessional financial assistance to Scheduled Tribes for income-generating activities. The celebration highlighted the organization’s contributions toward socio-economic development and empowerment of tribal communities across India over the past 25 years.

questions.question: Which bank partnered with the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) to provide credit support to sellers under the GeM Sahay initiative?
questions.explanation: Punjab National Bank (PNB) partnered with the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) to enhance credit access for platform sellers through the GeM Sahay initiative. Under this collaboration, PNB provides unsecured short-term loans against confirmed purchase orders generated on the GeM portal. This financing mechanism helps address working capital needs and improves liquidity for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), startups, and other emerging businesses. The initiative also integrates financial services into the digital procurement ecosystem, ensuring the timely execution of government orders and strengthening the overall efficiency of public procurement in India.

questions.question: Which Indian Union Territory includes the Doda region, where a Doppler weather radar and seismological observatory are being established?
questions.explanation: The Doda region is part of Jammu & Kashmir, a Union Territory in northern India characterized by mountainous terrain and high seismic vulnerability, falling under Seismic Zones 4 and 5. Due to its eco-fragile nature, the government is strengthening disaster preparedness by installing a Doppler weather radar for real-time weather monitoring and a seismological observatory for earthquake tracking. These initiatives enhance early warning systems, improve forecasting in remote areas, and contribute to minimising risks associated with natural disasters in the region.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Chairperson of the Nasscom Foundation in April 2026?
questions.explanation: UB Pravin Rao was appointed as the Chairperson of the Nasscom Foundation in April 2026, succeeding Rostow Ravanan. He brings over 35 years of extensive experience in global operations and large-scale transformation. Rao previously served as the Chief Operating Officer (COO) at Infosys from 2014 to 2021. His long association with Nasscom includes roles such as Vice-Chairperson and Chairman. Under his leadership, the foundation is expected to align with the government’s vision of Viksit Bharat, focusing on leveraging technology and ICT initiatives for social development and inclusive growth across India.

questions.question: Which country signed a currency swap agreement with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) valued at AED 20 billion in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Bahrain entered into a currency swap agreement with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) on April 9, 2026, with a total value of AED 20 billion (equivalent to BHD 2 billion). This agreement, set for a five-year period, aims to strengthen financial cooperation between the two nations. It involves the exchange of UAE Dirham and Bahraini Dinar to provide liquidity in local currencies. The initiative supports smoother cross-border trade, encourages the use of national currencies in transactions, and enhances regional monetary stability within the Gulf Cooperation Council framework.

questions.question: Which fintech startup entered the unicorn club in April 2026 after securing $280 million in pre-IPO funding?
questions.explanation: KreditBee achieved unicorn status in April 2026 after raising $280 million in a pre-IPO funding round, reaching a valuation of $1.5 billion. The company has shown strong financial performance, reporting ₹2,700 crore in revenue and ₹473 crore in net profit for FY25. Its Assets Under Management (AUM) grew significantly to ₹15,000 crore in FY26. The funding will support expansion in secured and MSME lending segments. Additionally, the company is preparing for an IPO, including merging its tech and NBFC entities, marking a significant milestone in its growth journey.

questions.question: In which city was India’s first Regional Passport Office to launch Braille script and sign language services for differently-abled applicants?
questions.explanation: Bhopal became the first city in India where the Regional Passport Office introduced Braille script and sign language services to enhance accessibility for differently-abled applicants. The initiative includes Braille booklets, signage for visually impaired individuals, and sign language video resources for hearing and speech-impaired users. QR codes have also been integrated for easy digital access to instructions. Additionally, a dedicated grievance redressal system ensures the timely resolution of issues. This step marks a significant advancement in inclusive governance and citizen-centric service delivery within the passport system.

questions.question: On which date is World Homoeopathy Day observed in India to commemorate the birth anniversary of Dr Samuel Hahnemann?
questions.explanation: World Homoeopathy Day is observed annually on April 10 in India to honour the birth anniversary of Dr Samuel Hahnemann, the founder of homoeopathy. The day highlights the importance and contributions of homoeopathy in healthcare. Various events, seminars, and awareness programs are conducted to promote its role in sustainable health. Homoeopathy has a long history in India, dating back to the early 19th century, and is supported by government initiatives such as the National AYUSH Mission to integrate it into mainstream healthcare systems.

questions.question: Which institution won the 6th edition of the international debate competition Hermes’ Dialogue 6.0 held in April 2026?
questions.explanation: The 6th edition of Hermes’ Dialogue 6.0, an international debate competition organised by BIMTECH on April 9, 2026, saw participation from teams representing multiple countries. The competition revolved around the theme of prioritizing energy independence amid geopolitical uncertainty. Team LeBroom from IIM Rohtak secured the first position, outperforming other notable teams such as Team Magnus from FORE School of Management and Team Strategy from SRCC. This achievement highlights IIM Rohtak’s strong presence in academic and debate forums at both national and international levels.

questions.question: What was the approximate weight of the simulated Crew Module used in the Second Integrated Air Drop Test (IADT-02) for the Gaganyaan mission?
questions.explanation: The Second Integrated Air Drop Test (IADT-02) conducted by ISRO on April 10, 2026, involved a simulated Crew Module designed for the Gaganyaan mission. The module weighed approximately 5.7 tonnes, which closely matches the mass of the G1 uncrewed mission module. This test was crucial for validating the parachute-based deceleration system, ensuring safe landing during future missions. The module was lifted to an altitude of 3 km using an Indian Air Force Chinook helicopter before being dropped. The successful test confirmed the readiness of critical systems required for India’s first human spaceflight mission.

questions.question: What is the revised economic growth forecast for India for the fiscal year 2026-27 as projected by the World Bank?
questions.explanation: The World Bank revised India’s economic growth forecast for the fiscal year 2026-27 to 6.6%, up from its earlier estimate of 6.3%. This upward revision reflects strong and resilient domestic demand, which continues to support economic expansion despite global uncertainties. India is also expected to grow at a higher rate of 7.6% in 2025-26, reinforcing its position as the primary driver of growth in the South Asian region. While the broader regional outlook shows a slight slowdown, India’s stable performance highlights its economic strength and importance in maintaining regional growth momentum.

questions.question: In which country were over 200 ancient archaeological sites spanning 6,000 years discovered in the Eretrian plain of Evia in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Greece witnessed a significant archaeological breakthrough in April 2026 with the discovery of over 200 ancient sites in the Eretrian plain of Evia. Using advanced technologies like LiDAR and GIS, researchers mapped around 30 square kilometres, uncovering evidence of continuous human habitation spanning 6,000 years. The sites include ancient farms, quarries, and road networks, reflecting socio-economic development across different historical eras such as the Mycenaean, Roman, and Ottoman periods. This discovery provides valuable insights into long-term settlement patterns and highlights the importance of modern technology in archaeological research.

questions.question: In which city was Vantara University, dedicated to wildlife conservation and veterinary sciences, launched in April 2026?
questions.explanation: In April 2026, Anant Ambani announced the establishment of Vantara University, a unique global institution focused on wildlife conservation, animal welfare, and veterinary sciences. The university is located in Jamnagar, Gujarat, which is also home to the Vantara wildlife conservation initiative developed by Reliance Industries. This initiative aims to provide advanced education and research opportunities in conservation science. The project draws inspiration from historic centers of learning like Nalanda University, combining ancient ideals of knowledge with modern scientific approaches to address global environmental and wildlife challenges.

questions.question: India signed the Punatsangchhu-II export tariff protocol with which country in April 2026?
questions.explanation: In April 2026, India entered into an agreement with Bhutan to sign the Punatsangchhu-II export tariff protocol and establish a framework for reactive energy accounting. The Punatsangchhu-II hydroelectric project, with a capacity of 1,020 MW, plays a crucial role in bilateral energy cooperation, with Bhutan exporting surplus electricity to India. This agreement strengthens the long-standing partnership between the two countries in the hydropower sector. Additionally, both nations continue to collaborate on other projects such as Punatsangchhu-I, reflecting their shared commitment to sustainable energy development and regional cooperation.

questions.question: What percentage of the Sundarbans mangrove forest has lost its capacity to recover from environmental stress between 2000 and 2024?
questions.explanation: A recent research study published in April 2026 highlights a concerning decline in the resilience of the Sundarbans mangrove ecosystem. It estimates that around 10-15% of the forest has lost its ability to recover effectively from environmental stress over the period from 2000 to 2024. This decline is attributed to multiple factors, including cyclonic disturbances, rising salinity due to reduced freshwater inflow, and human activities like shrimp farming and deforestation. The weakening resilience threatens biodiversity, including key species, and undermines the ecological stability of this critical mangrove habitat.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Managing Director (MD) and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Vibhor Jain assumed the role of Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) on April 7, 2026. He succeeded Thampy Koshy, who stepped down in April 2025. Before this appointment, Jain served as the Chief Operating Officer and had also taken on responsibilities as acting CEO, demonstrating his leadership within the organisation. ONDC, established as a not-for-profit entity under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, aims to create an open and interoperable digital commerce ecosystem in India, enhancing accessibility and competition across platforms.

questions.question: In which Indian state did the CAG audit find that around 160,000 PVTG individuals were excluded from welfare schemes as of March 2024?
questions.explanation: A Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) audit conducted between July 2024 and January 2025 revealed significant gaps in the implementation of welfare schemes for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) in Odisha. Despite various initiatives like the Odisha PVTG Empowerment and Livelihood Improvement Programme (OPELIP), about 54% of the PVTG population, roughly 160,000 individuals, remained excluded from benefits. The state has the highest number of PVTGs in India, making such exclusions a major concern. Issues like lack of access in newly identified villages and non-operational agencies contributed to the problem, highlighting administrative and implementation challenges.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the UT-ORNL Governor’s Chair for Quantum Devices to lead advanced research initiatives?
questions.explanation: Deep Jariwala, an Indian-origin scientist, was appointed as the UT-ORNL Governor’s Chair for Quantum Devices, a prestigious joint position between the University of Tennessee Knoxville and Oak Ridge National Laboratory. This role involves leading cutting-edge research in quantum materials, microelectronics, and computing systems. His work will also focus on optoelectronic systems and advanced device architectures for next-generation sensing technologies. The appointment reflects ongoing efforts to attract global scientific talent and strengthen collaboration between academic and national research institutions in the field of quantum science and technology.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer of the Indian Digital Payment Intelligence Corporation (IDPIC) in April 2026?
questions.explanation: K. Satyanarayana Raju was appointed as the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Indian Digital Payment Intelligence Corporation (IDPIC) on April 10, 2026. He brings extensive experience in the banking sector, having previously served as the MD & CEO of Canara Bank and held leadership roles in institutions like BoB Financial Solutions. IDPIC, established in 2025 as a not-for-profit entity, plays a crucial role in strengthening India’s digital payment ecosystem by using artificial intelligence to detect and prevent fraud in real time, thereby enhancing financial security and trust.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) effective November 4, 2026?
questions.explanation: Sanjay Khanna assumed the role of Chairman and Managing Director of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) effective November 4, 2026. Prior to this elevation, he served as Director (Refineries) at BPCL, where he managed key refining operations in Mumbai, Kochi, and Bina. With over three decades of experience in the petroleum sector, he has developed strong expertise in refinery management, supply chain operations, and execution of strategic projects. His leadership is expected to strengthen BPCL’s operational efficiency and support its growth as a Maharatna public sector enterprise.

questions.question: Who assumed the charge of Chief Adviser (Cost) in the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Anand Kumar Pal took over as the Chief Adviser (Cost) in the Department of Expenditure under the Ministry of Finance on April 10, 2026. A 1997-batch officer of the Indian Cost Accounts Service, he brings extensive experience in financial analysis, costing methodologies, and international trade policy. Prior to this role, he served as Additional Chief Adviser (Cost) in the Ministry of Defence and held positions in organisations like the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority and the Directorate General of Trade Remedies. His appointment reflects the importance of expert financial oversight in managing public expenditure and policy implementation.

questions.question: Who became the first fast bowler to reach 200 wickets in the history of the Indian Premier League (IPL)?
questions.explanation: Bhuvneshwar Kumar achieved a historic milestone by becoming the first fast bowler to take 200 wickets in the Indian Premier League. He reached this landmark during a match between the Royal Challengers Bengaluru and the Chennai Super Kings by dismissing Ayush Mhatre. Traditionally, spinners have dominated the top wicket-taking charts in the IPL, making this achievement particularly notable for a pace bowler. Bhuvneshwar has been a consistent performer since his debut in 2011 and is also known for winning back-to-back Purple Caps in 2016 and 2017, highlighting his excellence in the tournament.

questions.question: Which Indian state launched NARIT AI, an Artificial Intelligence-based investigation tool for narcotics cases, in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Gujarat became the first state in India to deploy an Artificial Intelligence-based investigation tool named NARIT AI for handling narcotics-related cases. Launched in Gandhinagar on April, 2026, the system uses advanced Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) technology to analyse FIRs and assist law enforcement officials. It operates on a secure, closed database to ensure data privacy and reduce errors. The tool provides legal guidance under the NDPS Act, helps identify procedural gaps, and enhances the efficiency of investigations, ultimately aiming to improve conviction rates in drug-related offences.

questions.question: On which date is National Safe Motherhood Day observed every year in India?
questions.explanation: April 11 is observed annually in India as National Safe Motherhood Day to emphasise the importance of maternal health, safe pregnancy, and quality childbirth care. The date marks the birth anniversary of Kasturba Gandhi, a prominent figure in social reform and women’s welfare. The day aims to raise awareness about maternal healthcare issues and promote better access to medical services, especially in rural and underserved areas. Initiatives such as free health check-ups, awareness campaigns, and workshops are conducted to ensure the well-being of mothers and reduce maternal and infant mortality rates.

questions.question: Which Indian state signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Vietnam’s Vingroup for multi-sector strategic investments in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra entered into a significant agreement with the Vietnamese conglomerate Vingroup in April 2026, marking a major step toward large-scale economic development. The deal involves an investment of approximately $6.5 billion, targeting sectors such as urban infrastructure, electric mobility, renewable energy, healthcare, and education. Key projects include the development of integrated townships across 1,000 hectares and the deployment of 60,000 electric vehicles. The initiative is focused on the Mumbai Metropolitan Region and aims to boost economic growth, sustainability, and infrastructure development through collaboration with agencies like MMRDA.

questions.question: What GDP growth rate did Moody's project for India for FY27 amid rising fuel costs and geopolitical tensions?
questions.explanation: Moody projected India’s GDP growth rate for FY27 at 6%, revising it downward from the earlier estimate of 6.8%. This adjustment reflects concerns over rising geopolitical tensions in West Asia, which have disrupted energy supplies and led to increased fuel prices. As India relies heavily on imports for crude oil and LPG, these disruptions have contributed to inflationary pressures and weakened household consumption. Additionally, the slowdown is linked to reduced industrial activity and investment momentum, along with fiscal challenges faced by the government due to higher subsidy burdens and lower tax revenues.

questions.question: Who was re-elected to a major UN committee during India’s unopposed victories in the ECOSOC elections in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Preeti Saran was re-elected to a major United Nations committee as part of India’s successful and unopposed performance in the ECOSOC elections held in April 2026. Her re-election to the Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights reflects her extensive diplomatic experience and global recognition. She has previously served in key roles such as Secretary (East) in the Ministry of External Affairs and as Ambassador to Vietnam. This achievement underscores India’s growing influence in global governance and highlights international confidence in its leadership and contributions to multilateral institutions.

questions.question: In which Indian state was Operation Him Setu launched by the Indian Army to evacuate stranded tourists in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Sikkim witnessed the launch of Operation Him Setu by the Indian Army on April 9, 2026, in response to a major landslide and heavy snowfall in its northern region. The operation was carried out by the Trishakti Corps under the Eastern Command, focusing on evacuating stranded tourists along the Lachen–Chungthang route. The Border Roads Organisation collaborated closely with army personnel to clear blocked roads, remove snow, and restore connectivity. This coordinated effort highlights the Indian Army’s capability in disaster response and the importance of inter-agency cooperation in challenging mountainous terrains.

questions.question: In which Indian state did the Indian Army launch the community radio station ‘Sikkim Sundari’ in a border village in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Sikkim became the location for the launch of the first community radio station in a border village by the Indian Army’s Trishakti Corps. Named ‘Sikkim Sundari’, the station aims to enhance communication in remote high-altitude areas by broadcasting local news, weather updates, and government schemes. It also serves as a platform to promote local culture and engage youth through skill development initiatives. This collaborative effort between the army, civil administration, and local communities highlights the importance of connectivity and outreach in strategically sensitive border regions.

questions.question: Which city’s government unveiled the draft Electric Vehicle Policy 2.0 (2026–2030) to promote cleaner mobility?
questions.explanation: New Delhi introduced the draft Electric Vehicle Policy 2.0 (2026–2030) to boost the adoption of electric vehicles and reduce pollution levels. The policy includes significant incentives such as tax exemptions, subsidies for electric two-wheelers and commercial vehicles, and scrappage benefits for older vehicles. It also outlines strict measures like banning new petrol-powered two-wheelers from 2028 and mandating electric transitions for certain vehicle categories. These steps are part of a broader effort to tackle air pollution and promote sustainable urban mobility in the capital city of India.

questions.question: INS Trikand delivered INSAS rifles and ammunition to the navy of which country during its port call at Mombasa in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Kenya received INSAS rifles and ammunition from the Indian Navy during the port call of INS Trikand at Mombasa. The handover was conducted by senior naval officials as part of strengthening bilateral defence cooperation. This initiative aligns with India’s MAHASAGAR vision, which focuses on regional security and growth. In addition to the equipment transfer, joint tactical exercises such as Visit, Board, Search and Seizure (VBSS) and training sessions on handling small arms were conducted. These activities highlight India’s commitment to enhancing maritime partnerships and defence collaboration with countries in the Indian Ocean region.

questions.question: In which city is the Central Ayurveda Research Institute (CARI) located, which received ISO 15189:2022 accreditation in April 2026?
questions.explanation: The Central Ayurveda Research Institute (CARI) achieved a significant milestone by becoming the first institute under the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS) to receive ISO 15189:2022 accreditation. This recognition was granted for its Biochemistry and Haematology laboratory standards by NABL. Located in Bengaluru, the institute has demonstrated remarkable progress in healthcare services, conducting over 1.52 lakh laboratory investigations and serving thousands of patients. The accreditation highlights its transition to globally recognised quality standards and reflects advancements in infrastructure, including the adoption of fully automated diagnostic systems under the Ministry of Ayush initiatives.

questions.question: Which tennis player defeated Carlos Alcaraz to win the Monte Carlo Masters title in April 2026?
questions.explanation: The Monte Carlo Masters 2026 witnessed a remarkable performance where Jannik Sinner secured victory against Carlos Alcaraz in straight sets. This win marked Sinner’s first title at the prestigious tournament and helped him reclaim the World No. 1 ranking in ATP standings. It also represented his third ATP 1000 title of the season, placing him among elite players. Sinner achieved a rare milestone by becoming the first since Novak Djokovic in 2015 to win the first three ATP 1000 events of the year. His consistent form and 17-match winning streak highlight his dominance in professional tennis.

questions.question: Which Indian state secured ₹2,000 crore investment interest during a Business Conclave and roadshow held in Bengaluru on December 04, 2026?
questions.explanation: Tripura attracted significant investment interest worth ₹2,000 crore during a Business Conclave and roadshow organised in Bengaluru. The event was conducted by the state’s Industries and Commerce Department to connect with investors, start-ups, and institutional stakeholders from Southern India. This initiative also served as a precursor to the upcoming ‘Destination Tripura: Business Conclave 2026’ in Agartala. Tripura, a northeastern state that gained full statehood in 1972, is notable for being the second-largest producer of natural rubber in India and shares a long international border with Bangladesh.

questions.question: Which country withdrew its candidacy to host the COP33 climate summit in 2028?
questions.explanation: India decided to withdraw its bid to host the COP33 climate summit in 2028 after reviewing its governmental commitments for that year. The proposal to host the event was initially announced during the COP28 summit in Dubai, where India aimed to strengthen its leadership role among Global South nations. The COP hosting rotates among UN regional groups, and the 2028 summit is designated for the Asia-Pacific region. With India stepping back, South Korea remains the only country to have formally expressed interest. India has previously hosted COP8 in New Delhi in 2002, which led to the Delhi Declaration.

questions.question: Which Indian state was officially declared Naxal-free in April 2026 after the surrender of 42 Maoist cadres?
questions.explanation: Telangana achieved a major milestone in internal security by being declared Naxal-free in April 2026. This followed the surrender of 42 cadres belonging to the Communist Party of India (Maoist), including key members such as a PLGA commander. The development marked the complete dismantling of the Telangana State Committee of the Maoists. Over the years 2024 to 2026, a significant number of Maoists surrendered, along with a substantial recovery of firearms and ammunition. This achievement reflects the effectiveness of coordinated efforts by state police and central strategies like the SAMADHAN approach to counter Left Wing Extremism.

questions.question: Which country postponed a legislative bill to return the Chagos Islands to Mauritius in April 2026?
questions.explanation: The United Kingdom delayed the legislative process to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Archipelago to Mauritius due to geopolitical concerns and lack of support from the United States. The proposed agreement included transferring full sovereignty while maintaining a 99-year lease of Diego Garcia for continued military use by the US and UK. The delay also reflects broader strategic considerations in the Indian Ocean region. Historically, the UK has controlled the islands since 1814, and the issue has been subject to international legal scrutiny, including a 2019 advisory opinion by the International Court of Justice urging decolonisation.

questions.question: In which city was a life-size bronze statue of Swami Vivekananda unveiled at Westlake Square in April 2026?
questions.explanation: A life-size bronze statue of Swami Vivekananda was unveiled at Westlake Square in Seattle on April 12, 2026. This marked a historic moment as it became the first instance of a US city government hosting such a monument dedicated to the Indian spiritual leader. The statue was sculpted by Indian artist Naresh Kumar Kumawat and gifted by the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR). The unveiling coincided with ICCR Day, highlighting efforts to strengthen cultural ties between India and the United States, while also honouring Vivekananda’s global influence and teachings.

questions.question: Which country participated with India in the 7th edition of the joint military Exercise DUSTLIK held in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Uzbekistan hosted and participated in the 7th edition of the joint military Exercise DUSTLIK alongside India in April 2026. Conducted at the Gurumsaray Field Training Area, the exercise involved personnel from the Indian Army, Indian Air Force, and Uzbekistan’s armed forces. This annual exercise is held alternately between the two countries and focuses on enhancing operational coordination in semi-mountainous terrain. Activities included land navigation, strike missions, and capturing enemy positions. Such joint drills strengthen military cooperation, improve interoperability, and reinforce strategic defence ties between India and Uzbekistan.

questions.question: What is the name of the medium-term strategic framework launched by the Reserve Bank of India in April 2026 to modernise the country's financial and technological landscape?
questions.explanation: Utkarsh 2029 is the medium-term strategic framework introduced by the Reserve Bank of India to enhance and modernise the financial ecosystem. It outlines a structured plan covering a three-year period from April 2026 to March 2029. The framework includes initiatives such as modernisation of currency management, expansion of digital banking infrastructure, and improved financial inclusion through nationwide systems. It also focuses on technological advancements like Central Bank Digital Currency, Artificial Intelligence regulations, and global expansion of payment systems, building upon earlier strategies to ensure a more robust and efficient financial environment.

questions.question: Which organisation is responsible for grassroots delivery and community-based intervention in the e-SafeHER cybersecurity awareness program?
questions.explanation: The Reliance Foundation partnered with C-DAC Hyderabad to launch the e-SafeHER program on April 13, 2026, under MeitY’s ISEA programme. The initiative aims to train one million rural women (Cyber Sakhis) by 2029, with phased rollout starting in Madhya Pradesh and Odisha through women’s Self-Help Groups using a peer-led model. C-DAC Hyderabad develops localised multilingual training content, while Reliance Foundation handles grassroots delivery. The program enhances last-mile cybersecurity awareness for secure digital transactions and rural livelihoods. C-DAC, established in 1988 and headquartered in Pune, is a premier R&D organisation under MeitY. Reliance Foundation, established in 2010 and based in Mumbai, drives community-based intervention under this initiative.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the new director of Israel’s Mossad intelligence agency in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Roman Gofman is the individual appointed as the new head of Israel’s Mossad intelligence agency. He succeeds the outgoing chief and is set to begin his five-year tenure in June 2026. His appointment is notable because he does not come from a traditional intelligence background, making him the first leader of the agency with such a profile. Having migrated from Belarus at a young age, he built a distinguished military career in the Israel Defence Forces, serving in key command roles and later as military secretary to the Prime Minister before assuming this position.

questions.question: In which city was the 4th leg of the Indian Athletics Series held?
questions.explanation: Ranchi is the city where the 4th leg of the Indian Athletics Series took place, showcasing performances across various track and field events. The competitions included long jump, high jump, javelin throw, sprints, hurdles, and long-distance races, featuring athletes from multiple states and organisations. The event was conducted at an athletics venue known for hosting national-level competitions. Ranchi, the capital of Jharkhand, has been emerging as a significant centre for sports infrastructure in India, contributing to the development and promotion of athletics through such major events.

questions.question: What was the percentage growth in India’s patent filings in the fiscal year 2025-26 compared to the previous year?
questions.explanation: 30.2% represents the growth rate of patent filings in India for the fiscal year 2025-26 compared to the previous year. This significant increase reflects the country’s expanding innovation ecosystem and rising participation from domestic inventors. The total number of applications reached a record high, demonstrating consistent growth over the past decade. A large share of filings came from Indian innovators, indicating stronger research and development activities within the country. The trend also highlights improvements in intellectual property awareness, regulatory support, and the overall strengthening of India’s position in the global innovation landscape.

questions.question: How many total medals did India win at the Asian Wrestling Championships 2026 held in Bishkek?
questions.explanation: 17 is the total number of medals won by India at the Asian Wrestling Championships 2026. The tally includes a combination of gold, silver, and bronze medals across different wrestling categories. The performance reflects India’s strong presence in the sport, with significant contributions from both men’s freestyle and women’s events. Athletes secured top finishes in multiple weight divisions, showcasing consistency and skill. The achievement highlights the country’s growing dominance in wrestling at the continental level and its ability to compete effectively against strong international opponents.

questions.question: In which state was the commemorative stamp release ceremony for ISRO’s human spaceflight programme held in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Karnataka is the state where the commemorative postage stamps honouring ISRO’s human spaceflight programme were released. The event took place in Bengaluru, which is also the headquarters of ISRO and a major hub for India’s space research and technological advancements. The ceremony highlighted India’s achievements in space exploration, including progress from early satellite launches to ambitious missions like Gaganyaan. The state plays a crucial role in India’s scientific development, housing key institutions and contributing significantly to advancements in aerospace, making it central to such national-level initiatives.

questions.question: Who led the Tisza party to victory in the Hungarian parliamentary elections held in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Peter Magyar is the leader who guided the Tisza party to a decisive victory in the Hungarian parliamentary elections. His party secured a majority in the 199-seat parliament with a significant vote share, marking a major political shift in the country. He has prior experience in government roles, including positions in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Hungary’s representation to the European Union. His political journey also includes serving in the European Parliament and holding leadership roles in state institutions, contributing to his rise as a prominent political figure in Hungary.

questions.question: Which state cabinet approved development packages exceeding ₹18,000 crore in April 2026 to boost irrigation, agriculture, and women's safety?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh is the state where the cabinet approved multiple development packages worth over ₹18,000 crore. These initiatives focus on strengthening irrigation infrastructure, promoting agricultural mechanisation, enhancing women’s safety, and improving health and nutrition services. Significant allocations were made for projects like the Midwas Medium Irrigation Project, Sub-mission on Agricultural Mechanisation, and welfare schemes such as Beti Bachao Beti Padhao. The approvals also include funding for public works and new medical colleges, reflecting a comprehensive approach to socio-economic development across rural and urban areas in the state.

questions.question: Which companies signed MoUs with the Ministry of Labour & Employment to enhance digital job matching through the NCS portal in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Porter and Gigin are the companies that entered into agreements with the Ministry of Labour & Employment to improve employment opportunities through the National Career Service portal. These collaborations aim to strengthen digital job matching by connecting jobseekers with verified opportunities in sectors like logistics and gig work. The initiative focuses on generating large-scale employment, increasing employer participation, and enhancing transparency using technology such as Artificial Intelligence. It also supports skill development and integrates with multiple platforms to expand access and improve the efficiency of the employment ecosystem in India.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the first female Chief of Army in Australia in April 2026?
questions.explanation: In April 2026, Australia made a historic decision by appointing Lieutenant General Susan Coyle as its first female Chief of Army in 125 years. She is set to assume office in July 2026, succeeding Lieutenant General Simon Stuart. With nearly four decades of military service, she has extensive experience in cyber-warfare and has held key leadership roles in operations across Afghanistan and the Middle East. Her appointment is part of a broader leadership reshuffle within the Australian Defence Force, reflecting a progressive shift towards greater inclusion and recognition of experienced leadership in defence services.

questions.question: Which country received 13 tonnes of BCG vaccines from India in April 2026 to support child immunisation against Tuberculosis?
questions.explanation: In April 2026, India extended humanitarian support by delivering 13 tonnes of Bacille Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccines to Afghanistan. This assistance was aimed at strengthening the country’s child immunization program, particularly for preventing Tuberculosis (TB), a disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The consignment was handed over to the Ministry of Public Health and was part of broader international cooperation efforts involving organisations like WHO and UNICEF. Such initiatives highlight India’s proactive role in regional health support and its commitment to addressing public health challenges in neighbouring nations.

questions.question: What GDP growth rate did the International Monetary Fund project for India for FY27 in its April 2026 outlook?
questions.explanation: In April 2026, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) revised India’s GDP growth forecast for the financial year 2026–27 to 6.5%, reflecting a slight increase from its earlier estimate of 6.4% made in January. This upward revision was driven by strong economic performance in the previous fiscal year and improved global conditions, including reduced tariffs on Indian exports by the United States. The IMF also projected that India would sustain this growth rate into FY28. Despite global uncertainties and slower trade growth, India’s economy is expected to remain resilient among emerging markets.

questions.question: Which company partnered with Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) to finalise a technical agreement for co-producing F414 jet engines in India in April 2026?
questions.explanation: In April 2026, GE Aerospace entered into a significant technical agreement with Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) for the co-production of F414 jet engines in India. This collaboration aims to strengthen India–U.S. defence manufacturing ties and enhance indigenous production capabilities. The engines are intended to power the Tejas Mark-2 fighter aircraft, an advanced version of India’s Light Combat Aircraft. The agreement builds upon a Memorandum of Understanding signed in June 2022 and reflects over four decades of partnership between the two entities in the aerospace sector, supporting India’s push for self-reliance in defence manufacturing.

questions.question: Which state revised its minimum wage rates effective from April 1, 2026, increasing unskilled workers' monthly pay from ₹11,257 to ₹15,220?
questions.explanation: The state government of Haryana implemented a revised minimum wage structure starting April 1, 2026, significantly increasing the monthly wages of unskilled workers from ₹11,257 to ₹15,220. This move was aimed at improving the standard of living for workers and ensuring fair compensation across different labour categories, including semi-skilled and skilled workers. In addition to wage reforms, the state also introduced social welfare measures such as a 33% reservation for women in ration depot allocations, prioritising disadvantaged groups like widows and members of self-help groups, thereby promoting inclusive development and economic empowerment.

questions.question: Who assumed charge as the Principal Chief Commissioner of Income Tax for Tamil Nadu and Puducherry on April 10, 2026?
questions.explanation: On April 10, 2026, Sunil Bajpai took charge as the Principal Chief Commissioner of Income Tax for Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. He is a senior officer from the 1990 batch of the Indian Revenue Service (IRS) and has held several important roles in tax administration and governance. Before this appointment, he served as Chief Commissioner of Income Tax-5 in Mumbai. His experience includes positions in the National Security Council Secretariat and the Municipal Corporation of Delhi. With strong academic qualifications from IIT Kanpur, IIT Delhi, and IIM Lucknow, he brings significant expertise to the role.

questions.question: Which state announced an interim hike in minimum wages on April 14, 2026, following labour unrest in the Gautam Buddha Nagar district?
questions.explanation: On April 14, 2026, the government of Uttar Pradesh introduced an interim increase in minimum wages for unskilled, semi-skilled, and skilled workers. This decision came in response to labor protests in the Gautam Buddha Nagar district, particularly in industrial hubs like Noida and Ghaziabad. The wage hike was applied retrospectively from April 1, 2026, with varying increases across regions, including 21% in major urban centers. The move aimed to address rising living costs and worker dissatisfaction in the National Capital Region. Additionally, the state announced plans to establish a Wage Board to recommend a permanent wage structure.

questions.question: Who became the Chief Minister of Bihar in April 2026 after the resignation of Nitish Kumar?
questions.explanation: In April 2026, a major political shift occurred in Bihar when Nitish Kumar resigned from the post of Chief Minister. Following this, Samrat Choudhary was elected as the leader of the NDA legislative party and took over as the new Chief Minister. His appointment marked a historic moment as he became the first Chief Minister from the Bharatiya Janata Party in the state. The swearing-in ceremony took place on April 15, 2026. The new government structure also includes two Deputy Chief Ministers from the Janata Dal (United), reflecting a coalition governance model in the state.

questions.question: Which Indian state’s Legislative Assembly passed the Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Bill, 2026, to enforce stricter penalties for religious sacrilege?
questions.explanation: In April 2026, the Legislative Assembly of Punjab passed the Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Bill, 2026, to impose stricter penalties for acts of sacrilege against the holy Sikh scripture. The bill was passed unanimously during a special session and introduced stringent punishments, including a minimum imprisonment of 10 years and up to life imprisonment. It also included heavy financial penalties ranging from ₹5 lakh to ₹25 lakh. This legislative move reflects the state’s commitment to protecting religious sentiments and maintaining law and order concerning sensitive cultural and spiritual matters.

questions.question: In which country has sexual violence against women reportedly quadrupled over the past three years of conflict, as highlighted in a 2026 UN Women report?
questions.explanation: The 2026 UN Women report highlighted a severe escalation in sexual violence against women in Sudan, where such cases have increased fourfold since the conflict began. The war, now in its fourth year, has led to widespread humanitarian challenges, including mass displacement and lack of access to essential services. Millions of women and girls are internally displaced, particularly in regions like Darfur and Kordofan. Women-led organizations are actively providing aid but face funding shortages and security threats. The crisis underscores the urgent need for international attention and support to address gender-based violence and humanitarian needs in the region.

questions.question: Who was named the Global Brand Ambassador of Infosys in April 2026 to promote AI-powered digital transformation in sports?
questions.explanation: Carlos Alcaraz was appointed as the Global Brand Ambassador of Infosys as part of a multi-year partnership announced on April 15, 2026. He represents the company in promoting the use of advanced technologies such as Generative AI and data analytics in professional sports. Alcaraz, a highly accomplished tennis player, has won seven Grand Slam titles and became the youngest male World No. 1 in history. His association also includes collaboration through his foundation for social initiatives, while Infosys leverages its AI platform, Topaz, to enhance performance analytics and coaching strategies.

questions.question: In which state was India’s first university-based Quantum Reference Facility inaugurated at SRM University-AP in April 2026?
questions.explanation: India’s first university-based Quantum Reference Facility (QRF) was inaugurated at SRM University-AP in Andhra Pradesh by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on April 14, 2026, coinciding with World Quantum Day. The facility is part of the Amaravati Quantum Valley Project and is designed to test and certify quantum hardware with capabilities of up to 100 qubits. Developed with support from institutions like TIFR, IISc, and DRDO, it aims to advance research in areas such as cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and drug discovery, strengthening India’s position in quantum technology development.

questions.question: What was the total value of India’s exports in the financial year 2025–26?
questions.explanation: India achieved a record total export value of $860.09 billion in the financial year 2025–26, reflecting a growth of 4.22% compared to the previous fiscal year. This increase was driven by both merchandise and services exports, with services showing notable growth. Despite the strong export performance, imports grew at a faster rate, resulting in a widened trade deficit. The export growth highlights India’s expanding global trade presence and diversification across sectors, while also indicating the need to manage rising imports to maintain a balanced trade position.

questions.question: Where was the Naval Commanders’ Conference-2026 held on April 14, 2026?
questions.explanation: The Naval Commanders’ Conference-2026 was conducted at Nausena Bhawan, the Integrated Headquarters of the Ministry of Defence (Navy), located in New Delhi. The event brought together senior naval officials and operational commanders to deliberate on strategic priorities such as combat readiness, energy security, and adoption of emerging technologies. Being hosted in the national capital highlights the importance of centralised defence coordination and decision-making. The conference also emphasised strengthening India’s maritime presence in the Indian Ocean Region and enhancing cooperation with friendly foreign countries through joint initiatives.

questions.question: In which state did the State Road Transport Corporation introduce a QR code-based real-time passenger feedback system in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation implemented a QR code-based feedback system across its buses to enhance passenger service and grievance redressal. QR codes were installed behind seats in AC and Volvo buses and at least one in standard buses, allowing commuters to rate services like cleanliness, punctuality, and staff behaviour, and upload photos. In March 2026, the system recorded 1,702 responses with an average satisfaction rating of 4.5 out of 5. Safety received the highest rating, indicating strong performance. The initiative reflects Gujarat’s focus on improving public transport quality and passenger experience.

questions.question: Who chaired the 7th District Collectors’ Peyjal Samvad held on April 15, 2026?
questions.explanation: Ashok Meena, Secretary of the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), chaired the 7th District Collectors’ Peyjal Samvad on April 15, 2026. The meeting focused on accelerating the implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 and Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen Phase 2. Key initiatives discussed included Jal Arpan for asset transfer to Gram Panchayats and Jal Seva Aankalan for performance assessment. The session also highlighted digital governance tools like Sujala Gaon ID and Sujalam Bharat App, along with district-level achievements in water supply, sanitation, and waste management across various regions.

questions.question: Which country opposed the two-tier permanent membership system and supported the G4 proposal during the UNSC reform discussions in April 2026?
questions.explanation: India strongly opposed the idea of a two-tier permanent membership system in the United Nations Security Council, arguing that it would create inequality by granting some permanent members no veto powers. Instead, it backed the G4 proposal, which suggests deferring veto rights for newly added permanent members for 15 years until a review is conducted. Represented by Ambassador P. Harish, India emphasised fair reform and expansion of both permanent and non-permanent categories. The stance reflects India’s long-standing demand for a more equitable and representative UNSC structure.

questions.question: Which company collaborated with OpenAI to integrate UPI and other payment methods into the Codex AI coding platform in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Razorpay partnered with OpenAI to integrate payment capabilities directly into the Codex AI coding platform, enabling developers to embed payment gateways into applications in under five minutes. This innovation simplifies the process of monetisation by removing complex infrastructure requirements. The collaboration also supports AI-driven financial operations through ChatGPT, including tracking settlements and managing refunds. Additionally, Razorpay worked with NPCI to develop agentic payment systems, allowing AI to complete transactions on behalf of users, leveraging India’s robust digital payment ecosystem, handling billions of UPI transactions monthly.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian woman and second woman globally to reach Mount Everest Base Camp using a bicycle in March 2026?
questions.explanation: Divya Singh achieved a remarkable feat by cycling to Mount Everest Base Camp, reaching there on March 24, 2026. She became the first Indian woman and the second woman in the world to accomplish this journey by bicycle. Starting from Kathmandu on March 16, she completed the expedition in 14 days, navigating challenging high-altitude terrain with low oxygen levels and temperatures as low as -12°C. She also hoisted the flag at an altitude of 17,560 feet, marking a significant milestone in adventure sports and endurance cycling.

questions.question: What was the annual rate of inflation based on the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) for March 2026 in India?
questions.explanation: The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation for March 2026 in India was recorded at 3.88% on a year-on-year basis. WPI reflects price changes at the wholesale or factory level and is an important indicator of inflationary trends in the economy. Among the components, Primary Articles showed higher inflation at 6.36%, while Manufactured Products stood at 3.39% and Fuel & Power at 1.05%. Despite stable food inflation at 1.85%, sharp price fluctuations were observed in commodities like crude petroleum and vegetables, indicating sector-specific volatility within the broader inflation framework.

questions.question: Which state launched a statewide AI literacy programme in 2026 to educate nearly 2 million government school students?
questions.explanation: In April 2026, Telangana introduced a large-scale AI literacy programme aimed at equipping nearly 2 million students in government schools with foundational knowledge in artificial intelligence. The initiative involves partnerships with organisations like Amazon Future Engineer and Pi Jam Foundation, ensuring both technological and educational support. The curriculum, designed by SCERT Telangana, targets students from Classes 5 to 9 and includes structured hours of AI learning annually. With additional measures such as teacher training and laptop distribution, the programme strengthens digital education infrastructure and prepares students for future technological advancements.

questions.question: Which bank partnered with Reliance Jio to launch the BoB World Lite mobile banking application for feature phone users in 2026?
questions.explanation: The BoB World Lite application was launched as a collaborative initiative between Bank of Baroda and Reliance Jio to enhance financial inclusion in India. Designed specifically for feature phone users, the app enables access to digital banking services without requiring a smartphone. It supports both existing customers and new users through a self-onboarding process. This innovation is significant as it targets millions of users who rely on basic mobile devices, aligning with the Reserve Bank of India’s push for inclusive digital payment systems and expanding banking accessibility across diverse population segments.

questions.question: On which date was World Voice Day observed globally in 2026?
questions.explanation: World Voice Day in 2026 was observed on April 16 as part of a global initiative to promote awareness about vocal health and prevent voice-related disorders. The day emphasises the importance of maintaining vocal hygiene through proper hydration, avoiding strain, and seeking early medical intervention when issues arise. It also supports professionals who rely heavily on their voice, such as teachers, singers, and speakers. The observance has grown internationally since its origin in Brazil in 1999 and now involves widespread participation, research initiatives, and educational activities to reduce stigma around vocal health problems.

questions.question: Which state government signed an MoU with the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) in 2026 to reduce fatalities caused by lightning strikes?
questions.explanation: In April 2026, the Government of Andhra Pradesh entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with the National Remote Sensing Centre to address the growing concern of lightning-related fatalities. The agreement focuses on identifying high-risk zones, improving early warning systems, and implementing preventive strategies, particularly in rural areas where vulnerability is higher. This collaboration combines scientific expertise from NRSC with administrative support from the state disaster management authority. The initiative aims to enhance disaster preparedness and response mechanisms, ultimately reducing the loss of life and property due to lightning incidents.

questions.question: Which institution developed a brain-inspired hafnium-oxide memristor that significantly reduces AI energy consumption?
questions.explanation: The development of the hafnium-oxide memristor was announced on April 17, 2026, by researchers from the University of Cambridge. This innovative device mimics brain-like synaptic behaviour by combining memory storage and processing into a single component, reducing energy consumption in AI systems by over 70%. Its efficient design replaces traditional architectures that rely on heavy data transfer between memory and processors. The use of hafnium oxide also ensures compatibility with existing semiconductor manufacturing, making the technology both practical and scalable for future applications.

questions.question: Which country is hosting the 7th edition of the bilateral military exercise Dustlik in 2026?
questions.explanation: The 7th edition of Exercise Dustlik in 2026 is being hosted by Uzbekistan at the Gurumsaray Field Training Area in Namangan. It focuses on enhancing coordination and interoperability in special operations, especially in challenging terrains like mountainous and urban regions. The exercise also promotes defence cooperation, strengthens bilateral relations, and enables both armies to share best practices, thereby contributing to improved readiness and regional stability.

questions.question: Who won the FIDE Women’s Candidates Tournament 2026 and became the challenger for the Women's World Chess Championship?
questions.explanation: R. Vaishali emerged as the winner of the FIDE Women’s Candidates Tournament 2026 held in Cyprus, securing 8.5 points out of 14. Her victory in the final round against Kateryna Lagno ensured her top position in the standings. At just 24 years old, she earned the opportunity to challenge reigning world champion Ju Wenjun for the Women’s World Chess Championship title. Vaishali’s achievement is significant as she becomes one of the few Indian women to reach this stage, marking a major milestone for Indian chess and highlighting her consistent performance at the international level.

questions.question: What was India’s unemployment rate in March 2026, marking a five-month high?
questions.explanation: In March 2026, India’s unemployment rate rose to 5.1%, reaching a five-month high. This increase was mainly attributed to rising joblessness in urban areas, where unemployment was significantly higher compared to rural regions. The data also indicated a decline in the Worker Population Ratio, reflecting reduced employment levels. Youth unemployment showed a noticeable rise, particularly among young women. Additionally, the Labour Force Participation Rate declined, highlighting reduced engagement in economic activity. These trends provide insights into labor market challenges and are crucial for policymakers in assessing economic conditions and planning corrective measures.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Secretary General of FICCI in April 2026?
questions.explanation: In April 2026, FICCI appointed Anant Swarup as its new Secretary General, marking a significant leadership update in one of India’s oldest and most prominent industry bodies. He is a 1992-batch Indian Railway Personnel Service officer with extensive experience in government administration and international trade. His career includes roles such as Additional Secretary in the Department of Commerce and Director General of Trade Remedies. With expertise in trade law, infrastructure, and logistics, his appointment is expected to strengthen FICCI’s role in policy advocacy and industry representation.

questions.question: Which state cabinet approved the formation of a committee to draft the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in April 2026?
questions.explanation: In April 2026, the Chhattisgarh Cabinet approved the creation of a high-level committee to draft a Uniform Civil Code, aiming to establish a common legal framework for personal matters such as marriage, divorce, inheritance, and adoption. The committee will be led by retired Supreme Court judge Ranjana Prakash Desai and will gather inputs from citizens, experts, and stakeholders before preparing the final draft. This move aligns with the Directive Principles of State Policy under Article 44 of the Constitution, which encourages the adoption of a uniform civil code across the country.

questions.question: Who was named the 2026 Person of the Year by the Harvard South Asian Association?
questions.explanation: The Harvard South Asian Association recognized Sayani Gupta as the 2026 Person of the Year for her impactful contributions to film and storytelling, along with her role in enhancing South Asian representation globally. This award is presented annually to individuals who significantly influence cultural identity and representation across various platforms. Sayani Gupta’s work in both mainstream and independent cinema, as well as on digital platforms, has earned her acclaim for portraying diverse and meaningful roles. The recognition highlights her growing influence in shaping narratives that resonate with global audiences.

questions.question: Who was elected unopposed as the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha for a third consecutive term in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Harivansh Narayan Singh was elected unopposed as the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha in April 2026, marking his third consecutive term in this position. His election took place during a special session of Parliament, reflecting a broad consensus among members. As a nominated member of the Upper House, his appointment is historically significant, as he became the first nominated member to hold this office. He has been recognized for his effective parliamentary conduct and efficient use of MPLADS funds, demonstrating administrative competence and commitment to public service over his previous terms.

questions.question: Which state government signed an MoU with NICDC Logistics Data Services Limited (NLDSL) in 2026 to digitise its logistics sector?
questions.explanation: In April 2026, the Government of Maharashtra partnered with NICDC Logistics Data Services Limited to modernise and digitise its logistics ecosystem through the Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP). The initiative focuses on improving efficiency, transparency, and real-time tracking within the logistics value chain, especially benefiting MSMEs and small exporters. Various digital tools such as the Logistics Data Bank, Koyla Shakti dashboard, and Track Your Transport system are part of this transformation. By integrating multiple systems and data sources, the project aims to streamline operations, reduce costs, and enhance the overall competitiveness of the state’s logistics infrastructure.

questions.question: In which state was the Ekatma Parv cultural festival inaugurated at Omkareshwar in 2026?
questions.explanation: The Ekatma Parv cultural festival was inaugurated in Omkareshwar, a significant spiritual site known for its association with Adi Guru Shankaracharya. The event highlights the principles of Advaita Vedanta and aims to connect traditional philosophy with contemporary themes such as artificial intelligence, environmental sustainability, and youth engagement. The festival also includes initiatives like the ‘Shankardoot’ pledge and features landmarks such as the Statue of Oneness and the upcoming Advaita Lok museum. This initiative promotes cultural heritage, spiritual learning, and global dialogue on peace and unity.

questions.question: Who felicitated top-performing ministries, states, and departments at the SADHANA Saptah 2026 ceremony?
questions.explanation: The SADHANA Saptah 2026 ceremony recognized excellence in digital capacity building across government institutions, with Union Minister Jitendra Singh leading the felicitation. The initiative saw massive participation, with millions of government employees engaging in structured learning programs under the Mission Karmayogi framework. It emphasised inclusivity by involving employees across all levels, including frontline workers. The program also highlighted the importance of adopting emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence to make the workforce future-ready. Coordinated by the Capacity Building Commission, it aims to institutionalise continuous skill development in governance.

questions.question: India is set to sign a Free Trade Agreement (FTA) with which country on April 27, 2026?
questions.explanation: India is scheduled to sign a Free Trade Agreement with New Zealand on April 27, 2026, aiming to strengthen bilateral economic ties and enhance market access. The agreement includes provisions for zero-duty access on Indian exports and reduced tariffs on most New Zealand goods, excluding sensitive sectors like dairy and certain agricultural products. It also facilitates mobility by allowing skilled Indian professionals to work temporarily in New Zealand. With targets to significantly boost trade and investment, the FTA represents a major step in expanding India’s global trade partnerships and economic cooperation.

questions.question: Who concluded the Chintan Shivir 2026, aimed at expanding insurance coverage for Ayush treatments in New Delhi?
questions.explanation: Prataprao Jadhav, serving as the Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for the Ministry of Ayush, concluded the Chintan Shivir 2026 in New Delhi. The two-day summit focused on expanding insurance coverage for traditional medicine systems under AYUSH and improving claim settlement processes for patients. The event included multiple strategic sessions to strengthen the sector and introduced digital initiatives like an official WhatsApp channel for better public engagement. These measures aim to enhance accessibility, credibility, and integration of AYUSH treatments within the broader healthcare system.

questions.question: In which state was the new snake species Calamaria garoensis discovered in 2026?
questions.explanation: The newly identified snake species, Calamaria garoensis, was discovered in the West Garo Hills region, a biodiversity-rich area known for its dense forests and ecological significance. This species was earlier misclassified but later recognised as distinct through detailed taxonomic research. The discovery highlights the rich herpetofaunal diversity of Northeast India, particularly within the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot. Meghalaya, with its unique terrain and ecosystems, continues to be a crucial region for biological discoveries, contributing significantly to scientific understanding and conservation of lesser-known reptile species.
