questions.question: Which state launched Project Zero as a zero-tolerance anti-corruption initiative in May 2026?
questions.explanation: The Kerala government launched Project Zero on May 26, 2026, as a comprehensive anti-corruption initiative aimed at ensuring zero tolerance towards bribery and promoting transparent public service delivery. The initiative is implemented by the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) through a structured and phased approach. Its key objectives include ensuring corruption-free access to government services, protecting whistleblowers with confidentiality, and strengthening internal vigilance systems through training and monitoring. The program also integrates advanced technology to detect modern digital forms of corruption and updates the long-standing Vigilance Manual of 1969 to align with current investigative needs. The initiative reflects Kerala’s broader commitment to administrative transparency and ethical governance.

questions.question: Which state launched the ₹236 crore Mission Queen Pineapple to develop an integrated value-chain ecosystem for GI-tagged Queen Pineapple?
questions.explanation: Tripura launched the ₹236 crore Mission Queen Pineapple on May 27, 2026, in collaboration with the Union Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER). The initiative is designed as a three-year roadmap from FY2026 to FY2028 to strengthen the production, processing, and marketing of the GI-tagged Queen Pineapple, which is one of the state’s key horticultural products. The project includes establishing a hub near Agartala airport and multiple spoke collection centers across districts, along with reviving the Nalkata Pineapple Processing Unit through a Viability Gap Funding model. It also promotes bio-economy initiatives such as bromelain extraction, pineapple leaf fiber processing, and GI-branded value-added products to boost farmer income and rural development.

questions.question: Which state launched the ‘Farm to Home’ programme for direct marketing of agricultural produce through Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs)?
questions.explanation: Andhra Pradesh launched the ‘Farm to Home’ programme on May 27, 2026, under the leadership of Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu to improve farmer income through direct marketing of produce. The initiative focuses on delivering fresh agricultural products directly to households via Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), reducing intermediaries in the supply chain. Alongside this, the state reviewed multiple agricultural and allied sector missions, including infrastructure development such as Cocoa City at Yadavolu and the Indian School of Agriculture at Madanapalle. The programme also integrates digital initiatives like the Digi Rythu Bazaar app, modernisation of Rythu Bazaars, and promotion of natural farming techniques, strengthening Andhra Pradesh’s agricultural economy and rural development framework.

questions.question: Which state inaugurated a ₹3 crore solar power plant managed by women Self-Help Groups (SHGs) in Khammam district?
questions.explanation: Telangana inaugurated a ₹3 crore solar power plant managed entirely by women Self-Help Groups (SHGs) under the Indira Mahila Shakti scheme on May 27, 2026. The project is located in Venkatapuram village in Errupalem mandal of Madhira constituency in Khammam district. It represents a major step in empowering women economically by involving SHGs in renewable energy production and management. The plant operates under Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) with DISCOMs, ensuring a guaranteed buyback of electricity and steady income generation. It is expected to earn daily revenue between ₹14,000 and ₹15,000. The initiative reflects Telangana’s broader push toward renewable energy adoption and women-led economic development.

questions.question: Which country’s state nuclear corporation Rosatom is leading the construction of Kazakhstan’s first nuclear power plant?
questions.explanation: Russia, through its state nuclear corporation Rosatom, has been appointed as the lead builder for Kazakhstan’s first nuclear power plant under a $16.5 billion agreement signed on May 28, 2026. The project aims to address Kazakhstan’s growing energy deficit and will be located in Ulken village near Lake Balkhash. It includes the installation of two VVER-1200 reactors, with construction expected to begin in 2027 and the first reactor targeted for completion by 2034. The Russian government will also provide export credit to support financing. This collaboration strengthens Russia’s role in global nuclear energy development and highlights expanding energy cooperation between Russia and Kazakhstan.

questions.question: Which company partnered with Israel’s Elbit Systems to establish India’s first private propellant manufacturing facility in Shirdi, Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: Nibe Group entered into a joint venture with Israel’s Elbit Systems on May 25, 2026, to establish India’s first private propellant manufacturing facility in Shirdi, Maharashtra. The collaboration aims to strengthen India’s defence manufacturing ecosystem under the “Make in India” and “Atmanirbhar Bharat” initiatives. The facility will produce key materials such as nitrocellulose, nitroglycerine, and various types of propellants including single, double, and triple base variants. Elbit Systems will provide technical expertise, while Nibe Group will manage investment and operations. The plant is expected to support advanced defence production, including artillery systems, missile technologies, rocket systems, and autonomous defence platforms, enhancing India’s strategic self-reliance.

questions.question: Which institution signed three maintenance contracts with the Indian Air Force for predictive maintenance of Su-30 MKI fighter aircraft?
questions.explanation: The Indian Air Force (IAF) signed three contracts with IIT Bombay on May 29, 2026, to implement predictive maintenance solutions for the Su-30 MKI fighter aircraft fleet. The initiative focuses on prognostic and prescriptive maintenance techniques aimed at reducing service costs and improving aircraft availability and operational lifespan. Developed using indigenous expertise at IIT Bombay, the project marks a shift toward data-driven engineering in defence systems. The agreement supports the modernisation of maintenance practices for one of India’s key multi-role fighter platforms. IIT Bombay, established in 1958 at Powai, Mumbai, has collaborated with the IAF to enhance technological innovation and strengthen self-reliant defence capabilities.

questions.question: In which city was the 35th India-China Working Mechanism for Consultation & Coordination (WMCC) meeting on border affairs held?
questions.explanation: The 35th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation & Coordination (WMCC) on India-China border affairs was held on 27 May 2026 in Beijing. The WMCC serves as an important institutional dialogue mechanism established in 2012 to maintain peace and stability along the India-China border. The meeting was led by Shri Sujit Ghosh from the Indian side and Ms. Hou Yanqi from the Chinese side. Discussions focused on border management, delimitation issues, and strengthening communication mechanisms. Both sides also emphasised preparations for future Special Representatives (SR) meetings and continued cooperation through established diplomatic and military channels to ensure peace and stability in border regions.

questions.question: Which state police force was awarded the President of India’s Police Colour in May 2026?
questions.explanation: The Sikkim Police was awarded the prestigious President of India’s Police Colour by President Droupadi Murmu on May 28, 2026, in Gangtok. This honour is the highest recognition given to any police force in India for exceptional and meritorious service. Established in 1897, the Sikkim Police has completed over 125 years of service in maintaining law and order and ensuring public safety. The award highlights its transformation from a colonial-era policing system to a more citizen-centric and transparent institution. The recognition also emphasises reforms focused on accountability, protection of vulnerable groups, especially women and children, and strengthening trust between the police and the public in line with modern governance goals.

questions.question: Who has been given an extension of additional charge as Director (Projects) of GAIL (India) Limited from June 1, 2026?
questions.explanation: Deepak Gupta has been granted an extension of his additional charge as Director (Projects) of GAIL (India) Limited for a period of six months starting from June 1, 2026, by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. This arrangement will remain valid until a regular incumbent is appointed or until further orders are issued. He is currently serving as the Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) of GAIL, India’s largest natural gas processing and distribution company. GAIL, established in 1984 and headquartered in New Delhi, holds Maharatna status and operates under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, playing a key role in the country’s energy infrastructure and gas transmission network.

questions.question: Which organisation partnered with EdCIL (India) Limited to establish Smart Digital Classrooms under a CSR initiative?
questions.explanation: Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) signed a Memorandum of Understanding with EdCIL (India) Limited on May 26, 2026, to develop Smart Digital Classrooms under a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative. The project aims to enhance inclusive education and improve learning outcomes by installing digital classrooms in schools located near SAIL’s operational areas. It aligns with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and contributes to Sustainable Development Goal 4, which focuses on quality education for all. SAIL, a Maharatna CPSE under the Ministry of Steel, and EdCIL, a Miniratna CPSE under the Ministry of Education, are collaborating to strengthen educational infrastructure and promote equitable access to modern learning resources.

questions.question: Which Indian peacekeepers are set to receive the Dag Hammarskjold Medal posthumously in 2026?
options: Harbhajan Singh and Sujit Kumar Pradhan
questions.answer: Harbhajan Singh and Sujit Kumar Pradhan
questions.explanation: Harbhajan Singh and Sujit Kumar Pradhan are scheduled to be posthumously awarded the United Nations Dag Hammarskjold Medal on May 29, 2026, in recognition of their distinguished service in UN peacekeeping missions. Harbhajan Singh served in MONUSCO in the Democratic Republic of Congo, while Sujit Kumar Pradhan served in UNMISS in South Sudan. The award is presented on International Day of UN Peacekeepers, observed annually on May 29, which commemorates the establishment of the first UN peacekeeping mission in 1948. The Dag Hammarskjold Medal is the highest posthumous honour for peacekeepers, named after the second UN Secretary-General, recognising those who sacrificed their lives in the service of global peace and security.

questions.question: In which city was the 11th Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting held in May 2026?
questions.explanation: The 11th Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting was held in New Delhi on May 26, 2026, bringing together India, Australia, Japan, and the United States to strengthen cooperation in the Indo-Pacific region. The meeting focused on key areas such as maritime security, critical technologies, infrastructure development, and economic resilience. A major outcome was the launch of the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration (IPMSC) to improve maritime domain awareness, particularly in the Indian Ocean Region. The discussions also covered defence interoperability exercises, undersea cable connectivity for Pacific Island nations, and investments in energy and communication technologies like 6G and Open RAN. The Quad continues to promote a free, open, and rules-based Indo-Pacific order.

questions.question: Which state was officially recognised as India’s fifth fully literate state under the ULLAS initiative in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Sikkim was officially declared India’s fifth fully literate state on May 28, 2026, under the ULLAS (Understanding Lifelong Learning for All in Society) initiative, also known as the Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram. This recognition aligns with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 framework, which focuses on improving foundational literacy, numeracy, and lifelong learning opportunities. With this achievement, Sikkim joins other fully literate states such as Mizoram, Goa, Tripura, and Himachal Pradesh. The ULLAS program targets non-literate individuals aged 15 and above and promotes comprehensive education through multiple skill-based components. This milestone highlights Sikkim’s continued progress in education and social development, reinforcing its role as a leader in human development indicators in India.

questions.question: Which country's President, U Min Aung Hlaing, began a five-day official visit to India in May 2026 to strengthen bilateral and civilizational ties?
questions.explanation: President U Min Aung Hlaing of Myanmar arrived in Gaya, Bihar, on May 30, 2026, for a five-day official visit to India. The visit was aimed at enhancing bilateral cooperation and reinforcing long-standing civilizational and cultural ties between the two neighbouring countries. During the visit, he paid respects at the Mahabodhi Temple in Bodh Gaya, a globally significant Buddhist pilgrimage site. The agenda also included high-level discussions with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, participation in a business forum, and engagements with industry leaders in Mumbai. The visit marked his first trip to India since assuming the office of President in April 2026.

questions.question: In which city was the Nausena Shaurya Vatika naval museum inaugurated by Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath in May 2026?
questions.explanation: The Nausena Shaurya Vatika naval museum was inaugurated in Lucknow on May 30, 2026, by Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Developed as an open-air museum at a cost of ₹19 crore over two acres, it showcases important naval artefacts and weapon systems from the decommissioned warship INS Gomati. Key attractions include the AK 726 Naval Gun, ZIF 101 missile launcher, TU 142M long-range maritime patrol aircraft, anti-ship missiles, torpedo launchers, and ship masts. The museum aims to promote awareness of India's naval heritage, military achievements, and maritime defence capabilities among the public.

questions.question: Which country signed a framework with India in May 2026 for cooperation in the supply of critical minerals and rare earths?
questions.explanation: India and the United States signed a framework agreement in New Delhi to strengthen cooperation in the supply of critical minerals and rare earths. The agreement was signed by External Affairs Minister Dr S. Jaishankar and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. It focuses on areas such as mining, processing, recycling of minerals, development of diversified supply chains, financing collaboration, and effective management of rare earths scrap. The framework builds upon commitments made in the India-U.S. Joint Statement of February 2025 and supports broader strategic initiatives such as Pax Silica, FORGE, and the India-U.S. AI Opportunity Partnership, enhancing bilateral cooperation in critical sectors.

questions.question: Which state collaborated with SIDBI on May 27, 2026, to launch a dedicated angel fund for deep-tech and emerging technology startups?
questions.explanation: Andhra Pradesh partnered with SIDBI to establish a dedicated angel fund aimed at supporting deep-tech and emerging technology startups. The initiative is being implemented through the Ratan Tata Innovation Hub (RTIH), which will provide funding, resources, and growth opportunities to innovative ventures. The fund focuses on sectors such as artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, electronics manufacturing, advanced manufacturing, and clean energy. Designed as a seed fund, it seeks to help startups access capital and real-world applications while enabling them to scale globally. The initiative also aligns with Andhra Pradesh’s broader economic and innovation-driven development strategy.

questions.question: In which state did the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) launch Operation Chakravyuh in May 2026 to dismantle organised drug trafficking networks?
questions.explanation: Operation Chakravyuh was launched by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) on May 30, 2026, to combat organised drug trafficking networks in Kerala. The operation involved coordinated actions across Kochi, Malappuram, and Thiruvananthapuram, leading to the seizure of 24 kg of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, including Methaqualone, Methamphetamine, and Hashish oil. Authorities apprehended five individuals under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. The operation highlighted various smuggling methods such as airport passenger baggage, courier consignments, and export cargo, demonstrating the government's continued efforts to strengthen anti-drug enforcement and curb illicit trafficking activities.

questions.question: In which country was the world's first simultaneous transplantation of a whole pig liver and two pig kidneys into a human recipient performed on June 1, 2026?
questions.explanation: The groundbreaking xenotransplantation procedure was carried out at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Guangxi Medical University in Nanning, China. It marked the first time that a whole pig liver and two pig kidneys were transplanted simultaneously into a human recipient. The donor pig had undergone six genetic modifications, including the addition of three human genes and the removal of three pig genes, to reduce the risk of rejection and blood clotting. The transplanted organs functioned successfully for several days, with the liver producing bile and the kidneys normalising waste-product levels. The achievement represents a significant advancement in xenotransplantation research and organ replacement therapies.

questions.question: Which fintech company received in-principle approval from the RBI for a Payment Aggregator-Physical (PA-P) license on May 26, 2026?
questions.explanation: Mobikwik, officially known as One Mobikwik Systems, received in-principle approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for a Payment Aggregator-Physical (PA-P) license on May 26, 2026. This approval allows the company to expand its services beyond online payments and facilitate offline merchant transactions as well. Payment Aggregators play a crucial role in enabling merchants to accept various payment methods from customers. Founded in 2009 and headquartered in Gurugram, Haryana, Mobikwik was co-founded by Bipin Preet Singh and Upasana Taku. The development strengthens the company’s position in India’s growing digital payments ecosystem.

questions.question: Which country received the sacred relics of Arahant Sariputta and Arahant Mahamoggallana transported by the Indian Air Force in May, 2026?
questions.explanation: The Indian Air Force transported the sacred relics of Arahant Sariputta and Arahant Mahamoggallana to Mongolia using its IL-76 strategic airlift aircraft, popularly known as Gajraj. These relics belong to the two chief disciples of Gautama Buddha and hold immense significance in Buddhist traditions. The initiative was undertaken to strengthen cultural and spiritual ties between India and Mongolia while supporting India’s broader cultural diplomacy and global outreach efforts. Such exchanges help promote shared heritage, deepen people-to-people connections, and reinforce historical links between Buddhist communities across nations. Mongolia, a landlocked country between Russia and China, has a strong Buddhist cultural heritage.

questions.question: Which application was launched by the Union Health Secretary to monitor compliance with tobacco-control norms in schools and colleges?
questions.explanation: The Tobacco-Free Educational Institutions (ToFEI) App was launched by the Union Health Secretary to strengthen the implementation of tobacco-control regulations in educational institutions across India. The application is designed to monitor compliance with rules that prohibit the sale of tobacco products within 100 yards of schools and colleges. Initially introduced as a pilot project in Rajasthan, Meghalaya, and Maharashtra, the app is intended for nationwide rollout. Alongside the app, a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for tobacco sample collection was also launched to ensure scientific accuracy and support legal enforcement. The initiative aligns with broader efforts to reduce tobacco use and protect youth from nicotine addiction.

questions.question: Which country is targeted under the NSDC and Fourth Valley Concierge Corporation partnership to facilitate the movement of at least 50,000 skilled Indian professionals over five years?
questions.explanation: The National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) partnered with Tokyo-based Fourth Valley Concierge Corporation (FVCC) on May 26, 2026, to enhance workforce mobility for Indian professionals. The collaboration aims to facilitate the movement of at least 50,000 skilled Indian workers to Japan over a five-year period. A key component of the initiative is the implementation of the "Credibility Check" system through NSDC Trust, which verifies identity, educational qualifications, employment history, and background records. The partnership supports the India-Japan human resource exchange action plan and seeks to improve transparency, trust, and opportunities for Indian talent in the Japanese workforce.

questions.question: Which institution developed a patented, injectable hydrogel made from silk cocoons and seaweed for treating fibrosis, announced on May 29, 2026?
questions.explanation: Researchers at IIT Madras developed a patented, cost-effective injectable hydrogel using silk cocoons and seaweed for the treatment of fibrosis and other degenerative conditions. The hydrogel is biodegradable and biocompatible, and it transforms from a liquid into a gel at body temperature, allowing it to adapt to the treatment site. The innovation aims to reduce therapy costs significantly, from around USD 2,000–3,000 to nearly USD 300. It has potential applications in treating pulmonary, liver, kidney, and muscle fibrosis, as well as Sarcopenia. The research was led by Prof. Vignesh Muthuvijayan and Ms Varshiny Gopinath of IIT Madras.

questions.question: What was India's global rank among countries that have deployed the advanced SkyCast integrated aviation weather monitoring system?
questions.explanation: India became the 19th country globally to deploy the advanced SkyCast integrated aviation weather monitoring system with its launch at Indira Gandhi International Airport in New Delhi. Developed under the Mission Mausam initiative, the system enhances aviation safety by providing real-time weather intelligence and short-term nowcasting services. It integrates sophisticated instruments such as a Radar Wind Profiler, Ground-based Fog Aerosol Spectrometer (GFAS), and CL61 Lidar Ceilometer. These technologies monitor atmospheric conditions including wind patterns and boundary-layer dynamics, helping reduce weather-related flight delays and improving the safety of aircraft take-offs and landings. Future expansion is planned for other airports across India.

questions.question: In which Indian state did ZSI scientists record the new cascade-dwelling frog species Amolops kamal in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Amolops kamal is a newly discovered species of cascade-dwelling frog recorded by scientists of the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI) on May 30, 2026. The species was found in the Kiphire district near Singrep village, located in Nagaland close to the India–Myanmar border. It belongs to the Amolops indoburmanensis species complex and the Amolops marmoratus species group. Molecular phylogenetic studies confirmed it as a distinct evolutionary lineage. The frog was named in honour of Kamal Choudhury, a mentor at B. Barooah College, Guwahati, and is commonly known as the Nagaland cascade frog.

questions.question: Which state is home to the SIRI Mathrushree Industrial Park inaugurated by Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan in May 2026?
questions.explanation: The SIRI Mathrushree Industrial Park was inaugurated in May 2026 in Belthangady of Dakshina Kannada district, Karnataka. The project was established to promote rural entrepreneurship and support women-led social transformation. It directly benefits more than 3,000 individuals and indirectly supports over 10,000 people, mainly women from disadvantaged sections of society. The park includes essential facilities such as hostels, residential quarters, childcare services, transportation arrangements, and hygienic kitchens. By creating livelihood opportunities and strengthening social infrastructure, the initiative contributes significantly to rural development and women's economic empowerment in Karnataka.

questions.question: Who assumed the additional charge of Chairman of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Rajesh Kumar Singh assumed the additional charge of Chairman of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and Secretary of the Department of Defence Research and Development on May 31, 2026. The appointment was approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet following the retirement of Dr. Samir V. Kamat, whom he succeeded. A 1989-batch IAS officer of the Kerala cadre, Singh has been serving as the Defence Secretary since November 2024. Before that, he served as Secretary of the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT). DRDO plays a crucial role in advancing India's self-reliance in defence technologies and strengthening national security capabilities.

questions.question: Who assumed charge as India's new Chief of Defence Staff (CDS in May 2026?
questions.explanation: General NS Raja Subramani assumed charge as India's Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) on 31 May 2026, succeeding General Anil Chauhan. As the country's highest-ranking military officer, the CDS serves as the principal military adviser to the Government of India and plays a crucial role in enhancing coordination among the Army, Navy, and Air Force. With more than four decades of military experience, General Subramani has held several important positions, including Vice Chief of Army Staff, Military Advisor at the National Security Council Secretariat, and General Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Central Command. His appointment is expected to further strengthen defence reforms, military modernisation, and tri-services integration in India.

questions.question: Who assumed charge as the Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Western Naval Command in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Vice Admiral Sanjay Vatsayan assumed charge as the Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Western Naval Command during a ceremonial parade held in Mumbai on 30 May 2026. Before taking up this position, he served as the 47th Vice Chief of the Naval Staff at Naval Headquarters in New Delhi. Commissioned into the Indian Navy on 1 January 1988, he is a specialist in Gunnery and Missile Systems. Throughout his distinguished career, he has commanded several naval vessels, including INS Vibhuti, INS Nashak, INS Kuthar, and INS Sahyadri. He has also held important strategic appointments and has been awarded the PVSM, AVSM, and Nao Sena Medal for his exemplary service.

questions.question: What was the growth rate of India's industrial production in April 2026 as measured by the Index of Industrial Production (IIP)?
questions.explanation: India's industrial production, measured by the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), recorded a growth rate of 4.9% in April 2026 compared to the same month in the previous year. The increase was driven mainly by the manufacturing sector, which grew by 6.2% and emerged as the key contributor to industrial expansion. During the same period, the government introduced a new IIP series with the base year 2022-23, replacing the earlier 2011-12 series. The revised series includes broader sector coverage, updated weights, additional products, and new categories such as gas supply and water management, making industrial measurement more representative of India's evolving economy.

questions.question: Who assumed charge as the 27th Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS) of the Indian Navy on 31 May 2026?
questions.explanation: Admiral Krishna Swaminathan assumed charge as the 27th Chief of the Naval Staff of the Indian Navy on 31 May 2026, succeeding Admiral Dinesh Kumar Tripathi. Commissioned into the Navy in 1987, he has nearly four decades of distinguished service and is a specialist in Communication and Electronic Warfare. During his career, he commanded several important naval vessels, including INS Vikramaditya, and held key leadership positions such as Commander of the Western Fleet, Vice Chief of the Naval Staff, and Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Western Naval Command. A highly qualified officer with extensive academic credentials, he has also been honoured with the PVSM, AVSM, and VSM for his exceptional service to the nation.

questions.question: Who assumed charge as the 48th Vice Chief of the Naval Staff (VCNS) on 29 May 2026?
questions.explanation: Vice Admiral Ajay Kochhar assumed charge as the 48th Vice Chief of the Naval Staff (VCNS) on 29 May 2026. Commissioned into the Indian Navy on 1 July 1988, he is a specialist in Gunnery and Missile Systems and has served for more than 37 years. During his distinguished naval career, he commanded major warships including the aircraft carrier INS Vikramaditya and the frigate INS Trikand. He also served as Commander-in-Chief of the Andaman and Nicobar Command, Commandant of the National Defence Academy, and Commander of the Western Fleet. His service has been recognised with prestigious honours such as the Param Vishisht Seva Medal, Ati Vishisht Seva Medal, and Nau Sena Medal.

questions.question: Which company partnered with the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) to launch Project Shikhar for helping MSMEs access capital markets?
questions.explanation: Meesho partnered with the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) to launch Project Shikhar, an initiative aimed at supporting Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and digital-first businesses in accessing capital markets. The programme is designed to help high-performing e-commerce sellers transition from privately owned enterprises to publicly listed companies. Through guidance on compliance, corporate governance, regulatory preparedness, restructuring, and listing procedures, Project Shikhar seeks to simplify the public listing process. The initiative also promotes easier access to growth capital, enabling businesses to expand operations, improve transparency, strengthen governance standards, and enhance their credibility among investors and stakeholders.

questions.question: Which state is home to the semiconductor start-up Netrasemi that launched the indigenous A2000 AI system-on-chip in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Netrasemi, a fabless semiconductor start-up established in 2020, is headquartered in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala. The company launched its flagship A2000 AI system-on-chip (SoC) on May 30, 2026, marking a significant step in India’s semiconductor and artificial intelligence ecosystem. The chip is designed for applications such as smart surveillance cameras, edge AI boxes, and intelligent video gateways. It features an in-house Neural Processor, Vision Processing Unit, and Image Signal Processor, along with a patented processing architecture. Supported by the Design Linked Incentive scheme and private investors, Netrasemi is contributing to India's goal of achieving greater self-reliance in advanced semiconductor technologies.

questions.question: Which state celebrates its Formation Day on June 2, commemorating its creation as a separate state in 2014?
questions.explanation: Telangana Formation Day is observed annually on June 2 to mark the creation of Telangana as a separate state in 2014. Formed through the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, Telangana became the 29th state of India after a prolonged statehood movement that sought greater regional identity, equitable development, and self-governance. The movement involved participation from students, farmers, employees, intellectuals, and political leaders over several decades. The day honours the contributions and sacrifices of those who supported the cause of statehood. Celebrations across the state include flag-hoisting ceremonies, tributes to martyrs, cultural programs, public meetings, awards, and exhibitions showcasing Telangana’s rich heritage and identity.

questions.question: By what percentage did gross GST collections grow year-on-year in May 2026?
questions.explanation: 3.2% was the year-on-year growth rate recorded in gross GST collections for May 2026. During the month, gross GST revenue reached ₹1.94 lakh crore, reflecting steady growth in tax collections. The increase was supported by higher economic activity, with taxable goods supplies growing by 26.9% and taxable services supplies rising by 22.2%. After accounting for refunds of ₹27,281 crore, net GST revenue stood at ₹1.67 lakh crore, registering a 3.3% increase. GST, implemented on July 1, 2017, remains one of India's most significant indirect tax reforms aimed at creating a unified national market.

questions.question: Which U.S. state became the first to initiate a lawsuit against OpenAI and its CEO Sam Altman over public safety and consumer deception concerns in June 2026?
questions.explanation: Florida became the first U.S. state to file a lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman on June 2, 2026. The legal action was initiated by the state's Attorney General through an 83-page complaint alleging that rapid commercial expansion and competition in the AI sector were prioritised over user safety. The lawsuit also raised concerns about misleading users regarding potential risks associated with AI systems, inadequate protections for minors, and the alleged facilitation of harmful activities. The case marked a significant development in the evolving debate over AI regulation, accountability, and consumer protection in the United States.

questions.question: Which bank partnered with Visa to launch a premium credit card portfolio for affluent customers on June 2, 2026?
questions.explanation: Karur Vysya Bank partnered with Visa to introduce a premium credit card portfolio aimed at affluent and emerging affluent customers. The portfolio includes four card variants—Aura, Samara, Altura, and Eternis—offering benefits across travel, dining, and premium lifestyle experiences. The initiative is designed to cater to salaried professionals, business owners, and high-value customers seeking enhanced financial and lifestyle services. Established in 1916 and headquartered in Karur, Tamil Nadu, Karur Vysya Bank is one of India’s leading private sector banks. The collaboration with Visa strengthens its premium banking offerings and expands its presence in the credit card segment.

questions.question: Which country co-chaired the second Defence Ministers’ Dialogue with India in New Delhi on June 1, 2026?
questions.explanation: Australia was the partner country that co-chaired the second India-Australia Defence Ministers’ Dialogue held in New Delhi on June 1, 2026. The dialogue was led by India’s Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh and Australia’s Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles. Discussions focused on strengthening maritime security, defence industrial cooperation, military exercises, and Quad-related initiatives in the Indo-Pacific region. Both nations also advanced plans for joint maritime collaboration, search and rescue exercises, defence services agreements, and personnel exchanges. The meeting highlighted the growing strategic partnership between India and Australia, particularly in ensuring security, stability, and cooperation across the Indo-Pacific region.

questions.question: Which Indian men's doubles pair became the first from India to win the Singapore Open title in 2026?
options: Lakshya Sen and H. S. Prannoy
Manu Attri and B. Sumeeth Reddy
Krishna Prasad Garaga and Vishnuvardhan Goud Panjala
questions.explanation: Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty became the first Indian men's doubles pair to win the Singapore Open title by securing the championship in 2026. They achieved this milestone after defeating Indonesia’s Fajar Alfian and Muhammad Fikri in a thrilling three-game final. The victory marked their third BWF Super 750 title and the ninth World Tour title of their careers. The triumph also ended a two-year title drought, with their previous title having come at the Thailand Open in 2024. Ranked World No. 4 at the time, the duo further strengthened their position among the world's leading badminton pairs.

questions.question: Which company announced the launch of the Finserv Intelligence initiative with an investment of up to ₹2,000 crore in AI, cybersecurity, quantum technologies, and fintech platforms?
questions.explanation: Bajaj Finserv launched the Finserv Intelligence initiative on May 29, 2026, with a planned investment of ₹1,500–2,000 crore over five years. The initiative is designed to develop scalable technology solutions for global markets by focusing on advanced fields such as artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, quantum technologies, and fintech platforms. The company has partnered with IIT Bombay for research and plans to build a specialised team of researchers and PhDs. It also aims to support early-stage startups and create technology solutions covering multiple Indian languages and dialects, helping bridge the gap between research and practical innovation in India.

questions.question: Which country signed the landmark Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) with India that came into force in June, 2026?
questions.explanation: Oman is the country with which India’s Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) officially entered into force on June 1, 2026. The agreement establishes a strategic trade corridor connecting India with the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region and East Africa. It provides extensive market access, including duty-free benefits for the majority of Indian exports, while also enhancing cooperation in services, investment, and trade facilitation. The pact supports sectors such as healthcare, engineering, information technology, and pharmaceuticals. It further strengthens bilateral economic ties and leverages Omani ports like Sohar, Duqm, and Salalah to improve regional connectivity and trade opportunities.

questions.question: Who assumed the appointment of Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief (AOC-in-C) of the Central Air Command on June 1, 2026?
options: Air Marshal Rakesh Kumar Singh Bhadauria
questions.explanation: Air Marshal Tarun Chaudhry assumed the appointment of Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief (AOC-in-C) of the Central Air Command on June 1, 2026. He took over the responsibility from Air Marshal Balakrishnan Manikantan, who retired after completing 40 years of distinguished service. Commissioned into the Fighter stream of the Indian Air Force in December 1989, Air Marshal Chaudhry has held several important operational, administrative, and diplomatic assignments. His experience includes serving as Defence Attachee in Sweden and holding senior positions related to projects, acquisitions, and human resource management within the Indian Air Force and integrated defence structures.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution did the President of India appoint five new judges to the Supreme Court on June 1, 2026?
questions.explanation: Article 124(2) empowers the President of India to appoint judges to the Supreme Court. On June 1, 2026, five new judges were appointed to the apex court under this constitutional provision. The appointments included former Chief Justices of various High Courts as well as a Senior Advocate appointed directly from the Bar. The Supreme Court, established on January 28, 1950, is the highest judicial authority in India. Provisions relating to its organisation, composition, powers, and functions are contained in Articles 124 to 147 of the Constitution. The court has a maximum sanctioned strength of 34 judges, including the Chief Justice of India.

questions.question: Which city emerged as India’s second-busiest domestic airport hub in April 2026, surpassing Mumbai in domestic passenger volume?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru emerged as India’s second-busiest domestic airport hub in April 2026 by handling 3.28 million domestic passengers, surpassing Mumbai’s 2.89 million passengers during the same period. This marked the first time since the post-pandemic years that Bengaluru overtook Mumbai in domestic traffic. While Mumbai continued to hold the second position in overall passenger traffic due to its stronger international operations, Bengaluru demonstrated greater resilience with only a marginal decline in domestic traffic. The achievement highlights the growing importance of Kempegowda International Airport as a major aviation hub and reflects increasing passenger demand in southern India.

questions.question: From which state was the month-long nationwide 'Khet Bachao Abhiyan' launched on June 1, 2026?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh is the state from which the month-long nationwide 'Khet Bachao Abhiyan' was launched on June 1, 2026, from Ramasiya village in Raisen district. The campaign focuses on improving soil health through balanced fertiliser use and Soil Health Cards, promoting natural farming, water conservation, and green manure usage, and creating awareness against counterfeit fertilisers and pesticides. It also includes field demonstrations, farmer training on modern agricultural technologies, deployment of agricultural experts, and initiatives to support women and rural youth through employment and skill development in the agriculture sector.

questions.question: Which country officially prohibited individuals under the age of 16 from registering on social media platforms effective June 2, 2026?
questions.explanation: Malaysia introduced a regulation prohibiting individuals under 16 years of age from registering on social media platforms beginning June 2, 2026. The measure is aimed at enhancing online safety for minors and reducing exposure to harmful digital content. The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is responsible for overseeing the implementation of the rule. Social media companies are required to verify users’ ages using government-issued records, while existing users must complete age verification within a six-month transition period. Non-compliant platforms may face substantial financial penalties, reflecting Malaysia’s efforts to strengthen digital governance and child protection online.

questions.question: Who was elected President of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on June 2, 2026?
questions.explanation: Khalilur Rahman, the Foreign Minister of Bangladesh, was elected President of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on June 2, 2026. He secured 99 votes in the election, defeating Cypriot diplomat Andreas Kakouris, who received 91 votes. Rahman is set to assume office on September 8, 2026, and will succeed Annalena Baerbock. His presidency will be guided by the theme “Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations that Delivers for All.” He also became only the second Bangladeshi diplomat to hold this prestigious position after Humayun Rasheed Chowdhury.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the new Chief Justice of the Patna High Court on June 3, 2026?
questions.explanation: Justice Meenakshi Madan Rai was appointed as the Chief Justice of the Patna High Court on June 3, 2026, through a notification issued by the Central Government. The appointment was made by the President of India based on the recommendation of the Supreme Court Collegium. She succeeded Justice Sangam Kumar Sahoo, who retired on June 4, 2026. Before this elevation, she served as a Judge of the Sikkim High Court since April 2015 and held the position of Acting Chief Justice on multiple occasions. She also achieved the distinction of being the first woman from Sikkim to be elevated as a High Court Judge.

questions.question: Who assumed the appointment of Additional Director General (ADG) of the Military Nursing Service (MNS) on June 01, 2026?
questions.explanation: Maj Gen Rachel Thomas assumed the appointment of Additional Director General (ADG) of the Military Nursing Service (MNS) on June 01, 2026. She succeeded Maj Gen Lissamma PV, who retired from the post on May 31, 2026. Commissioned into the Military Nursing Service on June 01, 1988, she is an alumna of the College of Nursing at the Armed Forces Medical College (AFMC), Pune. During her distinguished career, she held various clinical and administrative appointments in military hospitals under the Northern and Eastern Commands. Her appointment reflects her extensive experience and leadership in military healthcare services.

questions.question: Which state hosted the celebration of the 37th Raising Day of Project UDAYAK on June 01, 2026, at Doomdooma?
questions.explanation: The Border Roads Organisation (BRO) celebrated the 37th Raising Day of Project UDAYAK on June 01, 2026, at Doomdooma, Assam. Established in 1987, Project UDAYAK is headquartered at Doomdooma and plays a crucial role in developing and maintaining strategic road infrastructure in the challenging border regions of Northeast India. The project manages more than 1,457 km of roads across Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, enhancing connectivity along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and the Indo–Myanmar border. Its efforts support border security, infrastructure growth, and improved accessibility in remote areas.

questions.question: Who became the only Indian player in the FIDE global top 10 rankings by achieving the World No. 8 position as of June 02, 2026?
questions.explanation: Arjun Erigaisi achieved a significant milestone on June 02, 2026, by securing the World No. 8 position in the latest FIDE rankings, making him the only Indian player in the global top 10 at that time. He gained 10 rating points during the assessment period and strengthened his standing through strong performances in major international tournaments. One of his notable achievements was finishing as the runner-up at the TePe Sigeman 2026 tournament, where he lost to Magnus Carlsen in a playoff. Erigaisi, who became India's 54th Grandmaster in 2018, continues to be one of the country's leading chess talents.

questions.question: At which institution was the Unilever Fragrance Hub inaugurated by Hindustan Unilever Limited (HUL) on June 02, 2026?
questions.explanation: Hindustan Unilever Limited (HUL) inaugurated the Unilever Fragrance Hub on June 02, 2026, at the IIT Bombay campus in Mumbai. The facility is the third global hub established under Unilever’s €100 million investment programme aimed at strengthening in-house fragrance development capabilities. The hub integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI), advanced scientific research, proprietary creation software, and real-time evaluation systems to accelerate fragrance innovation. By locating the facility within a premier academic institution, HUL seeks to enhance collaboration with researchers and experts in science, technology, and data analytics. The initiative is expected to support innovation across products such as shampoos, body washes, deodorants, and laundry detergents.

questions.question: In which state was the newly discovered lizard species Mesalina bishnoi found near Gajner in the Bikaner district?
questions.explanation: Scientists from the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI) and other researchers announced the discovery of a new lizard species, Mesalina bishnoi, on June 1, 2026. The species was discovered near Gajner in the Bikaner district of Rajasthan and represents the first confirmed record of the genus Mesalina in India. It was named in honour of the Bishnoi community for their long-standing commitment to wildlife and environmental conservation. The lizard inhabits the arid landscapes of the Thar region and is currently considered endemic to western India. Genetic studies confirmed its placement within the Mesalina watsonana species complex.

questions.question: Who took the oath as the 18th Chief Minister of Karnataka on June 3, 2026?
questions.explanation: DK Shivakumar was sworn in as the 18th Chief Minister of Karnataka on June 3, 2026, at a ceremony held in Bengaluru. His appointment marked the implementation of the Congress party's power-sharing arrangement in the state. He succeeded Siddaramaiah as Chief Minister, while senior Congress leader G Parameshwara took oath as Deputy Chief Minister. Along with them, 13 ministers were inducted into the new cabinet, representing a mix of experienced leaders and emerging political figures. The transition also saw Siddaramaiah being appointed as a member of the Congress Working Committee (CWC), the party’s highest decision-making body.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer (MD & CEO) of Protean eGov Technologies from June 1, 2026?
questions.explanation: Ajay Rajan assumed charge as the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Protean eGov Technologies on June 1, 2026. With more than three decades of experience in banking, fintech, digital transformation, and technology-driven innovation, he is expected to lead the company's next phase of growth. Before joining Protean, he held senior leadership roles at YES Bank, overseeing areas such as transaction banking, government business, multinational banking, and Digital Public Infrastructure initiatives. He also spent nearly two decades at Deutsche Bank, including serving as Global Head of Fintech. Under his leadership, Protean aims to expand its capabilities in AI-enabled solutions, Digital Public Infrastructure, and international markets.

questions.question: Which indigenous air-to-surface missile was successfully flight-tested by the DRDO and the Indian Air Force on June 02, 2026?
questions.explanation: RudraM-II is an indigenous air-to-surface missile that was successfully flight-tested by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and the Indian Air Force (IAF) on June 02, 2026. Developed under the leadership of the Research Centre Imarat (RCI), Hyderabad, the missile is designed for high-precision strikes against surface targets. The test was conducted at the Integrated Test Range (ITR) in Chandipur, Odisha, and validated the performance of all major subsystems. The missile accurately hit its intended target even under extreme release conditions, demonstrating its operational effectiveness and strengthening India’s indigenous missile capabilities.

questions.question: In which state was the Swachha App launched on May 30, 2026, to facilitate real-time reporting and management of urban waste?
questions.explanation: The Swachha App was launched on May 30, 2026, in West Bengal by Union Minister Manohar Lal to improve urban waste management through real-time reporting. The initiative was introduced in Kolkata and initially covers 10 municipalities across the state, including Asansol, Durgapur, Basirhat, Pujali, Tufanganj, Contai, Krishnanagar, Baidyabati, and Madhyamgram. The app allows citizens to upload geo-tagged photographs of garbage accumulation, automatically forwards complaints to municipal authorities, and provides a digital feedback system with before-and-after cleaning verification, supporting efficient and scientific waste management practices.

questions.question: How many States/UTs signed reform-linked Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with the Ministry of Jal Shakti on June 02, 2026, under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0?
questions.explanation: On June 02, 2026, the Ministry of Jal Shakti signed reform-linked MoUs with five States and Union Territories—Arunachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Tamil Nadu, Nagaland, and Puducherry—to strengthen sustainable rural water governance under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0. The agreements promote a Gram Panchayat-led and community-centred approach to rural water supply and long-term operation and maintenance. They also support initiatives such as Sujal Gaon ID creation, Village Action Plans, Jal Arpan Diwas, greywater management, rainwater harvesting, and community participation through Village Water & Sanitation Committees. The mission's implementation period has also been extended until December 2028 to achieve its remaining objectives.

questions.question: Which Indian city has been selected by the University of Liverpool for establishing its first campus in India after receiving approval from the Ministry of Education?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru, the capital city of Karnataka, has been chosen as the location for the University of Liverpool’s first campus in India. The university received official approval from the Ministry of Education under the framework of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, which encourages reputed foreign universities to establish campuses in India. The initiative is expected to enhance access to global-quality education, promote international research collaborations, improve student mobility, and strengthen academic competitiveness. The new campus also represents a significant step in deepening India–UK educational cooperation and advancing the internationalisation of India’s higher education system.

questions.question: India jointly launched the Critical Minerals Global Supply Chain Observatory (GSCO) with which country to strengthen critical mineral supply chains and resource security?
questions.explanation: India and the United Kingdom jointly launched the Critical Minerals Global Supply Chain Observatory (GSCO) to enhance cooperation in securing critical mineral supply chains. These minerals are essential for electric vehicle batteries, renewable energy systems, semiconductors, defence technologies, and advanced electronics. The initiative aims to provide real-time market intelligence, monitor supply chain risks, identify geopolitical vulnerabilities, and support evidence-based policymaking. Developed through collaboration between institutions such as IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, TEXMiN, and the University of Cambridge, the observatory aligns with India’s National Critical Mineral Mission and supports long-term resource security, clean energy transitions, and sustainable industrial growth.

questions.question: Which company unveiled the Fairwater AI Data Centre in Wisconsin featuring an innovative closed-loop cooling system to promote sustainable AI infrastructure?
questions.explanation: Microsoft unveiled the Fairwater AI Data Centre in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin, as part of its efforts to develop sustainable artificial intelligence infrastructure. The facility spans approximately 315 acres and represents an investment of about $7.3 billion. One of its most significant innovations is a closed-loop cooling system that recycles the same water continuously after an initial filling, greatly reducing freshwater consumption. The data centre also uses a two-storey vertical design to improve efficiency and reduce land requirements. Through this project, Microsoft aims to address environmental concerns associated with AI infrastructure while supporting the growing demand for advanced computing power.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as India’s next Ambassador to Saudi Arabia by the Government of India?
questions.explanation: Veteran Diplomat Vipul, a 1998-batch Indian Foreign Service (IFS) officer, has been appointed as India’s next Ambassador to Saudi Arabia. Before this appointment, he was serving as India’s Ambassador to Qatar and had previously held several important diplomatic positions, including Consul General of India in Dubai and Joint Secretary (Gulf) in the Ministry of External Affairs. With nearly three decades of diplomatic experience and deep expertise in Gulf affairs, Vipul is expected to play a significant role in strengthening India’s relations with Saudi Arabia in areas such as energy, trade, investment, defence cooperation, and regional security.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the new Chairperson of the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) amid the ongoing On-Screen Marking (OSM) controversy?
questions.explanation: Lokhande Prashant Sitaram, a 2001-batch AGMUT cadre IAS officer, has been appointed as the new Chairperson of the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE). Prior to this appointment, he served as Additional Secretary in the Department of Home under the Ministry of Home Affairs. His appointment comes at a significant time when CBSE’s On-Screen Marking (OSM) system is facing scrutiny over complaints related to evaluation discrepancies, technical issues, and delays in verification. The leadership change is aimed at strengthening the administration of CBSE, one of the largest education boards in the world, which conducts Class 10 and Class 12 board examinations.

questions.question: Which country's Acting President, Delcy Rodríguez, visited India from June 3–7, 2026, to strengthen cooperation in energy, trade, technology, and investment?
questions.explanation: Delcy Rodríguez, the Acting President of Venezuela, visited India from June 3 to June 7, 2026, as part of an official diplomatic engagement aimed at strengthening bilateral relations. The visit focused on key sectors such as energy, trade, technology, investment, scientific research, and infrastructure. She was accompanied by a high-level delegation that included several cabinet ministers. During the visit, discussions with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and other Indian leaders were expected to cover bilateral cooperation, global energy markets, trade opportunities, South-South cooperation, and other issues of mutual interest.

questions.question: Which country became the latest nation where Indian travellers can use UPI-enabled applications for seamless QR-code-based payments through a partnership between NPCI International and ACLEDA Bank?
questions.explanation: Cambodia has become the latest country to accept India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) through a partnership between NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL) and ACLEDA Bank Plc. This initiative allows Indian travellers to make secure and instant QR-code-based payments using their existing UPI applications at over 4.5 million merchant locations across Cambodia. The integration uses Cambodia’s KHQR network, powered by the Bakong digital payment system, making transactions more convenient for tourists and business travellers. The partnership also aims to establish a two-way payment corridor in the future, enabling Cambodian users to make payments in India through their domestic digital payment platforms.

questions.question: Which city hosted the First World Yogasana Championship 2026 inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi?
questions.explanation: Ahmedabad hosted the First World Yogasana Championship 2026, a landmark event inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The championship brought together athletes from various countries and marked a significant step toward establishing Yogasana as a globally recognised competitive sport. Ahmedabad was chosen as the host city due to its cultural and historical importance as India’s first UNESCO World Heritage City. The event was organised ahead of International Yoga Day 2026 and aimed to promote yoga beyond wellness by showcasing its potential as a competitive discipline. It also highlighted India’s efforts to popularise yoga on the international stage and encourage global participation in Yogasana.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as India’s next Executive Director at the World Bank by the Government of India?
questions.explanation: Neelkanth Mishra, a distinguished economist and policy expert, has been appointed as India’s next Executive Director at the World Bank. He will represent the South Asian constituency comprising India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, and Sri Lanka for a three-year term. Before this appointment, he served as Chief Economist at Axis Bank and held several important positions, including membership in the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, UIDAI, and TRAI. With extensive experience in economic research, financial markets, and public policy, Mishra is expected to strengthen India’s voice in international economic decision-making and contribute significantly to discussions at the World Bank.

Celebrated annually, it serves as the world's largest platform for environmental awareness and action. The 2026 theme, “Inspired by Nature: For Climate. For Our Future.”, emphasises climate action, ecosystem restoration, and sustainable living. Hosted by Azerbaijan, the event brings together governments, organisations, businesses, and citizens to address pressing environmental challenges such as climate change, biodiversity loss, pollution, and deforestation while encouraging collective responsibility for protecting the planet.

questions.explanation: Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary, popularly known as Surha Tal, became India’s 100th Ramsar Site on World Environment Day 2026. Located in the Ballia district of Uttar Pradesh, the sanctuary is an ecologically significant wetland that supports a wide variety of migratory and resident bird species. Its recognition under the Ramsar Convention highlights its international importance for biodiversity conservation and sustainable wetland management. The sanctuary contributes to maintaining ecological balance by supporting aquatic life, regulating water systems, and providing breeding and feeding habitats for birds. This achievement also reflects India’s growing commitment to environmental conservation and wetland protection.

questions.question: From which date will the FSSAI's standardised vegan logo become mandatory on approved vegan food products in India?
questions.explanation: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has introduced a standardised vegan logo to help consumers easily identify certified vegan food products. The logo will become mandatory on all approved vegan food packages from July 1, 2027. This initiative aims to improve transparency, prevent misleading claims, and support informed purchasing decisions. The logo features a green square-framed design with a stylized “V” and a sprouting leaf, symbolising plant-based and sustainable food choices. Food businesses have been given sufficient time to update their packaging and comply with the new regulations before the implementation deadline.

questions.question: Which bank won the Gold Award at the Finacle Innovation Awards 2026 in the category of “Modern Technologies-led Innovation – Data Insights & Analytics Platform”?
questions.explanation: Jammu & Kashmir Bank won the Gold Award at the Finacle Innovation Awards 2026 for its advanced Data Insights and Analytics Platform. The award recognised the bank’s successful use of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), business intelligence, and advanced analytics to improve operational efficiency and decision-making. The platform supports customer analytics, risk management, business forecasting, customer retention, and performance monitoring. Presented during the Finacle India Connect 2026 event in Mumbai, the recognition highlights J&K Bank’s commitment to technology-driven innovation and places it among leading financial institutions adopting emerging technologies for digital transformation and enhanced customer service.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian player to win the prestigious Norway Chess title in 2026?
questions.explanation: R Praggnanandhaa created history by becoming the first Indian to win the Norway Chess tournament, one of the most prestigious events in world chess. The 20-year-old Grandmaster secured the title after defeating Germany’s Vincent Keymer in the final round and finishing with 18 points. His remarkable campaign included four consecutive victories in the later stages of the tournament and two classical wins against former World Champion Magnus Carlsen. This achievement is particularly significant because even renowned Indian players such as Viswanathan Anand and D Gukesh had never won the Norway Chess title, making Praggnanandhaa’s success a landmark moment for Indian chess.

questions.question: Which state became the 33rd Legislature in India to adopt the National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA) platform for digital legislative governance after signing an MoU in June 2026?
questions.explanation: West Bengal became the 33rd Legislature in India to adopt the National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA) after signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on 4 June 2026. NeVA is a Mission Mode Project of the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs aimed at digitising and modernising legislative functioning through a common digital platform. The initiative promotes paperless governance, transparency, efficiency, accessibility, and better record management. By joining NeVA, West Bengal contributed to the national vision of “One Nation – One Application,” which seeks to create a unified digital ecosystem for legislative institutions across the country.

questions.question: Which platform earned a Guinness World Records title for the highest number of users completing an online quiz within one week, with 390,812 verified participants?
questions.explanation: MY Bharat, operating under the Department of Youth Affairs, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, earned a Guinness World Records title for the “Most Users to Take an Online Quiz in One Week.” The achievement was accomplished through the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders’ Dialogue (VBYLD) Quiz, which engaged youth from across India in the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047. During the assessment period from 25 October to 31 October 2025, over 8.39 lakh quiz participations were recorded, and after extensive verification and audits, 390,812 eligible participants were certified. The record highlights India’s growing digital youth engagement and commitment to nation-building initiatives.

questions.question: Who has assumed charge as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the IndiaAI Mission while continuing as CEO of UIDAI?
questions.explanation: Saurabh Vijay, an IAS officer of the 1998 Maharashtra cadre and the CEO of the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), has taken charge as the CEO of the IndiaAI Mission. His appointment comes at a crucial time as India expands its artificial intelligence ecosystem through the ₹10,372 crore IndiaAI Mission. The initiative focuses on developing indigenous AI models, strengthening AI infrastructure, supporting startups and researchers, creating AI-ready datasets, and promoting responsible AI adoption. With extensive experience in public administration, finance, and governance, Saurabh Vijay is expected to play a key role in advancing India’s ambitions to become a global leader in artificial intelligence.

questions.question: What percentage of ethanol is contained in the newly launched E85 fuel introduced by India to reduce oil imports and emissions?
questions.explanation: E85 fuel is a high-ethanol blend consisting of approximately 85% ethanol and 15% petrol. Introduced as part of India's efforts to enhance energy security and promote sustainable transportation, the fuel is designed for use in Flex-Fuel Vehicles (FFVs). E85 aims to reduce dependence on imported crude oil, lower greenhouse gas emissions, and support domestic ethanol production. Since ethanol is produced from agricultural feedstocks such as sugarcane, maize, rice, and biomass resources, the initiative is also expected to create additional income opportunities for farmers and contribute to rural economic development while advancing India's clean energy goals.

questions.question: Which state's Sangeet Natak Akademi organised the SNA Samman Ceremony 2026, where 51 artistes were honoured for their contributions to music, dance, theatre, and folk arts?
questions.explanation: The SNA Samman Ceremony 2026 was organised by the Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi in Lucknow to recognise 51 distinguished artistes for their exceptional contributions to classical music, folk music, dance, theatre, and traditional folk arts. The awards were presented for achievements during the years 2021 to 2024 and celebrated artists who have dedicated their lives to preserving and promoting India’s cultural heritage. The event also highlighted the importance of safeguarding traditional art forms while adapting them to modern platforms, ensuring that India's rich artistic legacy continues to inspire future generations.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the next Vice Chief of the Air Staff (VCAS) of the Indian Air Force and is scheduled to assume office on July 1, 2026?
options: Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh
questions.explanation: Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit has been appointed as the next Vice Chief of the Air Staff of the Indian Air Force. Commissioned into the fighter stream in 1986, he is a highly experienced fighter pilot, experimental test pilot, and qualified flying instructor with more than 3,300 flying hours on over 20 aircraft types. He currently serves as the Chief of Integrated Defence Staff (CISC) and has contributed significantly to indigenous defence projects, military reforms, and joint operational planning. His extensive operational, leadership, and modernisation experience is expected to strengthen the Indian Air Force’s future capabilities and strategic preparedness.

questions.question: In which city were 18 Namo Oxygen Parks inaugurated under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign on World Environment Day 2026?
questions.explanation: Eighteen Namo Oxygen Parks were inaugurated across New Delhi on World Environment Day 2026 under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign. The initiative was launched by Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav and Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta to improve urban air quality, increase green cover, enhance biodiversity, and provide recreational green spaces for citizens. The parks are designed to function as urban green lungs and support environmental sustainability. Alongside this initiative, the Delhi Government announced a target of planting 15 lakh trees and released important environmental planning documents to strengthen conservation and ecological governance in the national capital.

questions.question: In which city was India’s seventh Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) inaugurated on 5 June 2026?
questions.explanation: India’s seventh Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) was inaugurated in Jammu by Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh on 5 June 2026. The centre has been established to provide advanced weather forecasting, climate monitoring, and disaster early-warning services for Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, and Himachal Pradesh. It offers district-level forecasts, flash-flood warnings, avalanche alerts, cloudburst notifications, and mountain weather advisories. The facility is expected to improve disaster preparedness and support sectors such as agriculture, tourism, transport, hydropower, and defence operations. The inauguration marks a significant step in strengthening meteorological infrastructure and weather forecasting capabilities in India’s Himalayan region.

questions.question: What percentage stake in Lenskart was sold by SoftBank for ₹2,873.3 crore through block deals in June 2026?
questions.explanation: SoftBank sold a 3.25% stake in Lenskart through block deals valued at ₹2,873.3 crore. The transaction was carried out by SVF II Lightbulb (Cayman), an affiliate of SoftBank, involving the sale of 5.65 crore shares at ₹508.55 per share. Following the sale, SoftBank's ownership in Lenskart decreased from 13.13% to 9.88%. The deal generated an impressive seven-fold return on SoftBank's original investment made in 2021. Major institutional investors, including Goldman Sachs Bank Europe and Societe Generale-ODI, participated in the purchase, reflecting strong confidence in Lenskart's growth prospects and business performance.

questions.explanation: Saurabh Vijay, a 1998-batch IAS officer of the Maharashtra cadre and the then CEO of UIDAI, officially took charge as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the IndiaAI Mission on June 5, 2026. The IndiaAI Mission, launched in March 2024 with a financial outlay of ₹10,372 crore, aims to strengthen India’s artificial intelligence ecosystem and promote sovereign AI capabilities using Indian datasets. The mission operates under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). His appointment is expected to support the mission’s objective of enhancing India’s competitiveness in the field of Generative AI and emerging technologies.

questions.question: Who received the Birrer-Brookes Award and the General Douglas MacArthur Military Leadership Writing Award at the US Army Command and General Staff College graduation ceremony in 2026?
options: Lt. Col. Taleh S F H H Alrashid
questions.explanation: Major Prabhat Mishra of the Indian Army earned two prestigious academic honours during the graduation ceremony of the US Army Command and General Staff College (CGSC) held at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas. He received the Birrer-Brookes Award for producing the Outstanding Master of Military Arts and Science Thesis and the General Douglas MacArthur Military Leadership Writing Award for excellence in military leadership writing. These recognitions highlight his academic achievement and leadership capabilities. The CGSC is a renowned institution that prepares mid-career military officers for senior leadership and staff responsibilities through advanced military education and training.

questions.question: Which state launched a comprehensive 100-day action plan on June 6, 2026, to mitigate human-wildlife conflict through technological interventions and infrastructure expansion?
questions.explanation: Kerala launched a comprehensive 100-day action plan to address the growing challenge of human-animal conflict. The initiative includes the construction of new solar fencing, deployment of drone squads, AI-enabled warning systems, and the establishment of additional Rapid Response Teams. The plan also introduces reforms such as enhanced compensation for victims and faster claim processing through a single-window system. Wildlife management measures include monitoring animal movement, controlling invasive species, and conducting studies on forest carrying capacity. These steps aim to improve public safety, protect wildlife habitats, and create a more effective system for managing interactions between humans and wild animals.

questions.question: Which company signed a Cloud Service Agreement with Google worth $920 million per month to provide computing capacity for its AI initiatives?
questions.explanation: Google entered into a major Cloud Service Agreement with SpaceX on June 5, 2026, to obtain computing capacity valued at $920 million per month. The contract is scheduled to run from October 2026 to June 2029 and includes access to approximately 110,000 NVIDIA GPUs, CPUs, and memory components. This infrastructure is intended to support Google's AI agent platform, Gemini Enterprise, by providing critical computing resources. The agreement highlights the growing demand for large-scale AI computing infrastructure and contributes significantly to SpaceX’s revenue from cloud and compute services, alongside other major technology partnerships.

questions.question: By which year does India aim to increase its seafood exports to $30 billion?
questions.explanation: India has set an ambitious target of increasing its seafood exports to $30 billion by the year 2031. This goal was highlighted during a national workshop on seafood exports inaugurated by Union Minister Piyush Goyal in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh. The target represents a significant increase from the current export value of approximately $8.5 billion. To achieve this objective, the government is focusing on expanding market access through free trade agreements, improving fisheries infrastructure, and supporting exporters. Andhra Pradesh, India's leading seafood-exporting state, is expected to play a crucial role in helping the country reach this milestone.

questions.question: Where was the 29th edition of the India-US Army-to-Army Staff Talks (AAST) held on June 06, 2026?
questions.explanation: The 29th edition of the India-US Army-to-Army Staff Talks (AAST) was conducted in Hawaii on June 06, 2026, as part of ongoing efforts to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between the two countries. The discussions focused on enhancing military interoperability, expanding professional exchanges, and reinforcing shared security interests in the Indo-Pacific region. The meeting was co-chaired by senior military officials from both nations, reflecting the growing strategic partnership between India and the United States. Hawaii also hosts the headquarters of the US Army Pacific (USARPAC), making it an important centre for military coordination and regional security initiatives.

questions.question: Which company signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Tamil Nadu government for an investment of ₹18,600 crore in data centres, electronics, and shipbuilding projects?
questions.explanation: Larsen & Toubro (L&T) signed an MoU with the Tamil Nadu government on June 4, 2026, committing an investment of ₹18,600 crore across multiple sectors. The investment includes ₹15,000 crore for data centre expansion in Kancheepuram, ₹2,500 crore for an electronics manufacturing facility in Coimbatore, and ₹1,100 crore for shipbuilding expansion at the Kattupalli complex in Tiruvallur. These projects are expected to generate around 8,200 jobs and support sectors such as cloud computing, artificial intelligence, electronics manufacturing, and maritime infrastructure. The initiative also aligns with Tamil Nadu’s long-term objective of becoming a $1.5 trillion economy by 2036.

questions.question: Which state's Modernisation of Command Area Development and Water Management (M-CAD) initiative was commended by the Union Ministry of Jal Shakti and recommended as a model for other States and Union Territories?
questions.explanation: Chhattisgarh's Modernisation of Command Area Development and Water Management (M-CAD) initiative received recognition from the Union Ministry of Jal Shakti for its effective approach to improving irrigation efficiency and water resource management. The programme was implemented using the state's own resources and focuses on enhancing water-use capacity, adopting scientific methods of water management, and expanding irrigation coverage. Due to its success, the Ministry recommended that all States and Union Territories consider adopting similar practices. The initiative highlights the importance of efficient water utilisation in agriculture and serves as a model for sustainable irrigation development across India.
