questions.question: Which state's bird checklist crossed the 500-species mark with the publication of its Bird Checklist 8.0 in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Goa achieved a significant biodiversity milestone with the publication of the Goa Bird Checklist 8.0, which recorded a total of 502 bird species in the state. Despite covering only 3,702 square kilometres, Goa hosts nearly 40% of India's approximately 1,300 bird species. The latest checklist added five new species, including the Wedge-tailed Shearwater and the Black-bellied Storm-petrel. Maintained by the Goa Bird Conservation Network and the Arannya Environment Research Organisation, the checklist serves as an important scientific resource for monitoring bird populations, ecological changes, and conservation efforts across the state.

questions.question: Which country launched the Storm Fighter program to develop autonomous Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) for a sixth-generation air force?
questions.explanation: The United Kingdom launched the Storm Fighter program on July 17, 2026, through the Royal Air Force (RAF) to develop autonomous Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA). The initiative aims to establish Europe's first sixth-generation air force by integrating "loyal wingman" drones with crewed fighter aircraft such as the Typhoon, F-35B Lightning II, and the future Tempest fighter. Backed by £5 billion in funding over four years, the program seeks to enhance combat capability, improve pilot safety, and strengthen the UK's position in next-generation military aviation and defence technology.

questions.question: How many improved crop varieties were launched by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) during its 98th Foundation Day celebrations in July 2026?
questions.explanation: The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) celebrated its 98th Foundation Day in New Delhi by launching 43 improved crop varieties aimed at enhancing agricultural productivity and resilience. Along with these, ICAR introduced 17 advanced agricultural technologies and released 14 research publications. Key innovations included climate-resilient Basmati rice varieties, India's first indigenous African Swine Fever vaccine, the Digital Swine Disease Atlas, and an affordable cassava harvester. The organisation also signed 72 Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with 51 industry partners to promote technology commercialisation and support the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 through science-driven agricultural development.

questions.question: What is the name of the world's first once-daily oral PCSK9 inhibitor approved by the US FDA for adults with high cholesterol?
questions.explanation: Lipfendra (enlicitide) became the world's first once-daily oral PCSK9 inhibitor after receiving approval from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on July 16, 2026. Developed by Merck, the medicine works by blocking the PCSK9 protein, allowing more LDL receptors in the liver to remove bad cholesterol from the bloodstream. Clinical trials showed that it reduced LDL cholesterol levels by 56% to 60%. It is intended for adults with hypercholesterolemia, including familial hypercholesterolemia, and is used alongside statins and a healthy diet to achieve better cholesterol control.

questions.question: Which city did the trophy tour for the 135th IndianOil Durand Cup reach in July 2026?
questions.explanation: The trophy tour for the 135th IndianOil Durand Cup reached Guwahati on July 17, 2026, ahead of the tournament scheduled from July 25 to August 23, 2026. During the two-day visit, the prestigious Durand Cup, President’s Cup, and Simla Trophy were displayed at prominent locations, including the Assam Legislative Assembly, IIT Guwahati, and the Bir Lachit Borphukan Statue. Guwahati is one of the five host cities for the tournament and will stage six Group F matches featuring clubs such as defending champions NorthEast United FC, Karbi Anglong Morning Star FC, and Bodoland FC.

questions.question: In which city was the White Rabbit Technology-based Indian Standard Time (IST) Distribution Demonstration Network inaugurated in July, 2026?
questions.explanation: The White Rabbit Technology-based Indian Standard Time (IST) Distribution Demonstration Network was inaugurated in Bengaluru at the Regional Reference Standards Laboratory (RRSL) in Jakkur. The initiative, launched under the vision of "One Nation, One Time," aims to establish a uniform and highly precise time synchronisation system across India. Implemented through the collaboration of the National Physical Laboratory (NPL), ISRO, BSNL, and SEBI, the network uses White Rabbit Technology to achieve sub-nanosecond accuracy. It is expected to strengthen digital infrastructure, financial systems, telecommunications, power grids, and national security while reducing dependence on foreign GPS-based timing sources.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian men's cricketer to score an ODI century at Lord's during the 2026 match against England?
questions.explanation: Rohit Sharma created history by becoming the first Indian men's cricketer to score an ODI century at Lord's, achieving the milestone against England on July 19, 2026. His remarkable innings not only guided India's run chase but also silenced speculation regarding his retirement from white-ball cricket. At 39 years and 80 days, Rohit became the oldest Indian to score an international century across all formats, surpassing Sachin Tendulkar's previous record. He also set several other milestones, including becoming the visiting batter with the most ODI centuries in a single country and surpassing Tendulkar's tally of international centuries as India's designated opening batter.

questions.question: Which stock exchange launched Electronic Gold Receipts (EGRs) backed by SEBI-regulated vault managers to modernise India's bullion market?
questions.explanation: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) launched Electronic Gold Receipts (EGRs) to provide investors with a transparent, secure, and efficient way to invest in gold without physically holding it. Each EGR represents ownership of a specified quantity of physical gold stored in SEBI-regulated vaults and is held in dematerialised form through a demat account. Investors can buy, sell, and redeem EGRs on the exchange while benefiting from standardised quality, transparent price discovery, enhanced liquidity, and secure storage. The initiative is expected to strengthen India's organised gold market, reduce dependence on informal trading channels, and encourage greater participation from institutional and retail investors.

questions.question: Who became the all-time leading scorer in FIFA World Cup history in July, 2026?
questions.explanation: Kylian Mbappe became the all-time leading scorer in FIFA World Cup history on July 18, 2026, during the third-place playoff against England. The French striker reached a remarkable total of 22 World Cup goals, surpassing Lionel Messi's previous record of 21 goals. Mbappe also finished the 2026 FIFA World Cup as the tournament's top scorer with 10 goals, leading the Golden Boot standings. He achieved the historic milestone in just 22 World Cup appearances, having scored four goals in 2018, eight in 2022, and ten in 2026. At only 27 years of age, he is expected to have further opportunities to extend his record in future World Cups.

questions.question: Who assumed charge as the Director (Commercial) of NMDC Limited in July, 2026?
questions.explanation: Vivek Nishant Nath assumed charge as the Director (Commercial) of NMDC Limited on July 18, 2026. He brings nearly fifteen years of experience with NMDC, having served in various commercial roles since 1992, along with leadership experience as Chief General Manager at Odisha Mining Corporation Limited. He has also worked with Essar Steel and ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India, strengthening his expertise in the mining and steel sectors. NMDC Limited, established in 1958, is India's largest iron ore producer and a Navratna Public Sector Enterprise headquartered in Hyderabad, Telangana. It functions under the administrative control of the Ministry of Steel and plays a key role in India's mineral sector.

questions.question: Which Union Territory is home to Puga Valley, where India's first and deepest geothermal wells were commissioned in July 2026?
questions.explanation: India's first and deepest geothermal wells were commissioned at Puga Valley in Ladakh on July 17, 2026, by Lieutenant Governor VK Saxena. Developed by the ONGC Energy Centre at an altitude of over 14,000 feet, the project marks a significant milestone in India's renewable energy sector. Both wells were drilled to a depth of 1,000 meters, with temperatures reaching 135°C at around 400 meters below the surface. The geothermal resource will support India's first 1 MW demonstration-scale geothermal power project. Located in the Changthang region, Puga Valley is renowned for its high-temperature hot springs and is considered India's most promising geothermal field.

questions.question: Which country is hosting the multinational Exercise Pitch Black 2026, in which the Indian Air Force is participating?
questions.explanation: Exercise Pitch Black 2026 is being hosted in Australia at the Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) Base Darwin from 20 July to 7 August 2026. It is the Royal Australian Air Force's premier biennial multinational air combat exercise, focusing on advanced air warfare, including night flying and Large Force Employment operations. The Indian Air Force is participating with Rafale fighter aircraft, C-17 Globemaster-III strategic airlifters, and IL-78 air-to-air refuelling aircraft, along with a contingent of pilots, engineers, technicians, and controllers. India's continued participation reflects its commitment to enhancing interoperability, operational readiness, and defence cooperation with friendly nations.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian player to win a BWF Super 750 title by clinching the Japan Open 2026?
questions.explanation: PV Sindhu created history by winning the BWF Japan Open 2026, becoming the first Indian badminton player to capture a BWF Super 750 title. She defeated world No. 3 Akane Yamaguchi in straight games, 21-17, 21-17, displaying remarkable composure, tactical brilliance, and consistency throughout the final. The victory marked Sindhu's first major title since the 2019 BWF World Championships and completed a successful comeback after recovering from injury and facing stiff competition from younger players. The triumph also elevated her back among the world's top-ranked players ahead of the BWF World Championships, reaffirming her status as one of India's greatest badminton stars.

questions.question: Who became the first footballer to start three FIFA World Cup finals after appearing in the 2026 final against Spain?
questions.explanation: Lionel Messi created history by becoming the first footballer to start three FIFA World Cup finals. He achieved this milestone during the 2026 FIFA World Cup final against Spain at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. His previous final appearances came in 2014, when Argentina finished runners-up to Germany, and in 2022, when he captained Argentina to the World Cup title against France. At 39 years of age, Messi also became the oldest outfield player to appear in three World Cup finals. Although Argentina lost the 2026 final 1–0 after extra time, Messi delivered an outstanding tournament, finishing with eight goals and four assists while once again demonstrating exceptional leadership and consistency.

questions.question: Which organisation launched the Mascot Design Contest on the MyGov platform in July 2026?
questions.explanation: India Post, operating under the Department of Posts in the Ministry of Communications, launched the Mascot Design Contest on the MyGov platform on 15 July 2026. The initiative aims to create a unique brand ambassador representing the organisation's core values of trust, reliability, inclusivity, service, and digital innovation. The contest is open to all Indian citizens, including artists, students, and creative professionals, and offers total prize money of ₹2 lakh across mascot design and naming categories. Established on 1 October 1854, India Post manages the world's largest postal network and continues to modernise its services while preserving its legacy of nationwide connectivity.

questions.question: Which country won the FIFA World Cup 2026 by defeating Argentina 1–0 in the final after extra time?
questions.explanation: Spain won the FIFA World Cup 2026 after defeating Argentina 1–0 in extra time in the final held at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Substitute Ferran Torres scored the decisive goal in the 106th minute, securing Spain's second men's FIFA World Cup title after their first triumph in 2010. Spain also created history by becoming the first nation to hold both the men's and women's FIFA World Cup titles simultaneously. Under coach Luis de la Fuente, the team remained unbeaten throughout the tournament and set a new defensive record by conceding only one goal during the entire competition.

questions.question: What was the year-on-year growth rate of India's Index of Core Industries (ICI) in June 2026 under the revised 2022-23 base year series?
questions.explanation: India's Index of Core Industries (ICI) recorded a year-on-year growth of 5% in June 2026, according to the provisional estimates released by the Office of Economic Adviser under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT). The data was published under the revised 2022-23 base year series, which introduced methodological improvements such as the inclusion of Iron Ore as the ninth core industry. Growth was mainly driven by strong performance in Electricity, Iron Ore, Cement, Coal, and Steel, reflecting improved industrial activity and strengthening momentum in infrastructure-related sectors during the first quarter of FY 2026-27.

questions.question: In which state is the Hollongapar Gibbon Wildlife Sanctuary, where 281 butterfly species were documented over a 12-year survey, located?
questions.explanation: Assam is home to the Hollongapar Gibbon Wildlife Sanctuary, where a 12-year biodiversity survey conducted between 2012 and 2024 documented 281 butterfly species. The findings were published in the book Butterflies of Gibbon Wildlife Sanctuary, released on 20 July 2026. Located in Jorhat district, the 20.98 sq km sanctuary is the only protected area in India named after the Hoolock Gibbon, the country's only ape. The sanctuary, designated in 1997, is known for its evergreen forest canopy and rich biodiversity, making it an important centre for wildlife conservation and ecological research.

questions.question: With which state government did Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) sign an MoU for the development and implementation of infrastructure projects in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Government of Goa on 17 July 2026 to develop and implement infrastructure projects in the state. Under the agreement, RVNL will serve as the primary executing agency for identified projects, while both parties will jointly identify and undertake infrastructure initiatives based on mutually agreed terms. In addition to this partnership, RVNL also secured a ₹967.93 crore contract from East Coast Railway for the construction of a railway bridge. Established in 2003, RVNL functions under the Ministry of Railways and is headquartered in New Delhi.

questions.question: Who became the new Prime Minister of the United Kingdom after meeting King Charles III in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Andy Burnham became the new Prime Minister of the United Kingdom after being appointed by King Charles III on 20 July 2026 following the resignation of Keir Starmer. As per the UK's constitutional process, the monarch appoints the politician who is most likely to command the confidence of the House of Commons. After meeting King Charles III at Buckingham Palace, Burnham formally assumed office and delivered his inaugural speech outside 10 Downing Street. In his address, he pledged to restore political and economic stability, rebuild public trust in government, and introduce a decade-long national plan to address the country's key social and economic challenges.

questions.question: What was the credit growth recorded by Indian scheduled commercial banks for the fortnight ended June 30, 2026, according to SBI Research?
questions.explanation: According to SBI Research, Indian scheduled commercial banks recorded a credit growth of 18.6% for the fortnight ended June 30, 2026, while deposit growth stood at 13.3%. This widened the gap between credit and deposit growth to 5.3%. The report highlighted that lending activity was driven by increased credit flow to agriculture, industry, and services, with working capital loans growing faster than term loans. It also noted that Indian banks are in a strong financial position due to healthy capital buffers and low non-performing assets, while the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) continues to support credit expansion across productive sectors.

questions.question: What institutional delivery rate was achieved by Sukma district under the Mukhyamantri Swasth Bastar Abhiyan?
questions.explanation: Sukma district in Chhattisgarh achieved an impressive 98.6% institutional delivery rate under the Mukhyamantri Swasth Bastar Abhiyan, marking a significant improvement from the previous 96–97% level. The campaign, launched on 14 April 2026, focused on strengthening maternal and child healthcare in remote and Left Wing Extremism-affected areas of the Bastar region. Along with increasing institutional deliveries, the initiative helped reduce maternal deaths to single digits, expanded door-to-door screening for diseases such as anaemia and sickle cell disease, ensured timely ambulance services, and improved access to essential medical care for pregnant women and vulnerable communities.

questions.question: Which state approved a financial outlay of ₹776.13 crore to upgrade and expand 73 health institutions in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh approved a financial outlay of ₹776.13 crore on 21 July 2026 to strengthen healthcare infrastructure by upgrading and expanding 73 health institutions across the state. The plan includes converting sub-health centres into Primary Health Centres, expanding PHCs into Community Health Centres, upgrading CHCs into 50-bed civil hospitals, and developing selected institutions into 100-bed hospitals. The Cabinet also approved ₹122.83 crore annually for operation and maintenance, created 1,600 regular posts along with contractual and outsourced positions, and focused on improving healthcare access and bed capacity in rural and semi-urban areas.

questions.question: Which pharmaceutical company developed QDENGA, India's first approved dengue vaccine?
questions.explanation: QDENGA, developed by Takeda, became India's first approved dengue vaccine after receiving authorisation from the Drug Controller General of India (DCGI). The live attenuated vaccine provides protection against all four dengue virus serotypes (DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, and DENV-4) and is approved for individuals aged 4 to 60 years without requiring pre-vaccination screening. Administered in two doses, the vaccine demonstrated high efficacy in global clinical trials involving over 28,000 participants. It has already been approved in 43 countries, prequalified by the World Health Organisation (WHO), and is expected to significantly strengthen India's efforts to prevent dengue infections and related hospitalisations.

questions.question: In which city was the Parivartan Scheme approved to replace old commercial vehicles with BS-VI and electric vehicles?
questions.explanation: The Parivartan Scheme was approved by the Delhi Government to promote cleaner transportation and reduce vehicular pollution in the National Capital Region (NCR). The scheme encourages owners of old BS-IV and older commercial vehicles to replace them with BS-VI-compliant or electric vehicles through incentives such as tax exemptions, registration fee waivers, interest subsidies, and manufacturer discounts. It covers goods vehicles and buses and is expected to benefit around 2.7 lakh operators in Delhi-NCR. The initiative also supports the objectives of the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy 2026 and aims to accelerate the transition toward sustainable and environmentally friendly mobility.

questions.question: Which dairy cooperative is establishing the world's largest curd manufacturing plant in West Bengal?
questions.explanation: Amul is establishing the world's largest curd manufacturing plant at the Howrah Food Park in West Bengal under the Amul Bengal Dairy Project. The project involves an investment of ₹700 crore and will have a final milk processing capacity of 30 lakh litres per day, along with a daily curd and cultured dairy production capacity of 10 lakh kilograms. The initiative is expected to directly benefit around 1.20 lakh dairy farmers and promote the White Revolution 2.0. It also includes modern infrastructure, cooperative development initiatives, and advanced livestock breeding facilities to strengthen the dairy sector in the state.

questions.question: On which date is National Flag Day observed every year in India?
questions.explanation: National Flag Day is observed every year on July 22 to commemorate the adoption of the Indian National Flag by the Constituent Assembly on July 22, 1947. The day recognises the Tiranga as a symbol of India's independence, unity, sovereignty, and constitutional values. It also pays tribute to the sacrifices of freedom fighters who carried the national flag during the freedom struggle. Educational institutions and organisations conduct awareness programs to promote respect for the Tiranga and educate citizens about its history, symbolism, the Ashoka Chakra, and the provisions of the Flag Code of India governing its proper use and display.

questions.question: Which country partnered with Arunachal Pradesh to establish India's first river kinetic energy demonstration plant?
questions.explanation: Norway partnered with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh to establish India's first 500-kW River Kinetic Energy Demonstration Project under the India–Norway Green Partnership. The Memorandum of Understanding was signed on July 14, 2026, between the Centre for Earth Sciences & Himalayan Studies (CES&HS) and Norway's Tidal Sail AS. The project is supported by India's Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) and Innovation Norway. It aims to harness the kinetic energy of Himalayan rivers to generate clean electricity, strengthen renewable energy research, and promote sustainable infrastructure through international collaboration.

questions.question: Which city hosted the 8th Global Real Estate Brand Awards in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru hosted the 8th Global Real Estate Brand Awards on July 21, 2026. The event recognised excellence, innovation, and leadership in the global real estate sector, bringing together leading developers, industry experts, and brand leaders. It provided a platform to celebrate outstanding achievements while encouraging discussions on the future growth of the property market. The awards also highlighted the importance of innovation in shaping the real estate industry. In India, the sector is regulated by the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA), which promotes transparency, accountability, and consumer protection.

questions.question: Which country signed a technical cooperation agreement with India's Ministry of Coal to promote scientific mine closure on July 22, 2026?
questions.explanation: Germany signed a technical cooperation agreement with India's Ministry of Coal through the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) on July 22, 2026, in New Delhi. The agreement focuses on scientific mine closure, technical cooperation for mines nearing closure, and the exchange of international best practices. During the event, the Ministry also released the AAROH report documenting the scientific closure of 42 coal mines, inaugurated Coal NEER plants for sustainable drinking water, and introduced frameworks such as RECLAIM, L.I.V.E.S., and SUVIKALP to support sustainable mine closure, land repurposing, and community engagement.

questions.question: Which state was the focus of the Indian Army's Operation Jal Rahat launched for flood rescue and relief operations in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Assam was the focus of Operation Jal Rahat, launched by the Indian Army on July 21, 2026, to carry out large-scale rescue and relief operations in flood-affected areas. The mission covered seven affected districts, including Charaideo, Sivasagar, and Jorhat, with support from the Assam Rifles and coordination from the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA). More than 57,100 people were affected by the floods, with Charaideo being the worst-hit district. The Indian Air Force was also placed on standby to provide aerial assistance if the flood situation worsened.

questions.question: On which date is World Brain Day observed every year?
questions.explanation: World Brain Day is observed every year on July 22 to raise awareness about neurological disorders and the importance of brain health. The day also marks the establishment of the World Federation of Neurology (WFN) on July 22, 1957. In 2026, the theme is "Brain Health: Access For All," emphasising equitable access to diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation, and quality neurological care for everyone. The campaign encourages governments, healthcare professionals, and communities to improve brain health services, promote research, support early detection, and educate people about preventing neurological disorders through awareness and healthy lifestyles.

questions.question: Which state became the first in India to pass the Ease of Doing Business Act, 2026 with a trust-based business permission framework?

The Act classifies businesses according to risk levels, allowing low-risk enterprises to obtain approvals through self-certification or certification by licensed professionals. It also introduces an auto-approval mechanism when departments fail to act within prescribed timelines, removes annual renewal requirements for certain licenses, and initially covers 43 services across eight departments. The reform is expected to reduce compliance costs and simplify business operations for nearly 1.5 million MSMEs in the state.

The initiative aims to strengthen wildlife conservation, promote scientific research, improve visitor experiences through interactive AI displays, and encourage sustainable eco-tourism while preserving the fragile wetland ecosystem.

questions.question: When is National Broadcasting Day celebrated every year in India?

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the new Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of NITI Aayog by the Central Government?

With nearly four decades of administrative experience in both the state and central governments, Jain has contributed significantly to governance, industrial policy, and infrastructure development. His appointment is expected to strengthen NITI Aayog’s role in policy formulation, implementation, and driving economic and institutional reforms across the country.

questions.question: Who has been given the additional charge of Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) of IRCTC?

questions.question: Which village has been recognised as Tamil Nadu's first Climate-Resilient Village?
questions.explanation: Killai, located in Cuddalore district near the ecologically significant Pichavaram Mangrove Forest, has become Tamil Nadu's first Climate-Resilient Village. The village has adopted a community-based approach to address climate challenges such as cyclones, coastal erosion, sea-level rise, flooding, and saltwater intrusion. Its model integrates scientific planning, ecosystem conservation, climate-resilient infrastructure, sustainable water management, disaster preparedness, and climate-smart livelihoods. The initiative demonstrates how active community participation and nature-based solutions can strengthen resilience, protect livelihoods, and serve as a model for other vulnerable coastal regions across India.

questions.question: Which institution is hosting the 5th BRICS Working Group meeting on geospatial technology from July 20 to July 23, 2026?

The meeting brings together BRICS members and newly inducted nations to discuss AI-based geospatial analytics, positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) technologies, and geospatial infrastructure for sustainable development. The event aims to establish common geospatial data standards, improve information sharing, and strengthen international cooperation in natural resource management, disaster risk reduction, and climate resilience.

The award, announced by the Tilak Smarak Trust, will be presented on August 1, 2026, in Pune by Union Home Minister Amit Shah. A retired IPS officer of the 1968 Kerala cadre, Doval has played a vital role in intelligence coordination, counter-terrorism operations, and protecting India's strategic interests, making him one of the country's most respected security strategists.

questions.question: India became which member to deposit its Instrument of Acceptance of the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies (AFS)?
questions.explanation: India officially became the 123rd member to deposit its Instrument of Acceptance of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies (AFS) on July 20, 2026. The agreement, adopted during the 12th WTO Ministerial Conference in Geneva in 2022, aims to curb harmful fisheries subsidies by prohibiting support for illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing and activities involving overfished stocks. In India, its implementation is supported by the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) and sustainable fisheries regulations, while safeguarding the interests of small-scale fishers and promoting responsible marine resource management.

questions.question: What is the name of the indigenous turbofan engine unveiled by Paninian India for combat drones and cruise missiles?
questions.explanation: Yantur 4.5kN is an indigenous turbofan engine unveiled by Paninian India Private Ltd on July 20, 2026, to power combat drones and long-range cruise missiles. The engine generates 4.5 kN of thrust and can be scaled up to 12.5 kN for larger autonomous combat platforms. It has been developed to support the Ministry of Defence's Make-I programme for the Long-Range Land Attack Cruise Missile (LRLACM). The project incorporates advanced technologies, including compressor innovations, digital-twin health monitoring, and indigenous manufacturing techniques, strengthening India's self-reliance in aerospace propulsion systems and reducing dependence on foreign technology.

questions.question: Who won the gold medal at the Menuires International Chess Championship held in France in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Indian Grandmaster Rohith Krishna won the gold medal at the Menuires International Chess Championship held in France on July 21, 2026. He secured the title by winning the tie-break with a score of 43 after finishing unbeaten with 7 points in 9 rounds. Fellow Indian player Raja Rithvik claimed the silver medal with a tie-break score of 41.5, while French Grandmaster Omelja Artem finished third with 6.5 points. The tournament featured 86 players from several countries, highlighting India's growing strength and consistent success in international chess competitions.

Its maiden flight test was successfully conducted on July 23, 2026, from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island off the Odisha coast. During the test, the missile accurately tracked and intercepted a high-speed electronic aerial target, validating its radar, guidance, command, and control systems. Designed to counter aircraft, missiles, UAVs, and other fast-moving aerial threats, the fully indigenous system is expected to significantly strengthen India's multi-layered air defence network after further operational evaluations.

questions.question: In which state was Bharat Taxi launched as a cooperative taxi service to promote driver ownership and transparent mobility?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra launched Bharat Taxi as a cooperative taxi service on July 23, 2026, at Navi Mumbai International Airport. The initiative was inaugurated by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis along with Union Minister of State for Cooperation Murlidhar Mohol. Inspired by the vision of “Sahakar Se Samriddhi”, the service aims to provide affordable, transparent, and reliable transportation while empowering drivers as cooperative members and owners. Unlike conventional ride-hailing platforms, Bharat Taxi follows a fixed service charge model with no surge pricing or hidden fees, allowing drivers to share profits and ensuring better earnings, improved passenger experience, and stronger cooperative-based employment opportunities.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Secretary of the Department of Higher Education under the Ministry of Education in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Naresh Pal Gangwar was appointed as the Secretary of the Department of Higher Education under the Ministry of Education following the approval of the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) on July 23, 2026. A 1994-batch IAS officer from the Rajasthan cadre, he succeeded Vineet Joshi, who was transferred to the Department of Panchayati Raj. Previously serving as Secretary of the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Gangwar brings extensive administrative experience. He holds a B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering, an M.Tech from IIT Delhi, and an M.A. in Economics from the University of Rajasthan, making him well-equipped to lead higher education policy reforms.

questions.question: Which country is scheduled to host the South Asian Federation (SAF) Games in early 2027?

SAARC, founded in 1985 and headquartered in Kathmandu, comprises eight member countries working together to foster regional development and cooperation.

questions.question: When is Income Tax Day celebrated every year in India to commemorate the introduction of income tax by Sir James Wilson?
questions.explanation: Income Tax Day is observed every year on July 24 to commemorate the introduction of income tax in India by Sir James Wilson on July 24, 1860. In 2026, the observance marks 167 years of India's income tax system. The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) officially began celebrating the day in 2010 to recognise the contributions of honest taxpayers and promote tax awareness. The occasion also highlights the transformation of India's tax administration from a paper-based system to a modern digital platform featuring online ITR filing, faceless assessments, e-verification, pre-filled tax returns, and faster refund processing, making compliance simpler, transparent, and taxpayer-friendly.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the next CEO and Managing Director of Infosys, succeeding Salil Parekh from April 1, 2027?
questions.explanation: Ashiss Kumar Dash has been appointed as the next Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Managing Director (MD) of Infosys, with his five-year term beginning on April 1, 2027, after Salil Parekh completes his tenure. A graduate of IIT Kharagpur, Dash joined Infosys in 1995 and has spent nearly three decades with the company, leading several global business portfolios and digital transformation initiatives. He also headed the Energy, Utilities, and Resources (EURS) business and worked for nearly a decade in Los Angeles. His appointment marks a historic milestone as he becomes the first internally promoted CEO in Infosys' history, reflecting the company's focus on leadership continuity and AI-driven growth.

questions.question: Which Indian boxer confirmed India's first medal at the Commonwealth Games 2026 by securing a direct semifinal berth in the women's 75 kg boxing event?
questions.explanation: Lovlina Borgohain confirmed India's first medal at the Commonwealth Games 2026 after receiving a direct entry into the semifinals of the women's 75 kg boxing event in Glasgow, Scotland. Since only five boxers competed in the category, all semifinalists were guaranteed a medal under international boxing rules. A bronze medalist at the Tokyo Olympics, Lovlina entered the Games in excellent form after winning gold medals at the National Boxing Championships, the Boxam Elite International Tournament in Spain, and the Grand Prix of Usti nad Labem in the Czech Republic. This also marks her first-ever Commonwealth Games medal after quarterfinal finishes in 2018 and 2022.

questions.question: Which Indian state signed an MoU with the UAE to launch a food processing partnership and trade framework focused on horticultural value chains?
questions.explanation: Andhra Pradesh signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the UAE on July 21, 2026, through the Andhra Pradesh Economic Development Board (EDB) to establish a UAE-backed food processing partnership. The initiative aims to develop integrated value chains for horticultural products such as mangoes, bananas, and cocoa, with a special focus on transforming the Rayalaseema region into a major horticulture hub. The UAE-based firm Floor Masters International has proposed an initial investment of ₹100 crore, while the first processing unit will be established at Gangadhara Nellore in Chittoor district. The partnership is also expected to boost exports of seafood, dairy, poultry, and pulses to Gulf countries.

questions.question: In which city will India host the International Type 1 Diabetes Summit 2026 from July 30 to August 1, 2026?
questions.explanation: Jodhpur in Rajasthan will host the International Type 1 Diabetes Summit 2026 from July 30 to August 1, 2026. The three-day global conference will bring together leading diabetes specialists, researchers, policymakers, government officials, and patient representatives from countries including India, the USA, and Australia. Organised by Friends of Mewar, Breakthrough T1D, and the William J. Clinton Foundation, the summit will focus on improving access to affordable insulin, advancing diabetes technologies such as continuous glucose monitoring and insulin pumps, promoting digital health solutions, strengthening international research collaboration, and enhancing the quality of life for people living with Type 1 diabetes.

questions.question: Which state unveiled a comprehensive Global Capability Centre (GCC) feasibility report and strategic roadmap to become a leading GCC hub by 2031?
questions.explanation: Kerala launched a comprehensive Global Capability Centre (GCC) feasibility report and strategic roadmap during the Kerala GCC Outlook 2026 conclave held at Technopark, Thiruvananthapuram, on July 21, 2026. The state aims to attract 150 GCCs and create around 2 lakh jobs by 2031, building on its existing base of over 45 operational GCCs. As part of the initiative, Technopark signed an MoU with Collabera, while Infoparks Kerala partnered with ANSR to strengthen the state's IT ecosystem. The roadmap focuses on leveraging Kerala's skilled workforce, robust digital infrastructure, and mature IT sector to attract global investments and establish the state as a preferred destination for multinational companies.

questions.question: Which country declared a national emergency as devastating wildfires spread across Europe, forcing large-scale evacuations?
questions.explanation: Spain declared a national emergency for the first time in its history as severe wildfires spread across central parts of the country. The move enabled the national government to coordinate firefighting efforts and emergency response more effectively after over 10,000 residents were evacuated from affected areas near Madrid and Avila. At the same time, France sought assistance through the European Union Civil Protection Mechanism as massive fires forced the evacuation of around 63,000 people from Cap Ferret. Authorities attributed the worsening wildfire situation to extreme heat, prolonged drought, strong winds, dense vegetation, and the growing impact of climate change, highlighting the need for stronger disaster preparedness and international cooperation.

questions.question: Who assumed charge as the Chairman of the National Commission for Minorities (NCM) on July 21, 2026?
questions.explanation: Harjit Singh Grewal assumed charge as the Chairman of the National Commission for Minorities (NCM) on July 21, 2026. The NCM is a statutory body established under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, and functions under the Ministry of Minority Affairs. It is responsible for safeguarding the rights and interests of six notified religious minority communities in India—Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis (Zoroastrians), and Jains. Along with Grewal's appointment, S. Munawari Begum took charge as Vice Chairperson, while Glenn Souza Ticlo and Berjis Desai joined the Commission as members representing the Christian and Parsi communities, respectively.

questions.question: Who was given the additional charge of the Ministry of Education after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned from the Union Council of Ministers?
questions.explanation: Pralhad Joshi was assigned the additional charge of the Ministry of Education after President Droupadi Murmu accepted the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan on the recommendation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi under Article 75(2) of the Constitution. Joshi will continue to handle his existing portfolios of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and New and Renewable Energy while overseeing the Education Ministry until further orders. A senior BJP leader and Member of Parliament from Dharwad, Karnataka, he has previously served as the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs, Coal, and Mines, bringing extensive administrative and ministerial experience to his new responsibility.

questions.question: Which Indian state launched Mission Golden Spice to transform the GI-tagged Lakadong Turmeric into a globally competitive brand?
questions.explanation: Meghalaya launched Mission Golden Spice on July 21, 2026, to promote the globally renowned GI-tagged Lakadong Turmeric, which is known for its high curcumin content of 7–10%, significantly higher than the global average. With an investment of ₹175.45 crore, the five-year mission (2025–2030) aims to strengthen the turmeric value chain, double farmers' income, expand cultivation from 2,500 hectares to 7,500 hectares, and establish the Northeast's largest integrated organic turmeric processing and curcumin extraction facility. The initiative is led by the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER) and the North Eastern Council (NEC) under the "Ashtalakshmi" vision.

questions.question: In which Indian state will Paras Semiconductors establish a ₹6,200 crore advanced semiconductor packaging (OSAT) facility under a new MoU signed in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Paras Semiconductors on July 22, 2026, to establish a ₹6,200 crore greenfield Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) facility in the Indore-Ujjain region. The project will focus on advanced integrated circuit (IC) packaging technologies, including 2.5D and 3D packaging, chiplet integration, wafer bumping, and heterogeneous integration. The agreement was signed with the Madhya Pradesh State Electronics Development Corporation (MPSeDC), reinforcing the state's ambition to become a major semiconductor and electronics manufacturing hub. The initiative is also expected to attract further investments, generate employment, and strengthen India's semiconductor ecosystem.

questions.question: Which country has been invited by India as a special guest to participate in the BRICS Summit 2026 in New Delhi?
questions.explanation: Bangladesh has been invited by India as a special guest to the BRICS Summit 2026, scheduled to be held in New Delhi from September 17 to 19, 2026. Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended the invitation to Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, reflecting India's commitment to strengthening regional partnerships and engagement with the Global South. Although Bangladesh is not a BRICS member, it has previously expressed interest in joining the grouping, with support from countries such as China and Russia. The invitation also aligns with India's BRICS Chairmanship theme of promoting resilience, innovation, collaboration, and sustainability while enhancing cooperation in areas such as health, disaster management, digital transformation, climate resilience, and sustainable development.

questions.question: In which Indian state will HCLTech establish its first AI-optimised data centre and a global technology centre with an estimated investment of ₹15,000 crore?
questions.explanation: Odisha has been selected as the location for HCLTech's first AI-optimised data centre and global technology centre, with an estimated investment of ₹15,000 crore. The project will be developed at the Odisha Sovereign AI Park in Bhubaneswar in partnership with Sarvam AI and the Odisha Government. Expected to become operational by 2028, it will generate around 5,000 jobs and strengthen India's sovereign AI ecosystem. The facility will provide secure AI computing infrastructure, high-performance computing, cloud services, AI training capabilities, and multilingual AI solutions, supporting sectors such as healthcare, governance, education, finance, and manufacturing while promoting the Digital India and Atmanirbhar Bharat initiatives.

questions.question: Which online code hosting platform was directed by the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C) to remove repositories related to the Bitchat messaging app over security concerns?
questions.explanation: GitHub was directed by the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C), operating under the Ministry of Home Affairs, to remove repositories associated with the Bluetooth-based messaging app Bitchat. The action was taken under Section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology Act, 2000, and Rule 3(1)(d) of the Information Technology Rules, 2021, citing national security concerns. Bitchat is a decentralised, open-source messaging application that uses Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) mesh networks instead of the internet or centralised servers. Authorities expressed concerns that its anonymous and offline communication capabilities could be misused by terrorists, cybercriminals, organised crime groups, and other anti-national elements, making monitoring and law enforcement more challenging.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the Director of the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU)-India during the major bureaucratic reshuffle approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)?
questions.explanation: Satya Pal Kumar, a 2005-batch Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the Income Tax cadre, has been appointed as the Director of the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU)-India. The appointment was approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) as part of a major bureaucratic reshuffle involving around 20 senior officers. FIU-India, functioning under the Ministry of Finance, is responsible for collecting, analysing, and sharing intelligence on suspicious financial transactions. The agency plays a vital role in combating money laundering, terror financing, financial fraud, and other illicit financial activities while supporting domestic and international enforcement agencies in maintaining the integrity of India's financial system.

questions.question: Which organisation signed a long-term contract with Safran Aircraft Engines for the production of turbine ring forgings for the CFM LEAP engine programme?
questions.explanation: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) signed a long-term contract with Safran Aircraft Engines in July 2026 to manufacture and supply critical turbine ring forgings made from superalloys for the CFM LEAP engine programme. The components will be produced at HAL's Foundry and Forge Division in Bengaluru using advanced near-net shape ring forging technology for high-temperature engine applications. The agreement was signed during the Farnborough International Airshow in the United Kingdom. This partnership strengthens HAL's role in the global aerospace supply chain, expands its presence in the international civil aviation market, and supports the production of one of the world's most widely used commercial aircraft engines.

questions.question: In which state did the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) approve two new Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMCs) with a total investment of ₹1,012 crore?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) approved two new Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMCs) in Tamil Nadu with a total investment of ₹1,012 crore. The Manallur Cluster will be developed over 474.3 acres with a project cost of ₹587.47 crore, while the Pillapaikkam Cluster will cover 379.3 acres with an investment of ₹424.55 crore. The initiative supports the Semicon India Programme and strengthens India's electronics manufacturing ecosystem. It is expected to boost semiconductor and electronics production, attract investments, generate employment, and enhance India's position as a global manufacturing hub. The approval also complements talent development and AI initiatives being implemented across the country.

questions.question: Which state approved a 10% reservation for ex-Agniveers in state civil services?
questions.explanation: Chhattisgarh approved a 10% reservation for ex-Agniveers in direct recruitment to Class-III (Group C) state government posts. The reservation applies to positions such as Police Constables, Forest Guards, and Praheri (Guards) in the Jail Department. The decision was approved by the state cabinet chaired by Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai through the Chhattisgarh Civil Services Reservation Rules, 2026. The benefit is available only to Agniveers who have completed four years of service in the Indian Armed Forces and hold a valid discharge certificate. The policy also complements the state's Industrial Development Policy 2024, which offers additional benefits to Agniveers, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes.

questions.question: Which country held bilateral talks with India to expand cooperation in maritime security, logistics, and digital transformation?
questions.explanation: Panama and India held bilateral talks on July 22, 2026, to strengthen cooperation in maritime security, logistics, maritime education, and digital transformation. The discussions included collaboration between India's Directorate General of Shipping and the Panama Maritime Authority, along with initiatives in Artificial Intelligence (AI), smart port logistics, maritime single-window systems, and resilient supply chains. Both countries also agreed to work together on green ship recycling, port modernisation, and warehousing. Recognised as a strategic gateway to Central America, Latin America, and the Caribbean through the Panama Canal, Panama plays a vital role in global maritime trade. India also invited Panama to participate in India Maritime Week 2026 in New Delhi.

questions.question: Which country successfully launched the Gravity-1 commercial rocket from a vessel, carrying nine satellites into orbit?
questions.explanation: China successfully launched the Gravity-1 commercial rocket from a vessel in the East China Sea on July 22, 2026, placing nine satellites into their designated orbit. Developed by the private aerospace company ORIENSPACE, the mission marked the world's first far-sea launch of a privately developed commercial rocket. The launch demonstrated the capability to conduct rocket missions under complex offshore conditions. Gravity-1 is the world's first medium-lift launch vehicle using all-solid-propellant strap-on boosters and can carry payloads to both Low-Earth Orbit and Sun-Synchronous Orbit. The satellites will support remote sensing, land mapping, AI-powered Earth observation, disaster response, and advanced satellite technology testing.

questions.question: Which institution is hosting the 3rd Digital India RISC-V (DIR-V) Symposium on August 1–2, 2026?
questions.explanation: IIT Madras is hosting the 3rd Digital India RISC-V (DIR-V) Symposium in collaboration with the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and RISC-V International. The event is being held at the IIT Madras Research Park in Chennai under the theme “Empowering Bharat’s Semiconductor Future.” The symposium focuses on advancing processor design, semiconductor technologies, AI hardware, embedded systems, cybersecurity, and secure silicon design. It supports the Government of India’s Digital India RISC-V initiative, which aims to achieve silicon sovereignty by promoting indigenous microprocessor development based on the open-source RISC-V architecture for global applications.

questions.question: Which state launched the Samras Vidya Setu campaign to re-enrol over 80,000 school dropout children into the formal education system?
questions.explanation: Gujarat launched the Samras Vidya Setu mega campaign in July 2026 to bring more than 80,000 school dropout children back into the formal education system. The initiative aims to enrol children from Standards 1 to 12 in age-appropriate classes through bridge courses, remedial coaching, and residential schools for students with learning gaps. The campaign uses the Early Tracking System, Child Monitoring System, and field monitoring by CRC and BRC coordinators to identify and support dropout students. It aligns with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, while recognising high-performing districts and School Management Committees on Teachers' Day to encourage sustained educational progress.

questions.question: Which country received 4.5 tonnes of life-saving medical supplies and personal protective equipment (PPE) from India to strengthen public health preparedness?
questions.explanation: Kenya received 4.5 tonnes of life-saving medical supplies and personal protective equipment (PPE) from India on July 24, 2026, under India's Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) framework. The relief package included PPE, emergency fluid management kits, and infection prevention supplies to enhance preparedness against Ebola and other infectious disease outbreaks. The assistance was coordinated through the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and the Indian High Commission in Nairobi. The initiative also strengthens India's ongoing cooperation with the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), reinforcing healthcare resilience, regional disease surveillance, and India's commitment to supporting global public health and humanitarian efforts.

questions.question: Which state will launch the ‘Mee Bhoomi–Blockchain’ pilot project to create a tamper-proof and integrated land records management system?
questions.explanation: Andhra Pradesh is launching the ‘Mee Bhoomi–Blockchain’ pilot project across seven mandals to modernise land records using blockchain technology. The project integrates data from the revenue, survey, and registration departments into a single secure platform. Built using Hyperledger Fabric by NIC Andhra Pradesh and the Centre of Excellence in Blockchain Technology at NIC Bengaluru, it assigns a unique blockchain identity to each land parcel. The system supports citizen services such as auto-mutation, subdivision, and extent correction while automatically stopping transactions when data mismatches are detected. Every transaction is permanently recorded with the responsible official’s identity and timestamp, ensuring transparency, security, and protection against record tampering.

questions.question: Which country signed three Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with India to double bilateral trade within the next three years?
questions.explanation: Romania and India signed three Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) on July 24, 2026, during President Droupadi Murmu's official state visit to Bucharest. The agreements cover cooperation in agriculture and food processing, renewable energy and clean technology, and cultural exchange and higher education mobility for the period 2026–2030. Both countries also set a target to increase bilateral trade to over $3 billion within the next three years. The visit marked the first by an Indian Head of State to Romania in nearly two decades, highlighting the growing strategic partnership and expanding collaboration in trade, sustainability, education, and cultural relations between the two nations.

questions.question: Which company became the first non-bank entity in India to receive a perpetual Authorised Dealer Category-II (AD Category-II) license from the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.explanation: EbixCash World Money became the first non-bank entity in India to receive a perpetual Authorised Dealer Category-II (AD Category-II) license from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). This license enables the company to provide cross-border trade-related remittance services in addition to family remittances under the regulatory framework of the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999. The approval is expected to benefit Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) by allowing them to make outward trade remittances directly without depending on traditional commercial banks. The milestone reflects the RBI's regulated approach to expanding foreign exchange services while maintaining compliance and financial stability.

questions.question: What is the minimum percentage of daily content that private FM radio channels must broadcast in the local language under the new government mandate?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting mandated that all operational private FM radio channels in India must broadcast at least 20% of their daily content in the local language of the city they serve. The initiative aims to promote regional languages, preserve local culture, traditions, and folk music, and strengthen community engagement. Announced on July 24, 2026, the policy applies to 386 operational private FM channels. It is part of the Phase-III FM expansion policy, which also encourages broadcasting in aspirational districts and Left Wing Extremism (LWE)-affected areas while supporting faster infrastructure rollout through the use of Prasar Bharati towers.

questions.question: In which city was the national 'Weaves of India' Handloom Festival inaugurated on July 26, 2026?
questions.explanation: The 'Weaves of India' Handloom Festival was inaugurated in New Delhi at the Central Cottage Industries Emporium by the Ministry of Textiles as part of the celebrations leading up to the 12th National Handloom Day. The festival showcases a wide range of GI-tagged handloom products, including Pashmina shawls, Kanjeevaram silk, Chanderi sarees, Pochampally ikat, and Muga silk. More than 150 master weavers and National Handicraft Awardees participate, providing a direct platform to connect with urban buyers. All displayed products carry the Handloom Mark and Silk Mark, ensuring authenticity and quality while promoting India's rich handloom heritage.

questions.question: Which state launched the Water Plan 2047 roadmap to ensure long-term water security for domestic and agricultural needs?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan launched the Water Plan 2047 under the leadership of Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma to strengthen long-term water security across the state. The roadmap integrates the Eastern Rajasthan Canal Project (ERCP) with the Parbati-Kalisindh-Chambal river interlinking project to improve water availability. It also aims to achieve 100% drip and sprinkler-based micro-irrigation in desert districts by 2035, mandates rooftop rainwater harvesting systems for commercial and institutional buildings, and proposes transferring surplus river water from southern Rajasthan to arid western regions. The comprehensive plan focuses on sustainable water management, agricultural development, and improved access to water for future generations.

questions.question: Which state plans to radio-collar herd-leading elephants ahead of the 2027 Haridwar Kumbh Mela?
questions.explanation: Uttarakhand has launched an initiative to radio-collar herd-leading elephants ahead of the 2027 Haridwar Kumbh Mela to improve public safety and reduce human-elephant conflict. The project is being implemented by the Uttarakhand Forest Department in collaboration with the Wildlife Institute of India (WII). Real-time tracking of elephant movements will help forest officials issue timely warnings, guide elephants away from populated areas, and respond quickly during the large gathering of pilgrims. The initiative also supports wildlife conservation by protecting elephants while ensuring safer management of one of India's most important elephant corridors near Rajaji National Park.

questions.question: In which city were solar-electric passenger boats launched on the River Ganga under the Jal Marg Vikas Project?
questions.explanation: Solar-electric passenger boats were launched on the River Ganga in Varanasi by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) in collaboration with the Uttar Pradesh Tourism Department. The initiative introduces zero-emission electric catamarans to replace diesel-powered boats across 84 historic ghats, promoting clean and sustainable river transport. Each boat can carry 50 passengers, travels at a speed of 10 knots, and uses fast-charging solar docks. The project is part of the Jal Marg Vikas Project on National Waterway-1 (Haldia to Prayagraj) and aims to reduce over 1,200 tonnes of carbon emissions while preventing oil pollution in the sacred Ganga River.

questions.question: Which state implements the Mahatma Jyotirao Phule Jan Arogya Yojana (MJPJAY) for cashless healthcare?
questions.explanation: The Mahatma Jyotirao Phule Jan Arogya Yojana (MJPJAY) is a flagship health insurance scheme implemented by the Government of Maharashtra to provide cashless medical treatment to eligible families. Launched in 2012, the scheme covers hospitalisation expenses up to ₹1.5 lakh per family annually, with coverage increasing to ₹2.5 lakh for organ transplants. Families eligible under both MJPJAY and Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY can receive combined health insurance coverage of up to ₹5 lakh per year. The scheme includes 996 medical procedures across 34 specialities and is available through empanelled government and private hospitals, ensuring affordable and accessible healthcare for beneficiaries.

questions.question: Who won the silver medal in the men's 65kg weightlifting event at the Commonwealth Games 2026?
questions.explanation: Raja Muthupandi won the silver medal in the men's 65kg weightlifting event at the Commonwealth Games 2026 held in Glasgow. He achieved a total lift of 286kg across the snatch and clean & jerk events. Despite recovering from an early failed attempt and briefly setting a Commonwealth Games record in the clean & jerk, he finished behind Malaysia's Aznil Bin Bidin Muhamed, who secured the gold with a Games record total of 299kg. Raja's remarkable comeback from a serious elbow injury and years of perseverance made his silver medal a significant achievement, further strengthening India's impressive weightlifting medal tally at the Games.

questions.question: When is CRPF Foundation Day celebrated every year in India?
questions.explanation: CRPF Foundation Day is observed every year on July 27 to commemorate the establishment of the Central Reserve Police Force, which was originally formed in 1939 as the Crown Representative’s Police. In 2026, the force celebrated its 87th Foundation Day, recognising the courage, sacrifice, and dedication of CRPF personnel. The CRPF plays a crucial role in maintaining internal security, conducting counter-terrorism and anti-insurgency operations, ensuring peaceful elections, controlling riots, protecting vital installations, and providing disaster relief. It also participates in United Nations peacekeeping missions, reflecting India's commitment to global peace and security.

questions.question: Sarnath became India's which UNESCO World Heritage Site after its inscription in 2026?
questions.explanation: Sarnath was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List during the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee held on July 26, 2026. With this recognition, Sarnath became India's 45th UNESCO World Heritage Site and the country's 36th Cultural World Heritage Site. Located near Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh, Sarnath is one of Buddhism's holiest places, where Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon to his first five disciples after attaining enlightenment. The site is renowned for monuments such as the Dhamek Stupa, Chaukhandi Stupa, Mulagandhakuti Vihara, and the Lion Capital of Ashoka, which serves as India's National Emblem.

questions.question: Who won the silver medal in the men's 79kg weightlifting category at the Commonwealth Games 2026?
questions.explanation: Ajaya Babu won the silver medal in the men's 79kg weightlifting event at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow with a combined lift of 330kg, consisting of 149kg in the snatch and 181kg in the clean and jerk. He narrowly missed the gold medal by just 1kg, as Malaysia's Erry Hidayat Muhammad secured first place with a Games record total of 331kg. During the competition, Ajaya also equalled the Commonwealth Games record with his total lift. His silver medal became India's sixth weightlifting medal at the Games, further strengthening the country's reputation as a leading force in international weightlifting.

questions.question: On which date is World Nature Conservation Day observed every year?
questions.explanation: World Nature Conservation Day is observed every year on July 28 to promote awareness about conserving natural resources, protecting biodiversity, and encouraging sustainable development. The observance highlights the importance of preserving forests, wildlife, rivers, oceans, wetlands, and other ecosystems that support life on Earth. It also draws attention to major environmental challenges such as climate change, deforestation, pollution, and habitat destruction. The day encourages governments, organisations, and individuals to adopt eco-friendly practices and strengthen conservation efforts to ensure environmental stability, economic progress, and a healthier future for coming generations.

questions.question: On which date is World Hepatitis Day observed every year?
questions.explanation: World Hepatitis Day is observed every year on July 28 to raise awareness about viral hepatitis and encourage prevention, early testing, vaccination, and treatment. The day commemorates the birth anniversary of Dr Baruch Samuel Blumberg, who discovered the hepatitis B virus and developed the first hepatitis B vaccine. The 2026 theme, "Hepatitis: Let's Break It Down," emphasises removing barriers to healthcare, improving access to screening and treatment, reducing stigma, and strengthening global efforts to eliminate viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030. It also highlights the importance of public awareness and timely medical intervention to save lives.

questions.question: Which state launched the e-Zero FIR system for cyber financial fraud cases in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Gujarat launched the e-Zero FIR system on July 27, 2026, to simplify and speed up the reporting of cyber financial fraud cases. The initiative allows victims to file complaints through the 1930 National Cybercrime Helpline without visiting a police station. Once a complaint is registered, an e-Zero FIR is automatically generated and electronically forwarded to the concerned police station for immediate action. Developed in collaboration with the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the Ministry of Home Affairs, the system aims to improve response times, increase the chances of recovering defrauded money, strengthen cybercrime investigations, and promote technology-driven policing and citizen services.

questions.question: In which state will Raghu Vamsi Aerospace Group establish a ₹600 crore integrated nickel-based superalloy manufacturing facility?
questions.explanation: Raghu Vamsi Aerospace Group announced a ₹600 crore investment to establish an integrated nickel-based superalloy manufacturing facility in Telangana on July 23, 2026. The 50-acre plant will have an annual production capacity of 5,000 tonnes, with commercial production expected to begin in January 2028. The facility will manufacture round bars, wires, forgings, castings, and tungsten carbide powders for strategic sectors such as aerospace, defence, nuclear energy, and gas turbines. Led by Dr. S.K. Jha, former CMD of MIDHANI, the project aims to strengthen India's self-reliance by reducing dependence on imported strategic materials and enhancing domestic supply-chain security.

questions.question: Who won the silver medal in the men's high jump at the Commonwealth Games 2026?
questions.explanation: Sarvesh Kushare won the silver medal in the men's high jump at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow with a best jump of 2.25 metres. He cleared the height on his final attempt, demonstrating remarkable composure under pressure. Although he could not clear 2.28 metres, his performance earned him the first major multi-sport medal of his career. The achievement also surpassed India's previous best result of a bronze medal in the event at the Commonwealth Games. Earlier, Sarvesh had set a new Indian national record of 2.31 metres at the Inter-State Athletics Championships, confirming his place among the country's finest high jumpers.

questions.question: Who won the gold medal in the women's 25m pistol event at the ISSF World Cup 2026 in Hangzhou, China?
questions.explanation: Esha Singh won the gold medal in the women's 25m pistol event at the ISSF World Cup 2026 held in Hangzhou, China. The 21-year-old shooter delivered an outstanding performance in the final by scoring 40 hits, defeating China's Zhang Yueyue, who secured the silver medal with 37 hits. Her victory also earned her direct qualification for the ISSF World Cup Final 2026 in Rome, Italy, as gold medalists automatically qualify for the season-ending event. Meanwhile, Manu Bhaker added another international achievement by winning the bronze medal, highlighting the continued excellence of India's women's pistol shooting team on the global stage.

questions.question: Which airline signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Saudia in July 2026 to expand codeshare connectivity?
questions.explanation: Air India signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Saudi Arabia's national carrier, Saudia, in July 2026 to strengthen their strategic partnership and expand codeshare connectivity between India and Saudi Arabia. The agreement includes plans to broaden existing codeshare arrangements, assess terminal co-location at selected airports, and explore cooperation between their frequent flyer programmes. The partnership may also extend to Air India Express and Saudi low-cost airline flyadeal. Since its re-acquisition by the Tata Group in 2022, Air India has significantly expanded its global network through numerous codeshare agreements and interline partnerships, enhancing international connectivity for passengers.

questions.question: Which bank was named the World's Best Corporate Bank 2026 by Global Finance?
questions.explanation: DBS was recognised as the World's Best Corporate Bank 2026 at the Global Finance Global Bank Awards announced on July 27, 2026. It became the first Southeast Asian bank to receive this prestigious honour since the award category was introduced in 2005. In addition, DBS was named Asia's Best Bank and Singapore's Best Bank, while also earning the titles of Best Bank for Financial Institutions in Asia-Pacific for the second consecutive year and Best Transaction Bank in Asia-Pacific for the third consecutive year. Headquartered in Singapore, DBS is known for integrating AI-enabled banking solutions and providing advanced financial services to SMEs and multinational corporations worldwide.

questions.question: Which Indian athletes won silver medals for India at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in men's 10,000m and women's 69kg weightlifting, respectively?
options: Jadumani Singh Mandengbam and Harjinder Kaur

Gulveer Singh created history by becoming the first Indian athlete to win a Commonwealth Games medal in the men's 10,000-metre event after clocking 27:49.78 to finish second behind Australia's Ky Robinson. Harjinder Kaur secured the silver medal in the women's 69kg weightlifting event with a combined lift of 227 kg. It was her second consecutive Commonwealth Games medal after winning bronze in Birmingham 2022. Their achievements helped India increase its overall medal tally to 12, reflecting the country's strong performance across multiple sporting disciplines.

questions.question: On which date is International Tiger Day observed every year?
questions.explanation: International Tiger Day is observed every year on July 29 to raise global awareness about tiger conservation and the protection of their natural habitats. Established following the 2010 Tiger Summit in St. Petersburg, Russia, the observance encourages governments, conservation organisations, and local communities to work together against poaching, habitat destruction, illegal wildlife trade, and climate change. The 2026 theme, "Securing the Future of Tigers with Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities at the Heart," highlights the crucial role of local communities in conservation. India, which is home to over 70% of the world's wild tigers, continues to lead global tiger conservation through initiatives such as Project Tiger and the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA).

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Official Liquidator for the winding-up of Paytm Payments Bank by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)?
questions.explanation: Girikumar Nair, former Chief General Manager of the State Bank of India (SBI), was appointed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) as the Official Liquidator for Paytm Payments Bank Limited. His responsibilities include supervising the winding-up process, ensuring compliance with the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, and the Companies Act, 2013, managing the settlement of liabilities, and protecting the interests of depositors and stakeholders. The RBI initiated the liquidation after the Delhi High Court approved the process following the cancellation of the bank's licence due to serious regulatory violations. The RBI also assured that the bank has sufficient liquidity to repay eligible depositors.

questions.question: What is India's global rank as a supplier of seafarers according to the BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2026?
questions.explanation: According to the BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2026, India has become the world's second-largest supplier of seafarers, contributing 311,936 maritime professionals, which account for 12.16% of the global seafaring workforce. India is ranked behind the Philippines and ahead of China, the Russian Federation, and Indonesia. This achievement reflects the country's remarkable progress in maritime education, skill development, and workforce training. India's share has grown significantly from 5.2% in 2015 to 12.16% in 2026, strengthening its position in the global maritime industry and supporting its vision of becoming a leading global maritime hub.

questions.question: Which state launched the Digital Square and ARISE initiatives to integrate Artificial Intelligence and Robotics into school education?
questions.explanation: Kerala launched the Digital Square and ARISE initiatives to strengthen Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Robotics education in schools across the state. Implemented by the Kerala Infrastructure and Technology for Education (KITE) under the General Education Department, the initiatives aim to create a scientific digital culture and establish robotics laboratories in all state syllabus high schools. Students will receive training in emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things (IoT), Drone Technology, and Robotics. The programme also expands Little KITEs IT clubs to additional school levels and enforces the Cyber Safety Protocol 2026, helping prepare students with future-ready digital skills.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian to win the Girls' Singles title at the World Squash Junior Championships in 2026?
questions.explanation: Anahat Singh created history on July 26, 2026, by becoming the first Indian to win the Girls' Singles title at the World Squash Junior Championships held in Niagara-on-the-Lake, Canada. The top-seeded Indian defeated Egypt's Ruqayya Salem in straight games, 11-3, 11-7, 11-9, to secure the championship without dropping a single game throughout the final. Her victory ended Egypt's 16-year dominance in the girls' singles category. Ranked No. 20 on the senior PSA Tour, Anahat's achievement is considered a major boost for Indian squash ahead of its Olympic debut at the 2028 Los Angeles Games.

questions.question: Which country eased the rules allowing Indian ₹200 and ₹500 currency notes to be carried across its border in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Nepal eased its regulations on July 26, 2026, by allowing Indian and Nepalese nationals to carry Indian currency notes of ₹200 and ₹500 denominations across the India–Nepal border. The revised rules permit individuals to carry Indian currency up to a maximum value of ₹25,000 per person, provided the ₹200 and ₹500 notes were issued on or after November 9, 2016. However, pre-November 9, 2016, ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes remain prohibited. The clarification was issued by the Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB), Nepal's central bank, to facilitate smoother cross-border transactions while maintaining regulatory oversight.

questions.question: Which country formally notified the United Nations of its decision to withdraw from the Rome Statute and exit the International Criminal Court (ICC)?
