questions.question: What global toy market share has the Toy Sector Task Force targeted for India by 2032?
questions.explanation: The Toy Sector Task Force, announced by Union Minister Piyush Goyal on July 27, 2026, has set a target of achieving a 5% share in the global toy market by 2032. The initiative aims to strengthen India's toy manufacturing ecosystem by integrating with global value chains, promoting innovation and design, resolving supply chain bottlenecks, and developing a skilled workforce. A comprehensive Toy Sector Playbook has also been launched to guide MSMEs, startups, and investors on manufacturing standards, intellectual property, compliance, and export opportunities. The initiative is expected to enhance India's competitiveness and establish the country as a major global toy manufacturing hub.

questions.question: Which state authorised the issuance of the Family Register Certificate through the MeeSeva platform in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Telangana authorised the issuance of the Telangana Family Register Certificate through the MeeSeva platform on July 28, 2026, to ensure uniform verification of family records across the state. Issued by the Revenue Department, the electronic Family Register captures details such as Aadhaar number, date of birth, gender, and relationship to the head of the family, with the Family Register Identification Number matching the family's Ration Card Number. Citizens can obtain the certificate through MeeSeva centres or mobile applications by paying a user fee of ₹62. The certificate is also recognised by the Election Commission of India as one of the accepted documents for the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

questions.question: Which institution designed and deployed the ANNAM.AI AI-powered smart weather stations for Kerala's climate-smart agriculture initiative?
questions.explanation: IIT Ropar designed and deployed the ANNAM.AI AI-powered hyper-local weather intelligence system for the Kerala government's climate-smart agriculture initiative launched on July 28, 2026. Introduced as part of the state's 100-day action plan, the system provides real-time weather data and localised advisories to help farmers make informed decisions regarding sowing, irrigation, harvesting, and crop protection. The initiative aims to enhance agricultural resilience, reduce crop losses, and improve farm productivity through data-driven decision-making. Established in 2008 in Rupnagar, Punjab, IIT Ropar is one of India's second-generation Indian Institutes of Technology operating under the Ministry of Education.

questions.question: Which state launched the Mukhyamantri Machhuara Samman Nidhi Yojana to provide financial assistance to fishermen during the annual fishing ban period?
questions.explanation: Himachal Pradesh launched the Mukhyamantri Machhuara Samman Nidhi Yojana on July 29, 2026, under the leadership of Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu. The scheme provides annual financial assistance of ₹3,500 to eligible fishermen to support their household needs during the closed fishing season. Around 3,700 fisherman families dependent on major reservoirs such as Gobind Sagar, Pong Dam, Kol Dam, Chamera, and Ranjit Sagar are expected to benefit. The state has allocated an annual budget of approximately ₹1.20 crore for the scheme, which also promotes sustainable fisheries by supporting fishermen during the breeding season when fishing is prohibited.

questions.question: Which UAE tourist attraction became the first to accept UPI for online ticket bookings in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Burj Khalifa became the first tourist attraction in the United Arab Emirates to accept UPI for online ticket bookings on July 29, 2026. The initiative was launched through a partnership between NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL), NEOPAY, and Emaar Entertainment. It marked the first use of UPI for e-commerce transactions in the GCC region, enabling Indian travellers to purchase tickets in Indian currency through UPI apps before arriving in Dubai. This development expands the global reach of India's digital payment ecosystem.

questions.question: Which bank is set to become the first Indian bank in 2026 to issue Basel III-compliant AT-1 Perpetual Bonds?
questions.explanation: State Bank of India (SBI) is set to become the first Indian bank in 2026 to issue Basel III-compliant Additional Tier-I (AT-1) Perpetual Bonds. Through this issuance, SBI plans to raise ₹5,000 crore as part of its ₹60,000 crore capital-raising programme for FY 2026–27. The bonds will include a five-year call option, subject to regulatory approval. AT-1 Perpetual Bonds help banks strengthen their capital base, improve the Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR), comply with Basel III regulations, and enhance their capacity to absorb financial losses. The initiative will also support SBI's future lending, business expansion, and long-term financial resilience.

questions.question: Which insurance company launched the Promise2Secure life insurance plan in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Canara HSBC Life Insurance launched the Promise2Secure plan on July 29, 2026, as a non-linked, non-participating individual life insurance product. The plan offers two variants, Life Secure and Life Secure with Return of Premium and provides protection against accidental death, permanent disability, and 40 specified critical illnesses. It also includes features such as Child Care Benefit, Waiver of Premium on terminal illness, premium deferment, instant claim payouts, legacy planning support, teleconsultation services, and a premium lock feature. Established in 2007, Canara HSBC Life is headquartered in Gurugram, Haryana, and primarily operates through the bancassurance model.

questions.question: Who won the gold medal in the Men's 100m T47 event at the Commonwealth Games 2026?
questions.explanation: Dilip Gavit won the gold medal in the Men's 100m T47 para-athletics event at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow. He completed the race in 10.71 seconds, setting a new Commonwealth Games record and registering his season's best performance. His victory helped India secure its third gold medal of the Games. Mohammed Basil Morssinganakathi won the silver medal with a timing of 10.83 seconds, creating India's first-ever one-two finish in the Men's 100m T47 event. Murali Sreeshankar also added a silver medal in the men's long jump with a leap of 8.09 metres.

questions.question: Which organisation approved an $850 million loan to support the expansion of the Pradhan Mantri Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana in July 2026?
questions.explanation: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) approved an $850 million loan on July 30, 2026, to support Subprogram 2 of the Accelerating Affordable and Inclusive Rooftop Solar Systems Development Program under the Pradhan Mantri Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana. The initiative aims to install rooftop solar systems for 10 million low- and middle-income households, achieve 30 GW of residential solar capacity by FY2027, train 6,000 individuals with at least one-third women, and reduce carbon emissions by an estimated 28.8 million tonnes, while promoting sustainable solar infrastructure and clean energy adoption across India.

questions.question: Which state launched the DWEEPTI Yojana, India's first women-led distributed renewable energy policy, in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Chhattisgarh launched the DWEEPTI Yojana in July 2026 to promote women-led solar entrepreneurship and expand renewable energy access across rural areas. The scheme aims to establish 5,000 women-led solar enterprises and generate around 50,000 green jobs by empowering Self-Help Groups (SHGs) with training, financial support, and business opportunities. It also targets providing clean energy to 5 lakh families and 10,000 public institutions. Implemented under the Pradhan Mantri Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, the initiative links renewable energy adoption with women's economic empowerment and sustainable rural development.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Director of the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) by the Union government in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Satya Pal Kumar, a 2005-batch Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer from the Income Tax Department, was appointed as the Director of the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) on July 30, 2026. The FIU functions under the Union Finance Ministry and is responsible for receiving, processing, analyzing, and disseminating information related to suspicious financial transactions to combat money laundering and financial crimes. Established in 2004 and headquartered in New Delhi, the FIU reports to the Economic Intelligence Council (EIC), which is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.

questions.question: Which company launched India's first UPI-based Flexi Benefits Wallet for employee tax savings in July 2026?
questions.explanation: OmniCard launched India's first UPI-based Flexi Benefits Wallet, called the Flexi Benefits Basket, in July 2026. Developed by Eroute Technologies Private Limited, the platform enables employees to manage tax-efficient benefits through a single digital wallet and make UPI Scan-and-Pay transactions at nearly 60 million UPI-enabled merchants. Built on an RBI-licensed Prepaid Payment Instrument (PPI) platform, it supports benefits such as meals, fuel, telecom, books, and gadgets. The solution also uses Merchant Category Code (MCC)-based controls to ensure tax compliance and aligns with the Income-tax Rules, 2026, enhancing employee tax savings and digital payment convenience.

questions.question: Which state approved the Special Asset Management Platform for Administration Tracking and Harmonisation Portal in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Kerala approved the Special Asset Management Platform for Administration Tracking and Harmonisation Portal on July 29, 2026, to strengthen digital governance and improve the management of government assets. The platform will maintain a comprehensive asset register covering land, buildings, roads, dams, bridges, vehicles, machinery, and other public infrastructure across 591 government institutions. The Cabinet also approved Plan Space 2.0 with GIS-based mapping of nearly 1,900 capital projects, initiated legislative reforms to simplify citizen services, and sanctioned additional land for the BrahMos Aerospace project, reflecting the state's commitment to efficient governance and infrastructure development.

questions.question: Which company is one of the founding members of the Open Secure AI Alliance launched to strengthen artificial intelligence security?
questions.explanation: NVIDIA is one of the founding members of the Open Secure AI Alliance, a collaborative initiative launched with global technology companies including Microsoft, IBM, Cisco, Dell Technologies, Cloudflare, Red Hat, Hugging Face, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow, and the Linux Foundation. The alliance aims to improve AI security by developing standardised tools to detect, investigate, and respond to AI-related cybersecurity threats. It also promotes the sharing of open-weight AI models, curated datasets, and cybersecurity research to enable safe and responsible adoption of artificial intelligence across industries.

questions.question: On which date is the World Day Against Trafficking in Persons observed every year?
questions.explanation: World Day Against Trafficking in Persons is observed annually on July 30 to raise awareness about human trafficking and promote the protection of victims' rights. Proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly in 2013, the observance encourages global cooperation to prevent trafficking, prosecute offenders, and support survivors. The 2026 theme, "Trapped Behind the Scam," highlights the growing threat of cyber-enabled trafficking, where victims are deceived through fake job offers and forced into online financial fraud and other criminal activities.

questions.question: Which state exported its first international consignment of Purabi Ice Cream to Bhutan in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Assam exported its first international consignment of 5,627 litres of Purabi Ice Cream to Bhutan on July 28, 2026. The consignment was flagged off by Chief Minister Dr Himanta Biswa Sarma. The ice cream was manufactured by West Assam Milk Producers' Cooperative Union Limited (WAMUL) and exported through North East Dairy and Foods Limited (NEDFL). APEDA supported the initiative by facilitating export documentation, regulatory compliance, and market access. The shipment is aimed at expanding the presence of Made-in-Assam dairy products in international markets, particularly in Bhutan's major cities such as Thimphu, Paro, Phuentsholing, and Wangdue.

questions.question: In which city will India's first Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) be established?
questions.explanation: India's first Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) will be established in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, to strengthen domestic telecom and electronics manufacturing. The project will be developed over approximately 350 acres through a collaboration between the Madhya Pradesh Government and the Department of Telecommunications (DoT). It is expected to attract investments of ₹12,000–15,000 crore and create around 5,000 direct jobs. The manufacturing zone will produce mobile phones, telecom equipment, semiconductors, optical fibre, and 5G/6G technology products, supporting the Make in India and Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiatives while reducing dependence on imports.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian to win the men's judo gold medal at the Commonwealth Games 2026?
questions.explanation: Harsh Singh created history by becoming the first Indian male judoka to win a gold medal at the Commonwealth Games. He achieved this milestone by defeating Australia's Joshua Katz in the men's 60 kg final at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games. The victory marked a major breakthrough for Indian judo and came on the same day that Asmita Dey won India's first-ever women's judo gold. Harsh's success reflects the steady growth of Indian judo, supported by his strong performances in International Judo Federation events and consistent progress on the international stage.

questions.question: What was India's global ranking in the 2023 Market Distortions Performance Index according to the Competere Foundation report?
questions.explanation: India secured the 57th position in the 2023 Market Distortions Performance Index, improving significantly from 82nd place in 2010 and climbing 25 positions over 13 years. The Competere Foundation credited this progress to major structural and pro-competitive reforms such as the Goods and Services Tax (GST), Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), regulatory simplification, and trade facilitation measures. The report highlighted improvements in ownership rights protection, domestic competition, and international competitiveness, reflecting India's efforts to create a more transparent, investment-friendly, and globally competitive economy that supports long-term sustainable growth.

questions.question: Who won the silver medal in the men's +110kg weightlifting event at the Commonwealth Games 2026?
questions.explanation: Lovepreet Singh secured the silver medal in the men's +110kg weightlifting event at the Commonwealth Games 2026 after finishing with a total lift of 388 kg. He narrowly missed the gold medal by just 1 kg, as New Zealand's David Liti lifted 389 kg to claim the top position. Lovepreet delivered an outstanding performance in the snatch event, setting a new Commonwealth Games record with a 176 kg lift. Despite a strong clean and jerk effort, he was unable to complete the decisive 217 kg lift, finishing second and adding another medal to India's weightlifting tally.

questions.question: Which country's instant payment system, Favara, has been integrated with India's UPI to enable real-time cross-border money transfers?
questions.explanation: The Favara-UPI cross-border payment corridor connects the Maldives' instant payment system, Favara, with India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI), enabling users to transfer money instantly from the Maldives to UPI-linked bank accounts in India. Transactions are initiated in Maldivian Rufiyaa (MVR) and automatically converted into Indian Rupees (INR). The initiative was launched through collaboration between the Maldives Monetary Authority (MMA), the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL), and participating banks. It aims to simplify personal remittances, strengthen digital financial connectivity, and enhance economic cooperation between the two countries.

questions.question: When is World Lung Cancer Day observed every year?
questions.explanation: World Lung Cancer Day is observed annually on August 01 to raise awareness about lung cancer, promote early diagnosis, encourage timely treatment, and support patients, survivors, and caregivers. The 2026 theme, "Together through Lung Cancer," emphasises community support, scientific progress, and equal access to healthcare. First observed in 2012 through the efforts of international respiratory and cancer organisations, the day also focuses on reducing stigma, advancing research, and educating people about risk factors, symptoms, prevention, and the importance of regular screening for improving survival rates.

questions.question: What was the year-on-year growth rate of India's gross GST collections in July 2026?
questions.explanation: India's gross GST collections recorded a 15.4% year-on-year growth in July 2026, reaching ₹2.11 lakh crore. The increase was driven by strong domestic tax revenues of ₹1.45 lakh crore and a significant 28.8% rise in GST collected from imports. Net GST collections after refunds stood at ₹1.81 lakh crore, reflecting continued economic resilience and improved tax compliance. The data also highlighted efficient refund processing, robust consumer demand, and healthy business activity, making July 2026 one of the strongest months for GST revenue collection in the financial year.

questions.question: Pithora painting, which recently received a Geographical Indication (GI) tag, is a traditional tribal art form primarily associated with which state?
questions.explanation: Pithora painting is a traditional ritual wall painting practised mainly by the Rathwa, Bhilala, and Nayak tribes of Gujarat and nearby regions. The recent Geographical Indication (GI) tag recognises the uniqueness and authenticity of this tribal art while protecting it from imitation. The recognition is expected to improve market access, increase the income of tribal artisans, and promote national and international recognition of their work. It also plays a vital role in preserving India's rich tribal cultural heritage by encouraging younger generations to continue practising this centuries-old artistic tradition.

questions.question: Which Bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2026 to strengthen measures against examination paper leaks and organised cheating in public examinations?
questions.explanation: The Anti-Paper Leak Amendment Bill was passed by Parliament in 2026 to strengthen the legal framework against examination paper leaks, organised cheating, and technological malpractice in public examinations. The legislation increases imprisonment to a minimum of five years and up to ten years, raises fines substantially, introduces Special Fast Track Courts, and mandates time-bound investigations and trials. It also empowers the Central Government to establish a Legal Council to coordinate investigations and combat examination-related crimes, ensuring greater transparency, fairness, and credibility in recruitment and entrance examinations across India.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian to win a gold medal in judo at the Commonwealth Games?
questions.explanation: Asmita Dey created history by becoming the first Indian judoka to win a gold medal at the Commonwealth Games. She achieved the milestone by defeating Canada's Heidi Quach in the women's 48 kg final at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games after a hard-fought Golden Score contest. Before this achievement, India had won only silver and bronze medals in Commonwealth Games judo, with no gold medal. Asmita's remarkable consistency, tactical discipline, and composure throughout the tournament marked a historic breakthrough for Indian judo and inspired a new generation of athletes in the sport.

questions.question: On which date is World Wide Web Day observed every year?
questions.explanation: World Wide Web Day is observed every year on August 01 to celebrate the invention of the World Wide Web by Sir Tim Berners-Lee in 1989. The day recognises the transformative impact of the web on communication, education, healthcare, business, governance, and entertainment. It also highlights the importance of technologies such as HTML, HTTP, and URL, which form the foundation of the web. The observance encourages awareness of how the World Wide Web has revolutionised access to information, connected people globally, and continues to drive innovation in the digital age.

questions.question: Who was appointed as India's next Ambassador to Mexico in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Ngulkham Jathom Gangte, a 1994-batch Indian Foreign Service (IFS) officer, was appointed as India's next Ambassador to Mexico on July 30, 2026. Before this appointment, he served as Special Secretary in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA). He previously served as India's Ambassador to Tunisia with concurrent accreditation to Libya and as the High Commissioner to Zambia from 2017 to 2021. A graduate of Hansraj College with a background in Chemistry, Gangte brings extensive diplomatic experience to strengthen India–Mexico bilateral relations.

questions.question: By which year does India aim to connect 100 crore people to 5G services?
questions.explanation: India has set a target of connecting 100 crore people to 5G services by 2030, as announced by Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia during the theme launch of India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026. The country has already connected 50 crore users within 2.5 years through nearly 5 lakh telecom towers, supported by an investment of around ₹4.5 lakh crore. India also launched its first Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) to strengthen domestic telecom production. With 1.33 billion mobile subscribers and affordable data prices of about ₹8 per GB, the initiative supports India's digital transformation and expansion of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI).

questions.question: How many heritage sites were declared as Protected Monuments by the Ladakh Administration?
questions.explanation: The Ladakh Administration declared 23 heritage sites as Protected Monuments to preserve the region's rich cultural and historical legacy. The notification was issued under the provisions of the J&K Ancient Monuments Preservation Act, Samvat 1977. The protected sites, located across Leh and Kargil, include ancient forts, caves, monasteries, and petroglyphs of archaeological significance. The initiative is intended to safeguard these monuments from encroachment, unauthorised alterations, and deterioration while encouraging sustainable cultural tourism and promoting awareness about Ladakh's unique heritage for future generations.

questions.question: What is the theme of the 10th India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026?
questions.explanation: "Scale without boundaries" is the official theme of the 10th India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026, unveiled by Union Minister Jyotiraditya M. Scindia on July 31, 2026. The event will be held from October 7 to 10, 2026, at Yashobhoomi in New Delhi and is organised by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) along with the Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI). The congress is built around four strategic pillars—Srishti, Suraksha, Sashakt, and Samvardhan—and will showcase advancements in 5G, 6G, Artificial Intelligence, Quantum technologies, satellite communications, and startup innovation through the ASPIRE initiative.

questions.question: In which city was the indigenous Diving Support Vessel Nipun built by Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL)?
questions.explanation: Nipun, the Indian Navy's second indigenous Diving Support Vessel, was built by Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL) in Visakhapatnam. Constructed with nearly 75% indigenous content, the vessel supports the Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative by promoting self-reliance in defence manufacturing. It serves as a mothership for Deep Submergence Rescue Vessels during underwater rescue missions and is equipped with advanced saturation diving systems and Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROVs) for deep-sea salvage and underwater operations. The induction of Nipun significantly strengthens the Indian Navy's underwater rescue and maritime support capabilities.

questions.question: Which state banned the sale, distribution, and advertisement of junk food within and around school premises in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra banned the sale, distribution, and advertisement of HFSS (High in Fat, Trans-fat, Sugar, and Salt) foods within school campuses and a 50-metre radius around them. The restriction covers government and private schools, benefiting nearly 2 crore students aged 22 months to 17 years. School canteens must obtain FDA food safety licenses and comply with the Food Safety and Standards Regulations, 2021. The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA), headquartered in Mumbai, will monitor compliance through inspections conducted at least twice a year under the legal framework of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

questions.question: Which state issued India's first exploration licence for a Rare Earth Elements (REE) block under the new critical minerals policy?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan became the first state in India to issue an exploration licence for a Rare Earth Elements (REE) block on July 30, 2026. The licence was awarded to the Central Mine Planning and Design Institute Ltd (CMPDI) for a 207.6 sq km area in the Nawatala-Devigarh region covering Balotra and Jodhpur districts. Geological surveys identified valuable rare earth elements such as lanthanum, cerium, praseodymium, and neodymium. These strategic minerals are crucial for electric vehicles, semiconductors, aerospace, and telecommunications, supporting India's goal of reducing dependence on imported critical minerals through domestic exploration.

questions.question: Which city will host the GI & Beyond 2.0 Summit on August 5, 2026?
questions.explanation: The GI & Beyond 2.0 Summit is scheduled to be held on August 5, 2026, at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre in New Delhi. Organised jointly by the Office of the Development Commissioner (Handlooms) and the Handloom Export Promotion Council (HEPC), the summit aims to promote India's GI-registered handloom and handicraft products. Key highlights include the launch of the Digital Handloom Atlas, unveiling of the HEPC Diamond Jubilee logo, participation of international buyers from around 10 countries, live weaving demonstrations, and an IIT Madras presentation on using Artificial Intelligence to strengthen the Geographical Indication ecosystem. Sessions will also focus on GI registration, intellectual property rights, and expanding domestic and global markets.

questions.question: Who assumed charge as the Controller General of Defence Accounts (CGDA) on August 1, 2026?
questions.explanation: Alka Nangia Arora, a 1991-batch officer of the Indian Defence Accounts Service (IDAS), assumed charge as the Controller General of Defence Accounts (CGDA) on August 1, 2026. As the head of the Defence Accounts Department under the Ministry of Defence, she brings over three decades of experience in public financial management. During her career, she has served as Additional Secretary and Financial Adviser in the Department of Agricultural Research and Education, Joint Secretary in the Ministry of MSME, Managing Director of the Central Cottage Industries Corporation of India Limited, and Additional Development Commissioner for Handicrafts under the Ministry of Textiles.

questions.question: Who has officially taken charge as the new CEO of IndiGo?
questions.explanation: Willie Walsh officially assumed charge as the new CEO of IndiGo on August 3, ushering in a new phase of leadership for India's largest airline. He succeeded Pieter Elbers and brings extensive experience from leading Aer Lingus, British Airways, International Airlines Group (IAG), and serving as Director General of the International Air Transport Association (IATA). Walsh is expected to guide IndiGo's international expansion, strengthen operational efficiency, and enhance customer service. His appointment reflects IndiGo's ambition to become a stronger global airline as India continues to emerge as one of the world's fastest-growing aviation markets.

questions.question: What was India's overall position in the medal tally at the Commonwealth Games 2026?
questions.explanation: India finished fourth in the overall medal tally at the Commonwealth Games 2026 held in Glasgow, Scotland. The country secured a total of 39 medals, comprising 13 gold, 17 silver, and 9 bronze medals. Although this was fewer than the 61 medals won at Birmingham 2022, the Glasgow Games featured fewer sports and medal events. India performed better in comparable sports, highlighting the country's growing competitiveness. Standout achievements included Gulveer Singh winning two medals, India's dominance in boxing with seven gold medals, and the nation's first-ever Commonwealth Games judo golds. The closing ceremony also marked the official handover of the Games to Ahmedabad for the 2030 edition.

questions.question: Who became the first woman Director General of the Geological Survey of India (GSI) in its 176-year history?
questions.explanation: Varsha Ashok Aglawe assumed charge as the 54th Director General of the Geological Survey of India (GSI) on July 31, 2026, becoming the first woman to lead the organisation in its 176-year history. A distinguished palaeontologist with more than 30 years of experience, she joined GSI in 1992 after serving at the Indian Bureau of Mines. Before her appointment, she was the Additional Director General and Head of the Eastern Region in Kolkata. She succeeded Asit Saha and is expected to strengthen GSI's role in geological mapping, mineral exploration, and geoscientific research under the Ministry of Mines.

questions.question: In which city was the Swami Vivekananda Cultural Youth Centre (Viveka Smaraka) inaugurated on August 1, 2026?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Swami Vivekananda Cultural Youth Centre, also known as Viveka Smaraka, at the Sri Ramakrishna Ashrama in Mysuru, Karnataka, on August 1, 2026. The centre commemorates the support extended by the then Maharaja of Mysuru to Swami Vivekananda about 130 years ago before his historic address at the 1893 Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago. The event also highlighted India's progress in education through the establishment of new universities, colleges, PM SHRI schools, and Atal Tinkering Labs. Additionally, the Kannada translation of the Valmiki Ramayana was released to promote regional literature and cultural heritage.

questions.question: Which state's Freedom of Religion Act, 2026 received President Droupadi Murmu's approval?
questions.explanation: President Droupadi Murmu approved the Maharashtra Freedom of Religion Act, 2026, completing the final constitutional requirement before the law can come into force. The Act will become effective only after the Maharashtra Government issues an official notification. It prohibits religious conversions carried out through coercion, fraud, misrepresentation, inducement, violence, or marriage for conversion purposes, while permitting voluntary conversions. The law also requires a 60-day advance notice to the district magistrate before conversion, allows close relatives to file complaints, shifts the burden of proving voluntary conversion to the person conducting it, and prescribes imprisonment of up to seven years for offences and up to ten years for repeat violations.

questions.question: Which country temporarily suspended the Schengen border-free travel arrangement with Spain following a significant migrant influx into Ceuta?
questions.explanation: Italy temporarily suspended the Schengen border-free travel arrangement with Spain for one month after a large number of migrants entered the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from Morocco. As part of the measure, Italy reintroduced passport and identity document checks for passengers arriving from Spain by air and sea, while targeted inspections were carried out on non-EU nationals. Italy also coordinated with France to strengthen security along the Franco-Italian land border. Under Schengen rules, member countries are permitted to restore internal border controls temporarily when there is a serious threat to public order or national security.

questions.question: Who assumed charge as the Deputy Chief of Naval Staff on August 1, 2026?
questions.explanation: Vice Admiral AN Pramod assumed charge as the Deputy Chief of Naval Staff on August 1, 2026, succeeding Vice Admiral Tarun Sobti, who retired after 38 years of distinguished service. Commissioned into the Indian Navy on July 1, 1990, he has played key operational roles in Operation Vijay, Operation Parakram, and Operation Snow Leopard following the Galwan incident. Before his appointment, he served as Director General Naval Operations and also held the post of Flag Officer Commanding Maharashtra Naval Area. His exemplary service has been recognised with the Ati Vishisht Seva Medal (AVSM) in 2024 and the Yudh Seva Medal (YSM) in 2025.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the next Director General Armed Forces Medical Services (DGAFMS), effective from August 31, 2026?
questions.explanation: Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja was appointed as the next Director General Armed Forces Medical Services (DGAFMS) by the Government of India on July 31, 2026, with effect from August 31, 2026. He will succeed Surgeon Vice Admiral Arti Sarin and is currently serving as the Director General Medical Services (Air). During his distinguished career, he played a key role in operationalising the BHISHM Cube for rapid humanitarian medical response and strengthening medical preparedness for the Gaganyaan Human Spaceflight Mission. A recipient of the Sena Medal and the Vishisht Seva Medal & Bar, he has also served as Commandant of AFMC Pune and held several important military medical appointments.

questions.question: Which city officially became the host of the 2030 Commonwealth Games after receiving the Games flag and ceremonial baton during the Glasgow 2026 closing ceremony?
questions.explanation: Ahmedabad officially became the host city of the 2030 Commonwealth Games after receiving the Commonwealth Games Flag and Host Baton during the closing ceremony of the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games. The handover marked the beginning of preparations for hosting the centenary edition of the Games in 2030. India will host the Commonwealth Games for the second time after previously organising them in New Delhi in 2010, becoming only the second country after Australia to host the event twice. The ceremony also featured a grand Indian cultural showcase highlighting the theme "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam," India's sporting achievements, musical collaborations, and performances by renowned artists, symbolising friendship, unity, and the transition of the Games to India.

questions.question: Which state recorded the highest number of deceased organ donors in India during 2025, according to the NOTTO Annual Report 2025–26?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu recorded the highest number of deceased organ donors in India during 2025, with 266 deceased donors, according to the NOTTO Annual Report 2025–26. The state also ranked second in total organ transplants, behind Delhi, and has the country's largest transplant infrastructure with 172 transplant centres. Tamil Nadu performed the highest number of transplants involving kidneys, livers, hearts, lungs, pancreases, and small bowels. The state's advanced healthcare system and well-established organ donation network have made it a national leader in promoting organ donation, improving transplant outcomes, and supporting patients in need of life-saving organ transplants.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian woman scientist to receive the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal in 2026?
questions.explanation: Annapurni Subramaniam received the prestigious COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal 2026, becoming the first Indian woman scientist and the fourth Indian overall to win the honour. The award was announced during the 46th COSPAR Scientific Assembly held in Florence, Italy. Jointly presented by the Committee on Space Research (COSPAR) and the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), the medal recognises outstanding contributions to space research by scientists from developing nations. Dr Subramaniam, Director of the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, is internationally known for her research on stellar populations, star clusters, and galaxy evolution, further strengthening India's global reputation in space science.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Executive Director of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) with effect from August 3, 2026?
questions.explanation: Monisha Chakraborty was appointed as the Executive Director of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) with effect from August 3, 2026. Before her promotion, she served as the Chief General Manager-in-Charge of the Department of Supervision and has over 30 years of experience in central banking. In her new role, she will oversee the Foreign Exchange Department and the Financial Markets Regulation Department. She holds a Bachelor's degree in Economics and a Master's degree in Business Economics from the University of Delhi, bringing extensive expertise in banking supervision, financial regulation, and foreign exchange management.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the next Ambassador of India to the Islamic Republic of Iran?
questions.explanation: Vishwesh Negi, a 2002-batch Indian Foreign Service (IFS) officer, was appointed as the next Ambassador of India to the Islamic Republic of Iran by the Ministry of External Affairs. Before this appointment, he served as Joint Secretary in the Ministry of External Affairs in New Delhi. He is expected to assume charge in Tehran and oversee India's diplomatic, strategic, and trade relations with Iran. His appointment is significant as Iran remains an important partner for India, particularly due to the strategic importance of Chabahar Port, which serves as India's gateway to Central Asia and beyond.

questions.question: On which date is International Clouded Leopard Day observed every year?
questions.explanation: International Clouded Leopard Day is observed annually on August 4 to raise awareness about the conservation of clouded leopards, one of Asia's rarest wild cats. The observance began in 2018 through the efforts of The Aspinall Foundation. In 2026, India marked the occasion by launching the Clouded Leopard Conservation Action Plan (CAP), aimed at protecting habitats, strengthening anti-poaching measures, promoting scientific monitoring, restoring forest corridors, and encouraging community participation. Clouded leopards are listed as Vulnerable by the IUCN due to habitat loss, illegal wildlife trade, deforestation, and increasing human-wildlife conflicts across their natural range.

questions.question: Which state released the first tranche of ₹160 crore as interim flood relief for families affected by the 2026 floods?
questions.explanation: Assam released the first tranche of ₹160 crore as interim flood relief on August 3, 2026, to support over 75,000 households severely affected by the 2026 floods. Each eligible family received ₹15,000 directly in their bank account to help with immediate recovery and rebuilding. The assistance primarily covered the districts of Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat, and Golaghat. The state also announced an additional ₹10,000 for severely affected families in selected districts and integrated subsidies under the Pradhan Mantri Surya Ghar Yojana. The floods affected around 1.36 lakh people, while the annual death toll reached 85.

questions.question: What is the new official name adopted by the Pacific island nation formerly known as Nauru?
questions.explanation: The Pacific island nation formerly known as Nauru has officially adopted the name Republic of Naoero to restore its traditional and indigenous identity. The change reflects the native Nauruan spelling and pronunciation and was approved by the country's parliament. Along with the new name, the nation introduced the country code NRO and changed the demonym of its citizens to dei-Naoero. The United Nations and several countries have already updated their official records. The renaming highlights the country's commitment to preserving its cultural heritage, language, and historical identity while strengthening national pride.

questions.question: In which state was the Bhogapuram Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi?
questions.explanation: Andhra Pradesh became home to the newly inaugurated Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram. Built under a Public-Private Partnership at a cost of over ₹5,640 crore, it is the state's first greenfield international airport since the 2014 bifurcation. The airport is designed to handle 6 million passengers annually in its first phase and features a 3,800-metre runway capable of accommodating wide-body aircraft. During the visit, development projects worth over ₹17,900 crore were launched, including South India's first assembly and test semiconductor facility approved under the India Semiconductor Mission, further boosting the state's infrastructure and industrial growth.

questions.question: Which state became home to its first Ramsar Site with the designation of Glaw Lake in August 2026?
questions.explanation: Arunachal Pradesh became the first state to have Glaw Lake recognised as its inaugural Ramsar Site, making it India's 101st Ramsar Site. Located within the Kamlang Tiger Reserve and Wildlife Sanctuary in the Eastern Himalayas, Glaw Lake is a natural freshwater wetland known for its exceptional ecological value. The area supports more than 150 tree species and 49 orchid species, along with diverse flora and fauna. Ramsar recognition highlights the importance of conserving wetlands for biodiversity, climate resilience, water security, scientific research, and sustainable livelihoods while strengthening India's commitment to protecting ecologically significant ecosystems.

questions.question: In which state did the Indian Air Force conclude the counter-drone exercise ROTOR CLAP III?
questions.explanation: The Indian Air Force concluded the week-long counter-drone exercise ROTOR CLAP III at the Pokhran Field Firing Range in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. Conducted with the theme "Counter-UAS" (Counter Unmanned Aerial Systems), the exercise focused on tackling emerging drone threats through realistic combat simulations. It validated mission planning, rapid response, and interoperability among various helicopter platforms operating in desert terrain. The exercise also included reconnaissance, troop insertion, casualty evacuation, and battlefield support missions. Pokhran, located in the Thar Desert, is also historically significant as the site of India's 1974 and 1998 nuclear tests.

questions.question: Which Indian state signed four Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with Australia to promote clean energy, advanced manufacturing, and inclusive education?
questions.explanation: Andhra Pradesh signed four Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with Australia to strengthen cooperation in clean energy, advanced manufacturing, workforce mobility, and inclusive education. One of the key agreements establishes a Centre of Excellence for Solar Manufacturing at IIT Tirupati in collaboration with the University of New South Wales (UNSW) and the Centre of Excellence for Energy Transition. The partnerships also focus on solar panel recycling, circular economy practices, teacher training, student mental health, and industrial research, supporting the state's economic reconstruction strategy and efforts to attract global investments through international collaboration.

questions.question: When was World Breastfeeding Week 2026 observed globally?
questions.explanation: World Breastfeeding Week 2026 was observed globally from August 1 to 7 to promote awareness about breastfeeding, child health, nutrition, and poverty reduction. The global theme for 2026 was “Breastfeeding for a Sustainable Start in Life: Strengthen What Works”. The observance was coordinated by the World Alliance for Breastfeeding Action (WABA), World Health Organisation (WHO), and UNICEF. Key recommendations include initiating breastfeeding within the first hour after birth, exclusively breastfeeding infants for the first six months, and continuing breastfeeding for two years or beyond alongside appropriate complementary foods.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the next Ambassador of India to Iran?
questions.explanation: Vishwesh Negi was appointed as the next Ambassador of India to the Islamic Republic of Iran by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on August 3, 2026. He is a 2002-batch Indian Foreign Service (IFS) officer and is currently serving as Joint Secretary in the Ministry of External Affairs in New Delhi. He is expected to assume charge in Tehran and oversee India-Iran strategic and trade relations. Iran’s capital is Tehran, and Chabahar Port is an important strategic asset for India, providing a maritime gateway to Central Asia.

questions.question: Which state government mandated five major administrative reforms under the “Zero Bureaucracy” model to streamline public service delivery?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra government mandated five major administrative reforms on August 4, 2026, through a Government Resolution to improve public service delivery under the “Zero Bureaucracy” model. The reforms include increasing administrative departments from 33 to 45, limiting decision-making to three administrative tiers, and introducing Government Process Re-engineering (GPR). The state will also use Aadhaar, Maha Samanvay, DigiLocker, and API-based systems to reduce physical documentation. A state-level GPR Approval Committee chaired by the Chief Secretary will supervise implementation. Maharashtra’s Right to Public Services Act, enacted in 2015, aims to ensure transparent and time-bound delivery of notified public services.

questions.question: Where was the Second BRICS Anti-Corruption Working Group Meeting held in August 2026?
questions.explanation: Hyderabad, Telangana, hosted the Second BRICS Anti-Corruption Working Group (ACWG) meeting on August 4–5, 2026. The meeting was organised by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) under India’s BRICS Presidency 2026. It focused on strengthening transparency, accountability, international cooperation, asset recovery, and measures to combat cross-border corruption. The event also addressed emerging corruption risks associated with FinTech and digital assets. Alongside the ACWG meeting, the Second BRICS Expert Network on Asset Recovery meeting was conducted. A special side event on ethical governance through technology was also scheduled during the gathering.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Executive Director of the Reserve Bank of India effective August 3, 2026?
questions.explanation: Monisha Chakraborty was appointed as the Executive Director (ED) of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), effective August 3, 2026. Before her promotion, she served as Chief General Manager-in-charge in the Department of Supervision. In her new role, she will oversee the Foreign Exchange Department and the Financial Markets Regulation Department, two important areas of the central bank’s operations. Chakraborty has more than three decades of experience at the RBI, with professional expertise in supervision, foreign exchange, and government and bank accounts. The RBI was established on April 1, 1935, and was nationalised on January 1, 1949.

questions.question: Which organisation developed India’s first indigenous African Swine Fever vaccine for pigs?
questions.explanation: ICAR (Indian Council of Agricultural Research) developed India’s first indigenous African Swine Fever (ASF) vaccine. The live attenuated vaccine was developed using the MA-104 cell line at ICAR–National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD), Bhopal. It was officially launched by Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan on ICAR Foundation Day 2026. The vaccine is expected to strengthen livestock biosecurity, reduce pig mortality and support pig farmers, particularly in the North-Eastern states that have faced severe ASF outbreaks since 2020.

questions.question: Which institution developed a hybrid magneto-rheometer for advancing Magnetorheological (MR) fluid technology?
questions.explanation: IIT Patna developed an innovative hybrid magneto-rheometer to advance the testing and application of Magnetorheological (MR) fluids. The research team, led by Prof. Chiranjit Sarkar, developed a custom-built instrument along with nano iron powder-based MR fluids. Supported by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), the instrument can measure both rheological properties, such as flow and deformation, and tribological properties, including friction and wear. It can also evaluate performance under simultaneous compression and shear forces. The technology has potential applications in aerospace, defence, healthcare, industrial automation, shock absorbers, vibration control systems, dampers, and actuators.

questions.question: Which country’s Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov visited New Delhi to strengthen strategic cooperation with India in mining and trade?
questions.explanation: Uzbekistan’s Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov visited New Delhi on August 5, 2026, to deepen the strategic partnership between India and Uzbekistan in critical minerals, mining, trade, and defence. Bilateral trade between the two countries has reached nearly $1 billion, with both sides aiming for further expansion. Cooperation is also being strengthened in infrastructure, energy, defence, and digital technology. Uzbekistan supported India’s BRICS Presidency in 2026, while India backed Uzbekistan’s candidacy to chair the Non-Aligned Movement for 2027–2029. Uzbekistan’s capital is Tashkent, and its currency is the Uzbekistani Soʻm.

questions.question: Where was the Ministry of Textiles Handloom Hackathon 2.0 successfully concluded?
questions.explanation: IIT Delhi hosted the successful conclusion of the Ministry of Textiles Handloom Hackathon 2.0, themed “Weaving Innovations,” on August 2, 2026. The event was held at the Foundation for Innovation and Technology Transfer (FITT) and witnessed participation from more than 2,500 participants and 100 shortlisted teams. Innovations were recognised across four categories, including weaver livelihoods, digital market access, sustainability, and design and operations. The hackathon aimed to combine India’s traditional handloom heritage with modern technology to improve the livelihoods of weavers and artisans. IIT Delhi, established in 1961, is located in Hauz Khas, New Delhi.

questions.question: Which company was designated as the lead financer for the ₹26,850 crore loan facility for the Meja Thermal Power Project expansion?

The loan agreement was signed by REC Limited and Power Finance Corporation (PFC) with Meja Urja Nigam Private Limited (MUNPL) on July 31, 2026. The debt facility is funded equally by REC and PFC. The project involves constructing three ultra-supercritical units of 800 MW each, adding a total of 2,400 MW to the state grid. REC Limited is a Maharatna Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Power, established in 1969.

questions.question: Who was re-appointed as the Chairperson of the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) for 27 months?
questions.explanation: K Rajaraman was re-appointed as the Chairperson of the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) for a further period of 27 months. The Central Government extended his tenure beyond July 31, 2026, until he reaches the age of 65 years. His extended term will conclude on October 24, 2028, or until further orders, whichever is earlier. Rajaraman was initially appointed as IFSCA Chairperson in 2023 for a three-year term. IFSCA was established in April 2020 under the International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019, and is headquartered at GIFT City, Gandhinagar, Gujarat.

questions.question: Who assumed charge as the acting Central Vigilance Commissioner (CVC) on August 3, 2026?
questions.explanation: AS Rajeev assumed charge as the acting Central Vigilance Commissioner (CVC) on August 3, 2026, following the completion of the tenure of Praveen Kumar Srivastava. His appointment was authorised by the President of India under Section 10(1) of the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003. Rajeev has more than 38 years of banking experience and has worked with Syndicate Bank, Vijaya Bank, Indian Bank, and Bank of Maharashtra, where he served as Managing Director and CEO. He was originally appointed as a Vigilance Commissioner on February 9, 2024. The CVC was established in 1964 based on the Santhanam Committee’s recommendations.

questions.question: When is Hiroshima Day observed every year to commemorate the atomic bombing of Hiroshima?
questions.explanation: Hiroshima Day is observed every year on August 6 to commemorate the atomic bombing of Hiroshima, Japan, by the United States in 1945 during the Second World War. Hiroshima Day 2026 marks the 81st anniversary of the tragedy. The day honours those who lost their lives, remembers the survivors known as Hibakusha, and promotes global peace, nuclear disarmament, and non-proliferation. On August 6, 1945, the uranium-based atomic bomb “Little Boy” was dropped on Hiroshima from the B-29 bomber Enola Gay. The bombing caused massive destruction and long-term health, psychological, and social consequences for survivors.

questions.question: Which company signed an MoU with Esri India to develop advanced GIS, Location Intelligence, and GeoAI solutions for the Indian defence sector?
questions.explanation: Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Esri India on August 3, 2026, to collaborate on advanced Geographic Information System (GIS), Location Intelligence, and GeoAI solutions for India’s defence sector. The partnership aims to modernise defence infrastructure and strengthen situational awareness and operational coordination. Esri India will provide specialised training to BEL personnel and support the development of in-house geospatial capabilities using the Indo ArcGIS platform. The collaboration will also explore emerging technologies such as Quantum Technologies, unmanned systems, and Big Data Analytics. BEL, established in 1954, is a Navratna CPSE under the Ministry of Defence and is headquartered in Bengaluru.

questions.question: Which state is hosting the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Meeting in Bhubaneswar from August 5 to 7, 2026?
questions.explanation: Odisha is hosting the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Meeting and the 3rd BRICS Senior Officials’ Meeting in Bhubaneswar from August 5 to 7, 2026. The meetings are being conducted under India’s BRICS Chairship 2026 and are led by the Ministry of Education. The agenda includes strengthening Early Childhood Care and Education, expanding vocational training through the BRICS TVET Cooperation Alliance, advancing the Mutual Recognition of Qualifications framework, and promoting research, innovation, and start-ups. A new Model BRICS Initiative has also been launched to familiarise students with multilateral diplomacy. Bhubaneswar, the capital of Odisha, is known as the ‘Temple City of India’.

questions.question: What GDP growth rate did SBI Research project for India in Q1 FY27?
questions.explanation: SBI Research projected India’s GDP growth at approximately 7% for Q1 FY27 in its Pre-Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) report released on August 1, 2026. This estimate is higher than the RBI’s earlier downgraded projection of 6.6%. Several economic indicators supported the optimistic outlook, including 7.3% growth in the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), 19.2% expansion in industrial activity and credit, and a 24.1% year-on-year increase in domestic passenger vehicle sales in June. Electricity demand and exports also recorded strong growth. SBI Research expects the economy to maintain momentum despite global uncertainties and geopolitical challenges.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian woman to feature in the Tour de France Femmes in 2026?
questions.explanation: Harshita Jakhar became the first Indian woman to feature in the Tour de France Femmes in 2026. The 19-year-old cyclist participated in the event in Switzerland and led the ceremonial start of Stage Two in Aigle, completing a 4.5 km ride ahead of the professional peloton. She was also selected for the UCI World Cycling Talent Programme, which provides elite international exposure to cyclists from developing nations. Jakhar won three gold medals at the 2025 Khelo India Youth Games and earned a silver and two bronze medals at the 2024 Asian Junior Cycling Championships. She trains at the SAI National Centre of Excellence in Patiala.

The project has a total investment of $6.2 billion and involves Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Installation, and Commissioning (EPCIC) of offshore facilities, along with upgrades to existing infrastructure. LTEH Offshore will act as the lead partner, working with international companies including TotalEnergies, Eni, and China National Petroleum Corp. L&T is a major Indian multinational conglomerate involved in EPC projects and high-tech manufacturing. It is headquartered in Mumbai and was founded in 1938 by two Danish engineers.

questions.question: When did SEBI extend the deadline for regulated entities to complete digital accessibility audits and resolve platform issues?

The extension provides additional time to comply with the requirements of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. The original deadline for completing digital platform accessibility audits was April 30, while the timeline for full compliance and remediation was July 31. The mandate applies to all SEBI-regulated entities and aims to ensure that digital platforms are accessible to persons with disabilities, promoting inclusivity and equal access to financial markets. SEBI regulates India’s securities market and protects investor interests.

questions.question: Which state officially operationalised the Dial 112 emergency response system, replacing the legacy Dial 100 system?
questions.explanation: Telangana officially operationalised Dial 112 as a unified emergency helpline on August 5, 2026, replacing the legacy Dial 100 police helpline. The system integrates police, fire, ambulance, disaster response, and women and child safety services under a single emergency number. It is operated from the Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC) in Hyderabad. The system reduces emergency call processing time by 30%, from 190 seconds to 133 seconds, and provides location-based tracking with 95% accuracy. Dial 112 is part of India’s Emergency Response Support System (ERSS), designed to provide a single emergency number across all States and Union Territories.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the new CEO of Air India in 2026?
questions.explanation: Tewolde Gebremariam, the former Chief Executive Officer of Ethiopian Airlines, was appointed as the new CEO of Air India in 2026. He succeeds Campbell Wilson, who led the airline during its initial stabilisation and integration phase after the Tata Group regained ownership in 2022. Gebremariam is known for transforming Ethiopian Airlines into a globally successful and profitable airline group by expanding international routes, modernising its fleet, strengthening cargo operations, and developing aviation training and maintenance facilities. At Air India, he is expected to focus on operational excellence, international connectivity, customer experience, safety, and the development of world-class aviation infrastructure.

questions.question: Which state government launched applications for the Nijut Moina and Nijut Babu schemes in August 2026?
questions.explanation: Assam launched applications for the Nijut Moina and Nijut Babu student welfare schemes on August 6, 2026, with Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma formally initiating the application process in Guwahati. Nijut Moina primarily provides financial assistance to girl students to encourage higher education and help prevent child marriage. Its eligibility was expanded in 2026 to include students pursuing polytechnic courses and seventh-semester integrated postgraduate programmes. Nijut Babu provides financial assistance to boys pursuing higher secondary, undergraduate, and postgraduate studies. The schemes aim to reduce the financial burden on families and encourage students to continue their education while maintaining regularity, discipline, and commitment to their studies.

questions.question: Which institution launched India’s first industry-academia orientation programme dedicated to the civil nuclear energy sector?
questions.explanation: IIT Hyderabad launched ANUGYAN, India’s first industry-academia orientation programme focused on the civil nuclear energy sector, on August 3, 2026. The programme, known as the Nuclear Technology Orientation Programme (NTOP), was developed in collaboration with Crimson Energy Experts Private Limited. It is a three-month fully residential course combining academic learning with industrial exposure. The curriculum covers reactor physics, thermal hydraulics, Small Modular Reactors, radiation safety, AERB regulatory compliance, quality assurance, simulator-based training, and engineering design. The initiative supports India’s long-term objective of increasing nuclear power capacity from 8.8 GWe to 100 GWe by 2047.

questions.question: When is National Handloom Day observed annually in India?
questions.explanation: National Handloom Day is observed annually on August 7 in India to honour the country’s rich handloom heritage and recognise the contribution of weavers and artisans. The day commemorates the Swadeshi Movement, which began on August 7, 1905, at Calcutta Town Hall and encouraged Indians to use indigenous products instead of foreign goods. The Government of India designated August 7 as National Handloom Day, with the first observance held in 2015. The occasion promotes traditional weaving skills, sustainable textiles, artisan empowerment, and the “Vocal for Local” campaign. Famous Indian handlooms include Banarasi Silk, Kanchipuram Silk, Sambalpuri Ikat, Pochampally Ikat, and Muga Silk.

questions.question: Which operation was launched by India to track and bring back fugitives hiding abroad using advanced technology and international law enforcement cooperation?
questions.explanation: Operation Trishul was launched by India to track and bring back fugitives hiding abroad through advanced technology and international law enforcement cooperation. Between 2019 and August 5, 2026, India successfully returned 274 fugitives from 36 countries under this effort. The operation uses satellite imagery, surveillance, and digital footprint analysis to identify the geo-location of fugitives. Its implementation involves major agencies including the Intelligence Bureau (IB), Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), Research and Analysis Wing (R&AW), and INTERPOL. A three-year roadmap has also been established to bring back identified narco-terrorist fugitives by 2029.

questions.question: Which company entered into a strategic partnership with Italy’s Lucchini RS Holding to develop an integrated railwheel manufacturing platform in India?
questions.explanation: Jupiter Wagons Ltd entered into a strategic partnership with Italy’s Lucchini RS Holding on August 4, 2026, to develop an integrated railwheel manufacturing platform in India. Under the agreement, Lucchini RS will acquire a 15% stake in Jupiter Tatravagonka Railwheel Factory (JTRWF), while SIMEST SpA will acquire a 10% stake. The combined 25% stake is valued at €28 million, approximately ₹307 crore. The partnership covers the production of railway wheels, axles, and wheelsets across the complete value chain. It also includes integrating the existing facility at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and developing a new greenfield manufacturing complex in Odisha.

questions.question: Which country is home to Noemi Aerospace (Elfly AS), Pawan Hans Limited’s partner for electric seaplane technology?
questions.explanation: Norway is the home country of Noemi Aerospace (Elfly AS), which signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Pawan Hans Limited on August 7, 2026, to collaborate on electric seaplane technology and sustainable aviation. The partnership focuses on technical knowledge sharing, workshops, feasibility studies, skill development, and capacity building for the electric aviation sector. Noemi Aerospace is headquartered in Bergen, Norway, and develops next-generation electric seaplanes. The collaboration aligns with India’s efforts to improve regional and island connectivity under the Make in India initiative. India’s Union Budget 2026 also introduced a Viability Gap Funding scheme to support seaplane operations.

questions.question: Which state imposed a blanket ban on unauthorised analogue dairy products such as paneer, cheese, and butter?
questions.explanation: Gujarat imposed a statewide ban on the manufacture, storage, transportation, and sale of unauthorised analogue dairy products such as paneer, cheese, and butter on August 7, 2026. The decision was taken due to public health concerns after laboratory tests by the state’s Food and Drug Regulatory Authority identified substitutes made using vegetable oils instead of milk. Such products can mislead consumers and affect genuine dairy producers. The ban applies to food business operators, including hotels, restaurants, and caterers. Violations will be prosecuted under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, which provides the legal framework for food safety regulation and established the FSSAI.

questions.question: Which state Cabinet approved the operation of 16 medical and dental colleges under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) mode?
questions.explanation: Bihar Cabinet approved a proposal on August 5, 2026, to operate 16 medical and dental colleges under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) mode. The decision was chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and aims to strengthen the state’s medical education and healthcare infrastructure. PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) was approved as the transaction adviser for the institutions with a sanction of ₹8.27 crore. The colleges include functional institutions at Pawapuri, Madhepura, Purnia, and Rahui, while several others are under construction. The Cabinet also approved funds for a Sports Science Centre, tourism initiatives, water-supply infrastructure, manuscript digitisation, and additional administrative posts across the state.

questions.question: On which date is Quit India Movement Day observed in 2026?
questions.explanation: August 8 is observed as Quit India Movement Day, commemorating the launch of the historic Quit India Movement in 1942. The movement began at the Bombay session of the All India Congress Committee (AICC) on August 8, 1942, where the Quit India Resolution was passed. Mahatma Gandhi gave the famous “Do or Die” call during the movement. The historic session was held at Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay, now known as August Kranti Maidan in Mumbai. The day commemorates the sacrifices of freedom fighters and the widespread participation of Indians in the struggle against British colonial rule.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Executive Director of SEBI on August 6, 2026?
questions.explanation: Prasanta Mahapatra was appointed as the Executive Director (ED) of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on August 6, 2026. In his new role, he will lead the Corporation Finance Investigation Department and handle the Recovery and Refund Department of the market regulator. Mahapatra joined SEBI in April 1999 and previously served as its Chief General Manager. He also worked at SEBI’s Eastern Regional Office in Kolkata. SEBI is the principal regulator of India’s securities market and received statutory powers under the SEBI Act, 1992.

questions.question: Which war witnessed Operation Safed Sagar conducted by the Indian Air Force?
questions.explanation: Operation Safed Sagar was an air operation conducted by the Indian Air Force during the Kargil War in 1999. It began in May 1999 to provide crucial air support to Indian ground forces fighting to reclaim strategic mountain positions occupied by Pakistani troops. The operation involved aerial reconnaissance, precision strikes, air defence, helicopter support and disruption of enemy logistics. Mirage-2000 aircraft played a particularly important role by using laser-guided bombs and precision weaponry against high-altitude targets. The operation was conducted under the major limitation that Indian aircraft were not permitted to cross the Line of Control.

questions.question: Where was BIOFACH INDIA 2026 organised by APEDA from August 6–8, 2026?
questions.explanation: Greater Noida hosted BIOFACH INDIA 2026 from August 6 to 8, 2026, at the India Expo Centre & Mart (IEML). The event was organised by the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), in collaboration with Nuernberg Messe India and IFOAM – Organics International. It focused on promoting India’s certified organic products and featured more than 200 exhibiting companies, including Farmer Producer Organisations, startups and women entrepreneurs. More than 35 international buyers from 13 overseas markets participated. Organic products such as cereals, pulses, millets, spices and medicinal plants were showcased at the event.

questions.question: Which state launched the AI-powered Composite Digital Crop Survey in Bengaluru?
questions.explanation: Karnataka launched the Composite Digital Crop Survey in Bengaluru on August 6, 2026, to integrate Artificial Intelligence and satellite technology into agricultural data collection. The initiative uses Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), high-resolution satellite imagery, drones, GIS data and Machine Learning algorithms to improve the accuracy and reliability of crop information. It will initially be implemented on a pilot basis in five selected hoblis representing different geographical divisions of the state. The survey aims to provide authenticated, plot-level crop data, supporting evidence-based policymaking, effective governance and better allocation of agricultural resources.

questions.question: Which airline entered into a codeshare partnership with Azerbaijan Airlines to enhance connectivity between India and Azerbaijan?
questions.explanation: Air India entered into a codeshare partnership with Azerbaijan Airlines on August 6, 2026, to improve connectivity and promote tourism between India and Azerbaijan. Under the agreement, Air India can place its ‘AI’ designator code on flights operated by Azerbaijan Airlines. The partnership includes daily flights between Delhi and Baku and between Mumbai and Baku. It allows Air India customers to travel to Baku on a single ticket and itinerary, including destinations not directly served by Air India. Air India was founded in 1932 as Tata Airlines and is headquartered in New Delhi.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian to win the gold medal in the men’s individual category at the FISU World University Squash Championship?
questions.explanation: Suraj Kumar Chand became the first Indian to win the gold medal in the men’s individual category at the FISU World University Squash Championship. He achieved this historic feat on August 6, 2026, in Mumbai by defeating Hungary’s Benedek Takacs in a thrilling five-game final. Suraj, a student of Somaiya Vidyavihar University, Mumbai, showcased remarkable composure and resilience throughout the tournament. His victory was especially significant as the championship was held at his home institution. Earlier, he had won bronze medals at the 2024 World University Championships and the HCL PSA Indian Tour event in Chennai in 2026.

questions.question: Which institute developed the E-Eye portable device for detecting toxic metals and bacteria in water?
questions.explanation: IIT Guwahati researchers developed E-Eye, a low-cost and portable optical sensing device for rapid on-site detection of water contamination. The device can detect heavy metals such as arsenic, lead, iron and chromium, along with fluoride and E. coli bacteria. It operates using the Beer-Lambert law and measures colour changes in chemical reactions to estimate contaminant concentrations. The device costs around ₹3,500, with an operational cost of about ₹2 per sample. Its performance is comparable to standard laboratory instruments, making it particularly useful for water-quality monitoring in rural areas.

questions.question: Who became the first woman pilot to qualify as a Fighter Combat Leader at TACDE?
questions.explanation: Bhawana Kanth became the first woman pilot to qualify as a Fighter Combat Leader (FCL) after successfully completing the prestigious FCL course at the Tactics and Air Combat Development Establishment (TACDE) in Gwalior on August 6, 2026. The rigorous 20-week programme focuses on advanced combat tactics and trains officers to lead complex air-to-air and air-to-ground operations. Bhawana Kanth was commissioned into the Indian Air Force in June 2016 as one of India’s first three women fighter pilots, alongside Avani Chaturvedi and Mohana Singh. Her achievement marks a significant milestone for women in India’s military aviation.

The proclamation also highlighted the establishment of a new Indian Consulate in Boston to support visa services, trade, and tourism. The occasion was further marked by the participation of the Indian Navy’s sail training vessel INS Sudarshini in the SAILBOSTON-250 maritime festival, showcasing India’s maritime heritage and strengthening India-US cultural ties.
